1. His journey & stats

This chapter records who Natural Hypertrophy is as a lifter: where he started, how his bodyweight, physique, programming and mindset changed over ~15 years, and the stats he has given for himself. The facts describe his own history, not advice; he repeatedly calls himself a "special case" whose volume most people do not need. His overall story is a weak, bullied teen who built a 6 ft, ~220 lb natural physique slowly, lost years to strength chasing, dirty bulking and injuries, and moved to self-written, hypertrophy-only training with more balance in life.

Starting point and early years

He started from very low and spent years at home with almost no equipment before ever entering a gym.

JRN-01 · Started small, weak and untrained at 14-15

  • Statement: He began training at 14-15 as the smallest kid in his class after losing arm wrestling to a girl; he could not do a single push-up and could only train about 10 minutes (knee push-ups, sit-ups, light curls).
  • Numbers: start age 14 or 15; 100, 110 or 120 lb; under 5 ft / 5'5" / ~5'2" at 14-15; 0 push-ups; ~10 min sessions
  • Scope: his own starting point
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — start age (14 vs 15), weight (100 vs 110 vs 120 lb) and teen height vary between videos
  • Sources: (STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08; 10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04; Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01; You weren't chosen by God. Now what?, 2024-06)

JRN-02 · Built training tolerance gradually

  • Statement: His first sessions were about 20 minutes of push-ups, sit-ups and air squats, and he extended them step by step; doing more at the start would have burnt him out.
  • Numbers: 10 min → 20 → 40 min → 1 h → 2 h
  • Scope: his own start as a complete beginner
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does a complete beginner start with short sessions (10-20 min) and build duration up gradually?
  • Sources: (How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03; Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01)

Bodyweight history and bulking lessons

His weight story runs from slow teenage gains, through a dirty bulk to 240 lb and a crash cut, to a long recomp and a slow bulk to 220 lb. See the stats timeline at the end of the chapter.

JRN-11 · Bodyweight path from 110 to 220 lb

  • Statement: He went from about 110 lb at 15 to a fat peak of 235-240 lb around age 23, crash-cut to ~205-210, recomped at 210 for about three years, then slowly bulked to 220 lb, which he now maintains.
  • Numbers: 110 (15) → 140 (17-18) → 150-160 (19) → 170 (20) → 185-190 (21) → 200-205 (22) → 235-240 peak (~23, 21-22% BF) → ~205-210 → mini-bulk 225 → ~215 → 210 recomp (2019-2022) → 215 (2023) → 220 (2024)
  • Scope: his own bodyweight
  • Confidence: high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — weight at 22 given as 200-205 or 220 lb; the 240-lb peak dated ~2017 in one video and 2018-2019 in others; in 2025 he recalled 110 kg in Dec 2019
  • Sources: (10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04; Recomp guide (part. 2)： Who can do it & diet manipulation, 2020-05; Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10; 20 inch arms CMON (Hypertrophy Log #9), 2024-12)

JRN-12 · His gains rate halved about every five years

  • Statement: Each five-year block brought roughly half the bodyweight gain of the one before.
  • Numbers: +60 lb (ages 15-20), +30 lb (20-25), +15 lb in 3 years (25-28)
  • Scope: his own natural progress
  • Confidence: medium — 1 video, 2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10)

JRN-13 · Best gains came from a tiny surplus held for years

  • Statement: As a skinny teen eating what his parents served, plus a little extra each day, he gained steadily for years without tracking, supplements or ever getting chubby; he calls the clean bulk that poverty forced on him "a blessing".
  • Numbers: +1 bowl of rice or some roast beef/day; ~10-15 lb quality mass/year; 110 → 170 lb in 5 years
  • Scope: his teen years, beginner
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current

Training phases and programming lessons

His programming went from no plan, through a productive simple plan, to a strength-focused era that stalled him, and finally to self-written hypertrophy programs.

JRN-21 · No program at first meant stalling

  • Statement: For his first one to two years he trained randomly (machines, bench) with no program; he still gained but never adapted neurologically and stalled, and a plan would have been far more productive.
  • Numbers: ~1-2 years without a program
  • Scope: his early training
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the lifter follow a written plan rather than picking exercises at random?
  • Sources: (Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03; 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐈𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐖𝐞 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭, 2022-10; 5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09)

JRN-22 · A simple linear dumbbell plan gave his best gains

  • Scope: his beginner years

  • Sources: (5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09; Fullbody template review, 2021-01; Hypertrophy Q&A #5, 2021-01)

2. Mindset, natural vs enhanced & genetics

This chapter covers the mental side of training (discipline, adherence, goals, comparison, ego, dysmorphia), his position on performance-enhancing drugs (PEDs) and testosterone replacement (TRT), and what he thinks genetics do and don't decide. His overall stance: discipline and years of consistency, not motivation or talent, carry a natural lifter. Never take PEDs, because the gains leave with the drug and enhanced advice doesn't transfer to naturals. Genetics are real but mostly set speed and shape, not whether you can get big, so "bad genetics" and "the natural limit" are usually excuses. General life philosophy (stoicism, media habits, social life) is in ch. 14.

Discipline and habits

He ranks discipline above motivation and treats it as a learned, daily habit. In 2024 he softens the rigidity but keeps the core.

MND-01 · Discipline over motivation

  • Statement: Motivation spikes and fades; discipline gets you to the gym. The top level is training without deliberation because it's simply on the schedule and you love it.
  • Numbers: three levels: motivation → discipline → "just doing it"; after 10-15 years he is rarely motivated
  • Scope: all lifters
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — he also once called motivation "the most important half" alongside method, against his usual view that it is too unreliable to carry you
  • Check: Is training run as a fixed habit rather than left to how motivated the lifter feels?
  • Sources: (The Educated Barbarian： Hagakure analysis (part. 3), 2020-07; Natural Q&A #6, 2021-03; Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (ⅠⅠ： Jeff Nippard, Eric Bugenhagen, 2022-04; Winter Arc 2025 is CANCELLED, 2024-11)

MND-02 · Motivational content replaces action

  • Statement: Hype and motivational videos are a dopamine spike that substitutes for training and makes you passive (the "David Goggins effect"); a video should be the spark that sends you to train, not a replacement.
  • Numbers: he'd rather you train 5 min than watch his 5-min video
  • Scope: all lifters
  • Confidence: high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Seven Deadly Fitness Sins： Envy, 2020-07; Alpha Male Routines are making me 𝐒𝐈𝐂𝐊, 2022-12; Winter Arc 2025 is CANCELLED, 2024-11; POV： Your therapist is a bodybuilder (Jung, ＂Modern Man in Search of a Soul＂), 2024-10)

Why stay natural: gains, health, lifespan

His core message is "never take PEDs": not one cycle, not a low dose, not TRT. The NAT principles below give his reasons and what follows for training.

NAT-01 · PED gains don't stay

  • Statement: Stop the drugs and most of the muscle goes, because the hormonal environment it grew in is gone, even with PCT and hard training; remove the drug and the physique collapses, remove the training and it largely stays.
  • Numbers: users shrink to normal or mediocre within ~3-4 months off
  • Scope: anyone considering PEDs
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: contradicted — he has also said PEDs "have been shown to increase myonuclei" and regaining is slightly easier after use, while later rejecting lasting myonuclei gains "in practice"
  • Sources: (How to spot a fake natty： rollercoaster progress, 2020-01; Reasons you should stay natural： you will become physically dependent on PEDs, 2020-03; Nucleus overload guide (part. 1)： What it is & how to implement it, 2020-05; 💉 Taking steroids is cheating ｜ Natural Bodybuilder Reacts 💪, 2025-01)

NAT-02 · Natural muscle is kept for life

  • Statement: Naturals lose muscle slowly and regain it quickly; keeping it only takes eating what you need and training, with no substance dependency. He calls this "the number one reason" to stay natural.
  • Numbers: legs built to 25 in shrink in a layoff but don't drop back to 20 in; some muscle remains into your 80s
  • Scope: naturals
  • Confidence: high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — in 2020 he said both that lost size "comes back very fast" and that after 10 years and a full detrain it takes much longer than a year; 2024: naturals "regain it quickly"
  • Sources: (How to spot a fake natty： rollercoaster progress, 2020-01; Why you should stay natural： permanent gains, 2020-02; Nether Beast Character Study： Staying on The Mark (13_22), 2020-10; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

3. Volume, intensity, frequency & rest

This chapter covers the four dials of a training program: how hard each set is (intensity, failure, reps in reserve), how many hard sets you do (volume), how you spread them over the week (frequency and splits), and how long you rest between sets. His later stance is that hard sets close to failure are what make naturals grow. He wants the least volume that keeps you progressing, spread over 2-3 sessions per muscle, with heavy work rested fully and everything else supersetted. He started (2020) as a high-volume maximalist and moved toward intensity and minimal-effective volume by 2024.

The frame: tonnage and the trinity

He reasons about training through tonnage (reps x weight) from hard sets, produced by three linked variables.

VOL-01 · Volume, intensity and frequency form one system

  • Statement: Volume, intensity and frequency are one trinity; none works alone, and pushing one while ignoring the others breaks the system.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees; the basis for every programming decision in this chapter.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： the primordial metric for muscle growth, 2021-01; Mike Mentzer： Mustachioed fraud or Bodybuilding genius? (🆃🅷🅴 🅷🅸, 2022-08; What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03)

VOL-02 · Growth comes from tonnage in a relevant window

  • Statement: Hypertrophy is driven by tonnage (reps x weight) accumulated over time, but volume counts only when the load sits in a relevant intensity window.
  • Numbers: 10 reps at 315 lb beats 2 at 350; 300x5 beats 350x1; 135 lb bench for 1000 reps won't make you big.
  • Scope: All trainees; tonnage means hard-set tonnage, never raw reps.
  • Confidence: high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02; The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04; No one understands training intensity, 2021-11; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09)

VOL-03 · Count working sets only

  • Statement: Only relevant tonnage from hard sets counts; warm-ups and very light work add tonnage but of low quality.
  • Numbers: 4000 lb of nucleus-overload work is worth about 400 lb of quality work.
  • Scope: All trainees; he still sees warm-ups as mildly useful.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： volume vs tonnage, 2020-03; ☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03; Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01)

VOL-04 · Stop a muscle when loads become irrelevant

  • Statement: End a muscle's work when it can no longer return to a load relevant to the opening strength work; judge this against absolute (fresh) intensity, not the rising relative intensity of a tired muscle.
  • Numbers: A 300 lb squatter who ends up doing a variation with 150 lb has "dug too deep"; 225x10 squats is easy as an opener but brutal after three other leg lifts.
  • Scope: All trainees; he prefers this in-session cue to MRV guesses.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： absolute vs relative intensity, 2020-10; The hypertrophy series： absolute vs relative intensity, 2020-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06)

VOL-05 · Muscular endurance caps the number of sets

  • Statement: The real limit on sets is muscular endurance: being able to return to baseline and repeat. It sets your maximum recoverable volume and differs by body part.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees; bigger muscles have more endurance, so set counts should differ per body part.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; ANIME WORKOUTS - Would Jack Hanma's Transformation in Grappler Baki be possible , 2020-12; Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07)

VOL-06 · Tonnage creeps up slowly, driven by set and rep progress

  • Statement: Tonnage should stay stable and rise slowly without big dips or spikes; let progress in sets and reps drive tonnage, and use tonnage math mainly to diagnose stalls.
  • Numbers: Adding a 10-rep set at 200 lb adds 2000 lb vs 50 lb from adding 5 lb to the bar.
  • Scope: All trainees; don't add sets just to hit a tonnage number.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current

Intensity: what it is and how much it matters

For him intensity is a measurable quantity (load relative to your max), and by 2024 it is the variable he protects first.

INT-01 · Intensity is a number, not a sensation

  • Statement: Intensity is load relative to your max (% of 1RM, RPE), or mechanical tension on the target muscle; screaming, burning, pain, nausea or breathlessness are not intensity.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09; No one understands training intensity, 2021-11; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01; Scientists VS Meatheads： Who is right? (Nippard vs Bugenhagen), 2024-06)

INT-02 · Pain and nausea are not growth indicators

  • Statement: There is no logical link between pain felt and hypertrophy; "no pain no gain" is in his words a "male power fantasy".
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to spot a fake natty： their training is lazy and yet they grow, 2020-09; A pain free approach to bodybuilding, 2020-10; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01)

INT-03 · Effort is the main hypertrophy variable for naturals

  • Statement: Intensity (effort) is the most important hypertrophy variable; extra volume is a later lever for continued growth, and "hard sets are king".
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Naturals, all levels; someone doing bench, squats, rows and pull-ups hard out-grows someone with perfect exercise selection and no intensity.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-21 he called himself volume-skewed and said he responded poorly to intensity; by 2023-24 intensity drives growth and volume is a last resort ("these days intensity").
  • Check: Does the program improve effort per set before it adds more sets?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09; Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; Time to become indestructible (Self-Improvement Q&A), 2024-10)

INT-04 · Intensity alone is not a program

  • Statement: Intensity is not the only variable: a "high intensity" program is really a low-volume one, and bodybuilding needs both; only-heavy and only-volume are emotional positions, not programming.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Bodybuilders; see VOL-01.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05; Blood and Guts program review, 2020-10; 5 reasons to only lift heavy weight DEBUNKED, 2021-01; Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (ⅠⅠ： Jeff Nippard, Eric Bugenhagen, 2022-04)

INT-05 · Naturals must lift heavy relative to their strength

  • Statement: Pump and volume alone don't work for naturals; heavy work puts you in relevant windows, gives high-quality tonnage in little time and builds the strength that drives volume.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Naturals. He claims anyone saying you can grow on pump and volume alone is on PEDs or doesn't lift (his opinion).

INT-06 · Heavy work saves time

  • Statement: Compounds at relevant loads rack up tonnage fast; very light work would need 4-10 h sessions to match it.
  • Numbers: Sets of 100 would take four hours; even if 30% intensity built equal size it is impractical versus 70%.
  • Scope: Bodybuilders with limited gym time (unlike athletes training ~8 h/day).

INT-07 · Most gym-goers never get close to failure

  • Statement: Quality volume means sets very close to failure; stopping when all reps look identical is just warming up, and he disagrees that ~65% effort is enough.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees, especially commercial-gym and science-content audiences.
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2024→2025
  • Status: current

INT-08 · Effort is a skill learned per exercise

  • Statement: You learn to push and to grind separately for each exercise; keeping form clean under near-maximal loads only comes from training close to failure regularly.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees; many aesthetics-focused trainees "never learn to push", unlike strength athletes.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2024
  • Status: current

INT-09 · Absolute vs relative intensity

  • Statement: Absolute intensity is what you can move fresh and warmed up; relative intensity climbs rep by rep, set by set and through the session as fatigue builds.
  • Numbers: A 70% set is 70% only on rep 1 and can end near 95%; 8 squats starting at 75% end near 100%; set 2's first rep at "80%" is really 81-82%.
  • Scope: All trainees; absolute intensity only changes slowly with strength.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： absolute vs relative intensity, 2020-10; The hypertrophy series： the impact of sets and reps on intensity, 2020-09; No one understands training intensity, 2021-11; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12)

INT-10 · Put the highest intensity at the start of the session

  • Statement: Because relative intensity keeps climbing, programming only by absolute percentages misprograms; optimal intensity exists only at the session's start, which is where strength work belongs.
  • Numbers: 80% at the end of a workout is not 80% at the start; dropping from 3 plates to 1 on rows late in a session means the later work was irrelevant.
  • Scope: Program design.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? (Analyzing Chris Bumstead's Workout w/ , 2022-10)

INT-11 · A set's intensity is the average of its reps

  • Statement: A heavy low-rep set can be more intense overall than a long set that only gets hard at the end, so low-rep sets near 90% keep a place.
  • Numbers: In a 20-rep set the first 10-12 reps are easy; 10 squat reps climb only from ~70% to ~78-79% effective intensity vs 100% for a max single.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Nucleus overload guide (part. 1)： What it is & how to implement it, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： the impact of sets and reps on intensity, 2020-09; Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12; Nucleus overload guide (part. 2)： Which body parts, how to target them & impact , 2020-05)

INT-12 · Intensity is not tied to a rep range

  • Statement: Low reps can be low intensity and high reps high intensity; "low reps for strength, high reps for size" is false, and any range means nothing without effort.
  • Numbers: 95% for 10 reps is possible; a heavy set of 8 is more intense than a light set of 3.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10; 5 reasons to only lift heavy weight DEBUNKED, 2021-01; The hypertrophy series： using intensity to assess risk to reward ratios, 2020-06; How to program evolving rep ranges, 2020-07)

INT-13 · "Heavy" is relative to the lifter and context

  • Statement: Whether a load is heavy depends on the lifter and where it falls in the session; don't let other people's standards push you into ever-lower reps.
  • Numbers: A 120 lb deadlift can be 30% for one lifter and 90% for another; for him 205x12 and 265x2 bench are both heavy; 185x10 close-grip late in a session would be 205-215 as an opener.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Do you need to lift heavy to get big?, 2020-02; Do you need to lift heavy to get big?, 2020-02; No one understands training intensity, 2021-11; Keep Ronnie Coleman's name out of your unworthy hardgainer's mouth, 2021-07)

INT-14 · Raising intensity without adding load

  • Statement: Pre-fatigue, supersets, variations and density raise intensity without more weight, but fatigue-inflated intensity should stay marginal, never the foundation of the program.
  • Numbers: Push-ups before bench make a 50% bench act like 65%; the same tonnage in 2 h instead of 4 h is more intense; with supersets, 4x10-15 instead of 3x12-20.
  • Scope: All trainees; planned pre-fatigue helps, unplanned pre-fatigue hinders progression.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： the hypertrophy rep range conundrum, 2020-05; Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： the impact of sets and reps on intensity, 2020-09)

Intensity windows: loads and rep ranges

INT-15 · Work mostly between ~60% and ~95% of 1RM

  • Statement: The productive window is roughly 60-95% of 1RM; below ~60% is junk volume, and true maxes above ~95% aren't worth the injury risk or the lost tonnage.
  • Numbers: 70-90% (2020-02); 60-95% (2020-09); 60-95/96% with 20-60% junk (2021-11); 70-90% for bodybuilders (2022-03); 60-90% (2022-12); 65-95% (2023-03). His own: 70-90/95%, ~90% for most lifts (2020). Absolute floor ~40% 1RM (2020).
  • Scope: Bodybuilding, naturals. Exception: nucleus overload (VOL-55).
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the bulk of working-set load between about 60% and 95% of 1RM?
  • Sources: (When are you intermediate and what it means programming wise (for bodybuilding), 2020-02; The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09; No one understands training intensity, 2021-11; What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03)

INT-16 · Average intensity about 85%

  • Statement: ~85% is the average across training, not a per-set target; individual days can swing as long as the bulk averages ~85%, and that average sets fatigue, frequency, sets and reps.
  • Numbers: ~85% average; a day at 95% and the next at 65% is fine.
  • Scope: Program-level planning.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: contradicted — 2020 he said steady 85-95% beats swinging between 99% and 60%; 2022 he allows swings around an 85% average.
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： deloading without wasting tonnage, 2020-12; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12)

INT-17 · Rep range: mostly 6-12, all work 3-15

  • Statement: Bodybuilding work sits mostly at 6-12 reps within an overall 3-15 span; above 15-20 is junk, and singles to triples should not make up the bulk.
  • Numbers: 20-35 cap (2020-02); 2-15 (2020-09; core 3-9 for tall lanky lifters); 2-12 (2021-06); 6-12 with extremes 3-4 and 15-20 (2022-12); 6-15 most work (2023-01); 3-15, mostly 6-12, >20 junk, "never 20+" (2024).
  • Scope: Looks-focused trainees; only some forearm and neck work goes higher.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — upper limit fell from 20-35 reps (early 2020) to ~15 (2020-09) and "never 20+" (2024).
  • Check: Do most working sets fall in 6-12 reps, with almost none above 15-20?
  • Sources: (Transcendent training review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02; How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

INT-18 · High-rep sets rarely reach real failure

  • Statement: Above ~15-20 reps each extra rep adds little intensity, and cardio, lactic burn or technique stop you before the muscle does. In 2025 he adds that true failure is reachable at 12-15, and higher ranges are more forgiving for grinding.
  • Numbers: First compound of the day ~10 reps, not 15; 10-15 hammer curls are worse than 8-12; 35 reps is "ridiculous"; 3x6-10 DB press beats 180 reps of raises.
  • Scope: All trainees; boredom in high-rep sets is a load-selection problem (2025).
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12; The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02; The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03)

INT-19 · Low reps build size too

  • Statement: Low reps (3-5, 4-8) work for size and help naturals by raising the absolute intensity used for higher-rep work; he rejects the claim that anything under 5 (or 7-8) reps is useless.
  • Numbers: EZ curls 3x5-8; weighted fat-grip pull-ups 4-8; naturals need 6-10, 4-8 and the occasional 3x5; "low reps" means under 5-6.
  • Scope: Naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11; Analyzing the Rock's ＂Black Adam＂ training program, 2021-03; The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell), 2023-07; Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12)

INT-20 · Never test true 1RMs for hypertrophy

  • Statement: True 1RMs have an atrocious fatigue-to-stimulus ratio, give little tonnage and raise injury risk; working up to a max and stopping gives you only the warm-up.
  • Numbers: Curls never below 3-4 reps; weighted dips never need true 1RMs.
  • Scope: Hypertrophy training; rare testing builds strength better than constant maxing.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the program avoid true 1RM attempts and keep singles-to-triples out of the bulk of the work?
  • Sources: (How to program an arm day (the Natural Hypertrophy example), 2020-01; Is CNS fatigue out to get you?, 2022-03; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06)

INT-21 · Low-rep work is a tonnage trap if overdone

  • Statement: A true 3RM gives little tonnage and can't be repeated for four sets, while many easy triples aren't truly intense; with low reps, fewer sets are better.
  • Numbers: 2x3 or 2x5 may beat 3x3 or 5x5 for hypertrophy (2023); only the last set of a 3x3 is near failure.
  • Scope: Naturals using low reps.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the issue of intensity without volume, 2020-07; The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12)

INT-22 · Fixed rep "zones" are myths

  • Statement: "6-8 strength / 8-12 size / 12+ endurance", "10-15 is best, never below 8" and "compounds low, isolations high" are wrong as fixed rules; choose 6-10, 8-12 or 10-15 by preference and by what lets you progress.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Bodybuilder Roasts AI Generated Program 👨‍💻, 2023-01; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01; Powerbuilding is an Abomination., 2023-10)

INT-23 · Still, match the rep range to the lift

  • Statement: Each lift and muscle has its own best window found by experiment; compounds usually go lower and isolations higher, and heavy/medium/light ranges should stay close together.
  • Numbers: Heavy 3-6/2-5/3-5, medium 6-10/6-12, light 8-10/8-12/8-15; never a 1-rep heavy day with a 20-rep light day; 1-15 is too wide to be useful; rear delts at 3-5 or weighted dips at 10-15 are mismatches.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： intensity windows and their applications, 2020-09; Fullbody template review, 2021-01; How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

INT-24 · A rep range is a bracket around near-failure

  • Statement: Pick the weight so the target rep lands near failure; without high intensity you plateau in any range.
  • Numbers: Lowering rep ranges ~12-20% across the board raises intensity; 6-10 is more intense than 10-15, and grinding 2 more reps past "failure" at 15 means the load isn't challenging.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 2), 2020-08; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01; Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01; Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02)

Failure and reps in reserve

Failure is defined narrowly (the muscle stops), used selectively, and never means missing a rep.

INT-25 · The target is muscular failure

  • Statement: Count only failure where the target muscle is the limit. Cardio, lactic burn, pump, occlusion or a structural breakdown (artificial or mechanical failure) feel hard but build little and cap tonnage.
  • Numbers: He curls 135 lb for 8 but can't do 40 empty-bar reps (pump fatigue, not muscular failure); 20% of your squat for max reps gives a pump but little stimulus.
  • Scope: All trainees; novices often mistake cardio fatigue for failure. A few artificial-failure sets are acceptable, not as the focus.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — terminology only: "mechanical failure" means structural breakdown in 2020-21 but in 2023 he "defines failure as mechanical failure" (stop when body English appears).
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： volume vs intensity, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： artificial vs organical failure, 2020-07; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; I was… wrong? (Giving Mike Israetel a Fair Review of RP’s Mass Gain Training, 2022-09)

INT-26 · Failure = no further clean rep

  • Statement: Failure is the point where you cannot do another rep with clean form; the set ends as soon as you need body English or a torso shift, and partials after failure only move the standard.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Bodybuilding.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05; SAVAGE PUSH DAY 🔥 (Hypertrophy Log #3), 2023-07; Why everyone HATES Paul Carter (liftrunbang1), 2024-02)

INT-27 · Never actually miss a rep

  • Statement: "Going to failure" means hitting the last rep you can complete; a missed rep is a programming error that raises injury risk, hurts morale and ruins the rest of the session.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Bodybuilders; missed reps may belong in powerlifting. Failing weekly means the program is wrong.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are loads chosen so that reps are reached at or near failure but never actually missed?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the importance of going to failure for muscle building, 2020-05; Smolov program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-08; The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11; The Educated Barbarian： An introduction to Stoicism (Enchiridion analysis part. , 2021-06)

INT-28 · Selective failure: isolations yes, squats and hinges no

  • Statement: Take isolation, upper-body presses, rows, pulldowns and other low-risk lifts to failure on every set; keep 1-2 reps in reserve on squats, deadlifts, good mornings and other risky lower-body compounds.
  • Numbers: 0 RIR on isolation, presses, rows; 1-2 RIR on squats and hinges. He personally takes 1 RIR on presses because of a neck/upper-back nerve issue.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~22 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 "every working set goes to failure" (with a rep kept on strength compounds); from 2022 failure only where it is safe and recoverable.
  • Check: Do isolation and upper-body sets end at 0-1 RIR while squats, deadlifts and good mornings stop 1-2 reps short?
  • Sources: (Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07; The hypertrophy series： the importance of going to failure for muscle building, 2020-05; Can you look like Kratos from God of War in real life? (RAGNAROK WORKOUT), 2022-11; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09)

INT-29 · Isolation lifts deserve full intensity

  • Statement: Isolations have the best stimulus-to-fatigue ratio and low injury risk, so push them as hard as a deadlift; small muscles respond to intensity like big ones.
  • Numbers: 10-12 cable curls with 10 RIR stimulate nothing; 5x10-15 easy arm work is junk.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08; Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique, 2022-11; Hypertrophy training is CANCELLED, 2024-06)

INT-30 · Failure is a calibration tool, not the goal

  • Statement: Proximity to failure is what matters; failure is the baseline for judging effort, and failing on everything misallocates recovery ("always training to failure is stupid").
  • Numbers: Sets at 70-90% also grow muscle.
  • Scope: All trainees; the opposite swing, fear of failure, is just as wrong.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2022→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11)

INT-31 · Decide where to fail by recoverability

  • Statement: Failure is fine where you can train the muscle again soon (curls, laterals), not where it blocks a pattern for a week; recovery cost depends on the load at which you fail.
  • Numbers: 4 curl sets to failure recover in ~3 days; 5 hard deadlift sets to failure can stop heavy hinging for ≥1 week.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the importance of going to failure for muscle building, 2020-05; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12)

INT-32 · Hard sets must be repeatable within 2-3 days

  • Statement: Keep enough in the tank to train the muscle again in 2-3 days; a set you can only recover from every 15 days is not a good hard set. Repeatability is "the bread and butter of natural bodybuilding".
  • Numbers: Retrain within 2-3 days; 99% efforts are fine if not too often.
  • Scope: Naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Check: Can every muscle be trained hard again within 2-3 days of its last session?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： defining hard sets, 2020-07; Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05; Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12)

INT-33 · Reps in reserve on squats and deadlifts

  • Statement: On heavy squats, deadlifts and their variations leave the "danger rep" in the tank for form and injury prevention.
  • Numbers: 2020: exactly 1 RIR, never 2+ (5 possible → do 4; 450x3 becomes 2). 2022-24: 1-2 RIR, often 2 (6 possible → stop at 4; 10 of 12 on good mornings; SSB squats without safeties 2 short).
  • Scope: Squats, deadlifts, good mornings and heavy variations.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-11 exactly 1 RIR and "2+ means bad weight selection"; 2022-24 1-2 RIR, usually 2.
  • Sources: (Serious injuries don't just ＂happen＂, 2020-01; The hypertrophy series： applying reps in reserve while minimizing tonnage loss, 2020-11; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; Bodybuilding is killing me (Hypertrophy Log #8), 2024-09)

INT-34 · RIR picks your battles

  • Statement: RIR is not the enemy of failure: before grinding, ask whether the rep is worth the risk that day; the last two grinding reps aren't magic, and heavy compounds benefit most from RIR.
  • Numbers: Dial back the last reps in 1-2 of every 4-5 sessions; 4 of a planned 6 squats is still quality tonnage.
  • Scope: Heavy compounds mostly.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06; 3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06; 3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06; Hypertrophy training is CANCELLED, 2024-06)

INT-35 · Use RIR on low-rep work, starting small

INT-36 · Learn failure before using RPE or RIR

  • Statement: RPE and RIR only mean something once you've trained to failure many times, so beginners must learn failure first.

INT-37 · Percentages vs RPE vs feel

  • Statement: Percentages, RPE and RIR are interchangeable A-tier tools and he recommends % of an estimated 1RM, yet in his own training he uses none of them: a rep range from experience, push to failure, add weight when the top gets easy.

INT-38 · Strength-athlete sandbagging doesn't suit bodybuilders

  • Statement: Planned sub-maximal strategies from strength sports (capping at 70%, RIR sandbagging, speed pulls) don't fit bodybuilding; progressing 4-6 reps with reserve "is just sandbagging".

INT-39 · Safer lower-body lifts go to failure

Hard sets, repeatability and sandbagging

INT-40 · Hard sets are the most important sets

  • Statement: A hard set uses a challenging load, ends at muscular failure and is repeatable enough to accumulate tonnage; make as much of your tonnage as possible come from hard sets, including accessories, not only strength work.
  • Numbers: ~10 hard sets fit in one workout across different planes; S tier (2023), "king" (2024).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are most of the program's sets hard sets ending near muscular failure?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： defining hard sets, 2020-07; The hypertrophy series： volume vs tonnage, 2020-03; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01)

INT-41 · A growth set moves the muscle off its baseline

  • Statement: A set that produces growth leaves the muscle unable to repeat the same effort within the session; it needs days, not 3-4 minutes, to recover. Too light and the muscle returns to baseline too easily.
  • Numbers: After one all-out set you still get ~80% of the reps, so keep working until loads become irrelevant (VOL-04).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05; Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01)

INT-42 · Repeatability tests show whether a set was hard

  • Statement: If you can nearly match a set shortly after, it wasn't hard enough.
  • Numbers: 55 push-ups then 53 two minutes later = not damaging; baseline 30, post-bench 30/29 = no stimulus, 30/20 = stimulus; after 12 to failure you should still get ≥8; a true max double shouldn't repeat after 10-15 min.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Nucleus overload guide (part. 2)： Which body parts, how to target them & impact , 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02; The hypertrophy series： stimulus to fatigue ratio, 2020-06; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01)

INT-43 · Load checks for too-light work

  • Statement: If you still hit the same back-off numbers after the main work, or the bar flies on squats and deadlifts, the weight is too light; if you could do 7 sets instead of 5 with the same reps, add load.
  • Numbers: Front squat 200x5 fresh and still 200x5 easily after back squats means raise it.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05; Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05)

INT-44 · Sandbagging: when it is fine and when it isn't

  • Statement: Sandbagging is giving less than full effort without a reason. Chosen sandbagging (warm-ups, planned RIR, a muscle trained again in 2 days) is fine; sandbagging forced by the scheme wastes quality tonnage.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees; it belongs at the start (strength work) and, involuntarily, at the end of a session, not in the middle.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11; Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05)

INT-45 · Fixed multi-set schemes force sandbagging

  • Statement: 5x5, 5x10, 10x10, 4x10 and fixed 8s or 12s force you to hold back early sets; with real effort reps decline across sets.
  • Numbers: If set 1 of 5x5 were a true 5RM, set 2 would be 3-4 reps; 10 then 9-8 is real; 3x5 beats 5x5; 3x8 bench invites more sandbagging than 3x4.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets, 2020-11; The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11; The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06; The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06)

INT-46 · Use evolving (declining) rep ranges

  • Statement: Write ranges so reps trickle down toward failure each set; small brackets mean more intensity and more sandbagging risk, wide ones the reverse.
  • Numbers: 6-10 should read 10/9/8; 8/7/6/5; at low reps a 2-rep window (6-8, not fixed 8 or a wide 5-8); 6-5-4 matches 5-5-5 tonnage with a more intense first set.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to start using evolving rep ranges in your training, 2020-09; Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-12; How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10)

INT-47 · Too much work forces survival pacing

  • Statement: Piling exercises or huge volume into a session makes you pace and sandbag the top work, turning lifting into cardio with weights; if you pace sets to survive later exercises, the program is badly built.
  • Numbers: Four heavy chest compounds in one session is an example; beginners on 15-rep machine work stop pushing by rep 8.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02; Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03; Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? (Analyzing Chris Bumstead's Workout w/ , 2022-10; Heavy Duty Arm Day (Hypertrophy Log #1), 2023-07)

Strength work, back-offs and grinding

INT-48 · Opening strength work is an appetizer

  • Statement: High intensity lives in 1-3 sets of opening strength work that should prime you, not wreck you; then come variations and accessories at relevant intensity.
  • Numbers: 1-3 strength sets; more than ~4 stops being max effort.
  • Scope: All trainees; top sets drive progression more than they build muscle directly. See ch. 7.

INT-49 · Bodybuilding intensity is sustained, not one explosion

  • Statement: Bodybuilding effort is "a steady fire" of repeated hard sets rather than one all-out effort.

  • Scope: Bodybuilders.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2021→2022

INT-50 · Back-off sets stay tied to the top weight

  • Statement: Back-off weight is tied to the strength-work weight and still pushed near failure in a sensible rep range; once you'd have to strip the bar, stop doing hard sets on that lift.

INT-51 · Don't open a session with junk

  • Statement: Never do light high-rep work before the main sets; lifters who know the lifts shouldn't start a program at low intensity, and pyramiding up to 8 reps is just a warm-up.

INT-52 · Grinding: damaging on compounds, useful on good isolations

  • Statement: Grindy compound reps drain you more than anything and the grind-through mentality causes injuries; reps should be challenging, never damaging. On isolations with a good strength curve, slow grinding reps keep you near failure longer and are desirable.

  • Scope: Compounds vs isolations (he never states the split explicitly).

INT-53 · Injury risk is near the max, not at 90%

  • Statement: With solid technique and recovery-matched volume, injury risk rises less with intensity than people think; the danger zone is near a true 1RM.
  • Numbers: 90% carries little more risk than 60%.
  • Scope: All trainees; see ch. 9.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020
  • Status: current

INT-54 · The pump is a by-product, not a goal

  • Statement: Chasing the pump means light weights, high reps and no attention to failure or load; tension and fibre damage drive growth, and a program can give no pump and still grow you.
  • Numbers: Pump rated C tier (2023); heavy 3-5-rep squats or bench rarely pump yet build more than band presses.

Intensity techniques

INT-55 · Techniques are the cherry on top

  • Statement: Drop sets, clusters, tempo, short rests, rest-pause and myo-reps are added to a quality set, never replacing it or hurting the hard sets.
  • Numbers: Myo-reps programmed as top sets are unacceptable.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05; The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell), 2023-07; Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01)

INT-56 · Rest-pause is his preferred technique

  • Statement: At failure, rest briefly while focusing on the muscle, then add reps; post-pause reps must be the hardest of the set. It works best at higher reps, so it pushes rep ranges up.
  • Numbers: Rest 10-20 s (range 3-30 s) → +2-5 reps, ~+10-50% hyper-intense volume; after 8 reps and 15 s ~4 more, on a 3-5 set barely one; start with 1-2 rest-pause sets, on the last set.
  • Scope: Introduce on isolations first, then upper-body compounds, only later lower-body compounds; advanced lifters especially.
  • Confidence: high — ~16 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: changed — 2020-21 skeptical, ranked last ("leaks tonnage", "three sets in disguise"); 2023-25 his favourite technique, preferred over drop sets.
  • Sources: (5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07; I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08; 20 inch arms CMON (Hypertrophy Log #9), 2024-12; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03)

INT-57 · Drop sets and forced reps: occasional at most

  • Statement: Drop sets on every set are pump-chasing junk; use them only to reach target reps once rest-pause fails. Forced reps, forced negatives and beyond-failure work are an extra set in disguise with a poor stimulus-to-fatigue ratio.
  • Numbers: Drop 5-10 lb on cable triceps extensions after failing at 10 of 15; beyond-failure work max 1 set per muscle per day (C tier); drop sets never on strength or main lifts.
  • Scope: Accessories; forced negatives once called "amazing" for biceps (2020).
  • Confidence: high — ~17 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07; The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04)

INT-58 · Lengthened partials: may work, not his tool

  • Statement: Lengthened partials may work and many intermediates report gains, but he finds them clunky and hard to standardise and gets more from rest-pause.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01; Why everyone HATES Paul Carter (liftrunbang1), 2024-02)

INT-59 · AMRAPs out of loaded bodybuilding work

  • Statement: AMRAPs don't belong on top sets, strength work or loaded accessories, where the weight should dictate a rep range; keep them for finishers and unweighted calisthenics.
  • Numbers: An AMRAP top set reaching 14 reps is in an irrelevant window; bodyweight pull-ups AMRAP 3-4 sets 1x/wk (2023).
  • Scope: Bodybuilding programs.
  • Confidence: medium — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 he liked AMRAP pull-ups; 2021 finishers and calisthenics only; 2024 drop AMRAPs from bodybuilding programs.
  • Sources: (Program critique #1 (Upper Lower Push Pull), 2020-02; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

INT-60 · Burnouts and widowmakers are occasional tools

  • Statement: Burnouts and widowmaker squats are occasional high-effort tools, not regular programming.
  • Numbers: Burnout: 20RM to failure, rest 2 min, failure, 1 min, failure, 30 s, failure. Widowmaker: 10RM squat for 20 reps without racking, about once a month, then time to flush fatigue.
  • Scope: Trained lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Squat Everyday vs Widow makers squats for hypertrophy, 2020-07; Can you look like Kratos from God of War in real life? (RAGNAROK WORKOUT), 2022-11; Did Tom Platz know how to train LEGS? (Analyzing the Quadfather's Training Metho, 2022-11)

INT-61 · Slow-tempo work kills intensity

  • Statement: Long-tempo sets are boring, kill focus and intensity, and make fatigue hard to track.
  • Numbers: E.g. 15 reps with 6-s negatives; 10 lb slow laterals without overload or failure.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: low — ~2 videos, 2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01; The Hypocrisy of Science-Based Lifters, 2024-12)

INT-62 · HIT and Mentzer: right on intensity, too far on volume

  • Statement: He sees himself as doing high intensity across many sets; one set to failure every 6-8 days is too little for naturals. Mentzer was right to focus on intensity but went too far.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Naturals; see VOL-12.
  • Confidence: medium — ~8 videos, 2020→2024

Focus and non-bodybuilders

INT-63 · Train with focus, save the hype

  • Statement: No phone, chatting or dates in the gym; think about the next set between sets. Save loud music for top sets so you don't desensitize.
  • Numbers: ~90-95% of sessions with podcasts, classical music or silence.
  • Scope: All trainees; he PRs whenever he trains with his gym buddy.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2022→2024
