INT-64 · Athletes and fighters: stimulate, don't annihilate

  • Statement: For athletes and fighters, lifting stays sub-maximal and never grinds; all-out effort belongs in competition.
  • Numbers: ~70-80% of capacity with 1-2 RIR.
  • Scope: Non-bodybuilders (athletes, fighters).
  • Confidence: medium — ~2 videos, 2021→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Lifting plans for Athletes (programming for sports), 2021-09; Bodybuilders can't FIGHT (but martial artists should lift), 2022-01)

Junk volume

Junk volume is his main tool for cutting programs down: work that adds sets without adding relevant tonnage.

VOL-07 · What junk volume is

  • Statement: Junk volume is work outside a relevant intensity window: unchallenging loads, pump chasing, and sets ended by cardio or pump rather than muscular failure.
  • Numbers: Typical case: a 30-rep weight stopped at ~20 by pump; BFR or pump drop sets; 25-rep machine sets.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the program free of sets that end from burn, pump or breathlessness rather than muscle failure?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： nucleus overload vs junk volume, 2020-10; Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02; WEIGHTS vs MACHINES： Which one is better for muscle gains?, 2022-01)

VOL-08 · Junk is relative and mainly hurts when it replaces hard sets

  • Statement: Junk volume depends on your muscular endurance and is mainly a problem when it replaces hard sets or takes time from other muscles; calling every set after a top set junk is Mentzer logic.
  • Numbers: A second set costs about 3-4 minutes.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: changed — 2021 he called the junk-volume concept "overblown"; 2022-24 he applies the label widely and asks for the "bare effective minimum".
  • Sources: (The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; Pushing progression and avoiding plateaus using evolving rep ranges, 2021-04; Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10; This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06)

VOL-09 · Typical junk schemes, including 10x10

  • Statement: 10x10/GVT, 5x10 and 5x20 schemes, 25 chest sets, 13+ biceps sets in a session, 10x20 cable work and many sets of light laterals are typical junk. 10x10 is a band-aid: if you can repeat 10 reps for 10 sets the load is uninteresting.
  • Numbers: On 25 chest sets 60-70% of reps do nothing; on a ~300-rep push day 65-75% is junk; true GVT forces ~55-60% 1RM instead of 70-75%; 3 sets in a relevant window may beat it.
  • Scope: All trainees; 2024: "10x10 is sandbagging".
  • Confidence: high — ~25 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The issue with 10x10 / German Volume Training, 2020-11; Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05; The BEST Workout if you like to waste time for no results (Ryan Humiston Split/P, 2022-02; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

VOL-10 · Most programs are too greedy

  • Statement: He trims most reviewed programs and says most bodybuilders could cut a fifth to a third of their training for the same results.
  • Numbers: Typical cut 20-30% (sometimes 40-80%); arm programs of 21-30 sets cut by 80%; a chest+biceps day for naturals could lose 45%.
  • Scope: All trainees, especially program reviews.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (5 days Upper Lower program review (part. 1), 2020-10; How to modify any training program, 2021-03; Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

How much volume

VOL-11 · Do the least volume that keeps you progressing

  • Statement: Do as little as needed for as much growth as possible: the minimal sets that keep you progressing and injury-free, leaving room to add later. Volume "only serves the purpose of progression".
  • Numbers: By 2024 he places himself "closer to HIT than to 18-20 sets" per muscle.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~16 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: changed — 2020-22 maximalist ("more work always gives more" if you recover, sit at the brink of overtraining, 2-3 h sessions); from 2021 minimal-effective, and by 2024 low on the volume spectrum.
  • Check: Is each muscle's weekly volume the lowest that still produces progress?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03)

VOL-12 · Both extremes fail: one set and 10x10

  • Statement: HIT's single set is too little for naturals and GVT/10x10 too much; naturals grow in the middle. Multiple hard sets compound reps and give room to modulate effort.
  • Numbers: One set of 17 can't beat 13+10+10+10; 3-4 sets at 240 lb beat 1 at 250; 2024: HIT still beats GVT because it leaves room to add.
  • Scope: Naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #2, 2020-10; Minimalist training bad, 2021-06; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

VOL-13 · Minimalism is a tool, not an ideology

  • Statement: Minimal programs fit strength, athletes, beginners and busy people, but tend to build unbalanced physiques for bodybuilders; at an advanced level the maximalist's last ~20% decides things.
  • Numbers: Cuts hurt maximalists more in absolute tonnage (50,000 → 25,000 vs 10,000 → 5,000).
  • Scope: Advanced bodybuilders vs everyone else.
  • Confidence: medium — ~8 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: contradicted — in 2024 he calls maximalist whole-body isolation the best, yet places himself closer to HIT and says most could cut 20-30%.
  • Sources: (Minimalist training bad, 2021-06; Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03; Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09)

VOL-14 · Too little vs too much: err slightly high

  • Statement: Constantly doing too little gives plateaus and too much gives injury or regression; when guessing, err slightly high, but add conservatively.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: changed — 2020 "too much is worse than too little"; 2022 too many sets cost at worst some junk volume, so err high.
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： using volume to assess recovery abilities, 2020-06; Hypertrophy Q&A #2, 2020-10; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03)

VOL-15 · People respond differently to volume and intensity

  • Statement: Some respond more to volume and others to intensity; a muscle that won't grow may need more volume, and someone who can't recover needs less volume and more intensity.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Individual tuning; he saw himself as a volume responder in 2020-22.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Recomp guide (part. 3)： performance & body fat loss/distribution, 2020-06; STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08; Jeff Nippard & Alec Enkiri Want Me To Deload... I Don't Wanna (Size vs Strength , 2022-03; The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08)

VOL-16 · Train between medium and maximum recoverable volume

  • Statement: Maximum recoverable volume (MRV) is the most work you can recover and grow from; aim between medium and maximum. MRV is individual, found by experiment and only diagnosable after the fact, and it rises with training age.
  • Numbers: ~25% above minimum without passing the max is fine; most people don't overshoot.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~12 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02; The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07)

VOL-17 · Signs of too much volume

  • Statement: Lingering soreness or failing to repeat performance session to session signals too much volume; at high weekly sets with slow strength gains, try less volume and more intensity.
  • Numbers: 15-20 weekly sets with slow strength gains → try less.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — 1 video, 2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06)

VOL-18 · Manual laborers need less gym volume

  • Statement: Office workers can aim at their MRV; manual laborers should stay lower with high intensity and low frequency, and athletes must count the volume from their sport.
  • Numbers: 2 heavy sets of a compound instead of 4-8.
  • Scope: Physical jobs, athletes.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Scheduling your training for White Collar workers, 2021-02; Scheduling your training for White Collar workers, 2021-02; TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09)

Weekly sets per muscle

VOL-19 · A weekly set count means little on its own

  • Statement: Arbitrary weekly numbers ignore frequency, rep range and distribution; the optimal count is whatever produces growth, and ±1-2 sets don't matter. Different body parts naturally take different counts.
  • Numbers: The 10-20 guideline is "mathematically sound but not a hard rule".
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Natural Q&A #2, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07)

VOL-20 · If you need a number: 8-14 hard sets a week

  • Statement: As a rough answer, 8-14 weekly sets per muscle; at 3x/week and high intensity, 9-15 hard sets is enough to keep growing.
  • Numbers: 8-14 (rough math ~7-14: about 4 sessions per 8 days x 2-4 sets, 2022); 9-15 at 3x/wk (2023).
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced naturals; back is an exception (VOL-45).
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2022→2023
  • Status: current
  • Check: Do most muscles get roughly 8-14 hard sets a week?
  • Sources: (How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06)

VOL-21 · Weekly sets by training level

  • Statement: Novices need few weekly sets and build up; intermediates build toward a cap of about 12.
  • Numbers: Novice 3-6/wk (3 once or twice a week, never 6 at once); intermediate 6-12, cap 12, +2 at a time; 2020: 3 → 9 → 12 hard sets by level.
  • Scope: Novice → intermediate; see ch. 12.
  • Confidence: high — ~4 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01; Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01)

VOL-22 · Almost no one needs 16-20 weekly sets

  • Statement: 16-20 weekly sets per muscle is more than almost anyone needs and is impractical to schedule.
  • Numbers: 20 sets/wk would mean 5 sessions x 4 sets or 2 x 10; most lifters do 12-20, about 10 can work for intermediates; an advanced natural on ~4 hard sets/wk may only maintain.
  • Scope: Most muscles; back excepted.
  • Confidence: medium — ~2 videos, 2022
  • Status: contradicted — 2023 back caps reach 20-28 and his own 2023 week had 20 back and 18 shoulder sets; partly explained by the back's tolerance.
  • Sources: (Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11)

Sets per exercise and per session

VOL-23 · Two to four sets per exercise, usually three

  • Statement: Most exercises get 2-4 sets ("rule of three"); fewer for advanced lifters on taxing lifts, with a 4th set only as icing.
  • Numbers: 2020: accessories almost always 4 (2 too few, 5 too many). 2023: 2-4, usually 3. 2024: 3 for novice/intermediate, 2 for advanced. 2025: 2 per taxing lift if you progress. A 5th-7th set means the load wasn't challenging (2021).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: changed — 2020 four sets as default; 2023-25 three, then two for advanced lifters.
  • Check: Do most exercises use 2-4 working sets?
  • Sources: (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03)

VOL-24 · Heavy low-rep work: one to three sets

  • Statement: Heavy strength work gets 1-3 sets, never 5 or 10; one heavy set leaves room for more accessory volume, three means easier accessories.
  • Numbers: 1-3 sets (2020); low-rep compounds 2-3, never more (2024).
  • Scope: Strength work on compounds; see ch. 7.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06; How to set up evolving rep ranges (theoretical aspects), 2020-06; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

VOL-25 · Two to four sets per muscle per session

  • Statement: 2-4 sets per muscle per session is the most productive range and is used in all his programs; 6+ sets in one session forces lower frequency.
  • Numbers: 2022: two sets per body part per day is plenty; 2024: 4-6 hard sets per muscle per session already counts as high volume.
  • Scope: All trainees, at 2-3x/week frequency.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does each muscle get about 2-4 hard sets per session rather than 6+ on one day?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How the King of Zoomers Trains to Look like a Greek God (Alex Eubank Program Rev, 2022-12; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

VOL-26 · At most two exercises per muscle per day

  • Statement: Use at most two exercises per body part per day; a third variation is excess fatigue.
  • Numbers: 1 for novices, 2 normally, 3 for some advanced; 3+3 sets of two compounds is plenty; after pull-ups and one pulldown the lats are done.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does every muscle get at most two exercises per session?
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05; Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? (Analyzing Chris Bumstead's Workout w/ , 2022-10; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06; The Natty Arnold? (Joel Kellett aka Overkell), 2023-07)

VOL-27 · More sets per session means less intensity per set

  • Statement: Packing a muscle's sets into one session costs both frequency and per-set intensity; low per-session sets suit high frequency.
  • Numbers: 8-12 sets for a body part in one session costs frequency and intensity; 2+2 sets of two similar exercises avoid the intensity loss of 4 straight sets.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2022→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06; The Hardworking Lifter who BROKE the Natty Limit (Alex Leonidas), 2023-05; I was… wrong? (Giving Mike Israetel a Fair Review of RP’s Mass Gain Training, 2022-09)

VOL-28 · Session set totals by split (2024)

  • Statement: Total sets per session shrink as training days increase.
  • Numbers: 4 days/wk ≈ 20 sets per session; 5 days ≈ 14-15 (cut 15-20%); upper/lower: upper 18-24, lower 16-20; his commercial-gym days ≈ 24 sets in under 2 h, 30-34 is a heavy day.
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced; 2024 figures.
  • Confidence: medium — ~2 videos, 2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

Adding and cutting volume

VOL-29 · Add volume only on a stall, two sets at a time

  • Statement: Add volume only when load, reps and tonnage stall, in small steps; past a point progress should come from intensity rather than more sets.
  • Numbers: About +2 sets per body part (2-4 max) per adjustment.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2021→2025
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are sets added only after progress stalls, and only about two at a time?
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05; Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split, 2021-06)

VOL-30 · Never jump volume

  • Statement: Volume spikes bring no results, sickness or overuse injury, and people then wrongly blame volume.
  • Numbers: You can't jump from 9 to 16 sets; don't double volume on becoming intermediate.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05; How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09; Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10; TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09)

VOL-31 · Introducing a new exercise

  • Statement: Start a new exercise at low volume and build up, trimming other work to make room; or use several sets with very light weight.
  • Numbers: 1-2 sets (~50% of the main lift's volume), trim others to 2, then +1 set every week or two up to 4; adding 4 sets of a brand-new exercise exhausts you.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： maintaining tonnage stability for long term progress, 2020-05; How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09)

VOL-32 · Bringing in a new small muscle

  • Statement: Start direct work for a newly trained small muscle at 2-3 weekly sets and build.
  • Numbers: Biceps 3 → 4 → 6; neck 3 → 6 → 9 → 10-12; abs 2-3; small muscles 3 → 6; weak arms 3 sets then 7-8.
  • Scope: Muscles not trained directly before; see also FRQ-27.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Pain free wrist curls： the finger curls solution for bigger forearms, 2021-04; How to modify any training program, 2021-03; Most UNDERRATED Muscle for Aesthetics (TAKE THE NECK PILL), 2022-11; Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01)

VOL-33 · Add conservatively, cut liberally

  • Statement: Programming is subtraction as well as addition: be conservative when adding and liberal when removing. "If you can shrink a day, always shrink it."
  • Numbers: If you still progress at 12 sets, drop from 15.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2021→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets per muscle group, 2020-10; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How to modify any training program, 2021-03; Jeff Nippard's Push Pull Legs program review, 2021-01)

VOL-34 · Cut sets, not reps; cut strength sets first

  • Statement: To reduce fatigue, cut sets rather than reps, and cut strength-work sets (to 1-3) before lowering back-off intensity.
  • Numbers: Strength work is a small share of tonnage, so cutting it barely matters.
  • Scope: All trainees; see ch. 4.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1), 2020-10; The hypertrophy series： using strength work to control tonnage without sacrifice, 2020-07; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03)

VOL-35 · Move volume from dominant muscles to weak points

  • Statement: Budget weekly volume: take some from a dominant muscle and spend it on weak points or recovery; dominant parts won't shrink.
  • Numbers: Take 30-40% from a dominant muscle; cutting 20% of dominant-leg volume "makes no difference" (2024).
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced; e.g. cut leg volume to let the upper body catch up.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to modify any training program, 2021-03; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11)

VOL-36 · Maintenance takes about half the volume

  • Statement: Keep intensity and roughly halve the volume to maintain a muscle that has reached your goal; taper it down gradually.
  • Numbers: Taper 8 → 6 → 4 sets/wk; legs: squat 3x5 @2 RIR + RDL 3x12 every 10 days, or 3x6-8 squats. He maintains biceps with intensity alone.
  • Scope: Muscles at goal size; legs need more maintenance tonnage than biceps.
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05; What really happens when you skip a day, 2021-05)

VOL-37 · Don't cut volume pre-emptively for age or a cut

  • Statement: Lowering volume and intensity in advance because of age causes the muscle loss people then blame on age. During a cut, stay at the edge of the intensity you can handle rather than dropping to ~60%.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Older lifters, dieting lifters; see ch. 11.
  • Confidence: low — ~2 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The reason people lose so much strength/size on cuts, 2020-09; How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com), 2021-12)

Work capacity

VOL-38 · Work capacity is built gradually

  • Statement: Work capacity is what lets you do the volume that drives growth; it is built and lost gradually, and more muscle raises it.
  • Numbers: Building capacity for 2 h of heavy work may take 3-4 years.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： surpassing cardiovascular limitations, 2020-05; How to start doing more volume in your training, 2020-09; Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

VOL-39 · "Intermediate syndrome": use a bridge program

  • Statement: Jumping from a low-volume novice program to a high-volume one fails; use a bridge program, because an advanced program "must be earned".
  • Numbers: Intermediates with poor capacity drop the last line of each day.
  • Scope: Novice → intermediate transition; see ch. 12.
  • Confidence: high — ~4 videos, 2021→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08; Can you look like Kratos from God of War in real life? (RAGNAROK WORKOUT), 2022-11; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06; Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout), 2022-10)

VOL-40 · Advanced lifters pack more tonnage into the same time

  • Statement: Advanced lifters need more tonnage but get no more gym time, so they raise density with supersets; eventually the only way to add volume is longer sessions.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： controlling volume & intensity to promote progression, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： determining optimal training durations, 2020-06; Building work capacity with cardio specificity, 2021-02)

Distribution of volume

VOL-41 · Strength work is ~20%, the rest makes you grow

  • Statement: Strength work opens the session and gives the highest-quality tonnage but is a minority; the variations and accessories that follow provide most of the growth stimulus.
  • Numbers: ~20% strength vs ~80% variations and accessories; typical 2020 day: 1-3 strength sets + 6-8 back-off/variation/accessory sets.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How I utilize body part splits for maximum muscle hypertrophy (versus upper lowe, 2020-01; The hypertrophy series： programming strength work to bolster tonnage quality & p, 2020-11; How to structure a Gentleman split (volume & intensity), 2020-12; Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09)

VOL-42 · Most tonnage at moderate reps; offset heavy and volume work

  • Statement: The bulk of tonnage sits at 4-12 reps, and "volume work" means above 6 reps. When the strength set is heaviest, the following volume work should be lightest, offsetting tonnage swings with variations.
  • Numbers: 4x6-10 or 4x8-12 beats 4x5; evolving sets swing tonnage hugely (1x4 vs 8-6-4).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11; Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10; How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09)

VOL-43 · Count indirect volume

  • Statement: Compounds spread tonnage across several muscles, so count it: bench is triceps and front-delt volume, and a 300 lb squat isn't 300 lb of quad tonnage. Shared structures such as the lower back cap how much you can send through them.
  • Numbers: Send part of back volume through legless moves (~300/700 of 1000 lb).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： diffuse vs targeted tonnage, 2020-07; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; Level up your back, 2022-02; Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02)

VOL-44 · Isolation vs compound share

  • Statement: He has given both an isolation-heavy and a compound-heavy ratio.
  • Numbers: About 2:1 isolation:compound per muscle (2023); compounds should be the program's bulk (2024).
  • Scope: Program design.
  • Confidence: low — ~2 videos, 2023→2024
  • Status: contradicted — 2023 isolation 2:1 vs 2024 compounds as the bulk.
  • Sources: (Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12; Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02)

Body-part volume

Per-muscle detail lives in ch. 6; these are the volume rules he states in general terms.

VOL-45 · Upper back is a volume black hole

  • Statement: The upper back takes huge volume and recovers fast, so it gets the most sets, as long as the lower back isn't taxed; most people undertrain it.
  • Numbers: Weekly caps rise by stage: 12 → 20 → 12-24 → 14-28 (covers 99.9% of lifters); arms would not tolerate 20. Naturals start with 1-2 pulls per session (one vertical, one horizontal) at ~4 sets each.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~13 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06; Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? (Analyzing Chris Bumstead's Workout w/ , 2022-10; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09)

VOL-46 · Legs respond to minimal, hard volume

  • Statement: Legs grow from intensity and progression, not "a million sets": one quad movement plus one hinge or knee-flexion movement at about 3 hard sets each.
  • Numbers: 2022: 6-7 heavy knee-flexion sets/wk; 2023: ~9 quad + 8 posterior hard sets/wk is enough, 18-24 total at 3x/wk is plenty; 2024: 6 quad + 6 posterior sets/wk for himself.
  • Scope: Naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 at least 11-12 heavy squat sets per squat day plus giant-set finishers; 2022-24 minimal hard sets.
  • Sources: (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01; The PERFECT Hybrid Calisthenics Program (Feat Bald Omni Man), 2023-01; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

VOL-47 · Chest grows on modest volume, but presses need enough

  • Statement: Chest grows on modest weekly volume and about three exercises is the session limit; still, very low pressing volume (3x5 bench) is too little.
  • Numbers: ~6-8 sets/wk; he does 8-12/wk (2023) then 6/wk (2024); four horizontal presses in a session exceed most people's weekly need; 3x5 bench (15 reps) too little, ≥60 working bench reps wanted (2020).
  • Scope: All trainees; add push-ups or dips, which are easier to recover from.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04; 4 days Body parts split program review, 2020-10; The OPTIMAL 6D/WEEK Hypertrophy Program by Mike Israetel Review, 2022-09; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09)

VOL-48 · Vertical presses and shoulders tolerate more

  • Statement: Vertical pressing tolerates up to double the horizontal press sets; shoulders get 1-2 isolations plus 1-2 vertical presses per day, and more after a press plus one isolation is junk.
  • Numbers: Shoulders 12-20 sets/wk total, 6-12 isolation; vertical press 6-8/wk, up to 12-16 if you recover fast; he runs 9-12 shoulder sets vs 6 chest (2024).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (FREE 4 days Body Parts split for Intermediates, 2020-06; Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10; Superman Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Henry Cavill Physique Workout), 2023-02; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09)

VOL-49 · Arms are main lifts, not accessories

  • Statement: Treat arms as main lifts with 2-4 hard sets per muscle per session; bro-style 20 sets/wk per arm muscle is junk. If ~12 weekly arm sets don't grow arms, check progression first, then change exercises or even lower volume.
  • Numbers: ~9 biceps + 9 triceps sets/wk himself (2024); 2 hard biceps sets/wk won't grow trained arms.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Blood and Guts program review, 2020-10; Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01; Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique, 2022-11; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

VOL-50 · Small muscles: less per session, recover fast

  • Statement: Small muscles take fewer sets per session but recover quickly; feed them through varied angles, frequency and supersets.
  • Numbers: See the small-muscle reference table at the end of this part.
  • Scope: Rear delts, traps, forearms, neck, abs, calves.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： big vs small muscle groups, 2020-07; I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08; Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05)

Set structures

VOL-51 · Back-off sets: two or three after the work sets

  • Statement: After 1-3 strength sets, usually 2-3 back-off sets of the same pattern with a modest drop. After a 3x3, a heavy 3x8-12 back-off on the same lift is too much, so use a variation.
  • Numbers: 2-3 (sometimes 3-4) back-offs, never 10; after 275 lb work sets go to ~245, not 185 (2024).
  • Scope: Compounds.
  • Confidence: medium — ~12 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 back-offs are "a must… free tonnage"; 2023 B tier, better as a variation; 2024 he skips them on dips and non-priority squats.
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： utilizing back-off sets to accumulate quality tonnage, 2020-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04)

VOL-52 · Evolving sets: keep the span narrow

  • Statement: When the number of sets evolves, keep the span to 2-4 sets; it is an advanced tool because swinging sets changes volume far more than swinging reps.
  • Numbers: 2-4 sets (2-5 or 2-6 max, never 1-8); 3-6 bench sets "is already a big range".
  • Scope: Advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09; How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09)

VOL-53 · Match total reps when changing schemes

  • Statement: When swapping set/rep schemes keep total reps similar, or know why you are changing volume.
  • Numbers: 5x5 = 25 ≈ 3x8; 4x4 = 16 ≈ 3x5; replace 5x5 with 5x3-6 or 4x4-7.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to modify any training program, 2021-03; Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06; The problem with 5x5/3x5, 2020-06)

VOL-54 · Finishers and pyramids drift into junk

  • Statement: Pyramids and drop-set finishers drift toward junk; weight progression builds quality tonnage. A finisher only makes sense after real work has used up the muscle.
  • Numbers: Max 2-3 finishers per session (2021); drop sets C tier, finishers D tier (2023).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
  • Status: changed — 2021 finishers are fine and build work capacity; 2023 "textbook junk volume" or active recovery at best.
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11)

VOL-55 · Nucleus overload: a light complement, later rated minor

  • Statement: Nucleus overload (NO) is frequent, high-volume, very light work kept easy enough to repeat, used to complement strength work for the same muscle, never to replace it. It is the one exception to intensity windows.
  • Numbers: ~15-30% intensity, 4-25 reps (he corrected an earlier 40-60), ≥5 reps left; months (4-5) to show; spread through other days as supersets, never on the day the muscle gets hard sets; traps NO 2-4x/wk.
  • Scope: Lats, shoulders, abs, forearms, traps.
  • Confidence: medium — ~20 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: changed — 2020-22 an advocated accessory method for most body parts; 2023 D tier, ~1-2% of results. Also contradicted on whether NO reaches failure.
  • Sources: (Nucleus overload guide (part. 1)： What it is & how to implement it, 2020-05; Nucleus overload guide (part. 4)： Reps, sets and frequency schemes, 2020-10; ☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11)

Session length

VOL-56 · Train until the day's stimulus is done, then leave

  • Statement: There is no fixed time cap: train as long as the day's stimulus takes, don't drag sessions into junk, and cram the necessary work into the least time.
  • Numbers: 2021: 1h15 target, 10 saved minutes ≈ 2 extra quality sets; a 25-35 min session is fine if you progress; 2024: 45-60 min of hard sets exhausts most people.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 advanced lifters must lengthen sessions and naturals "cannot just train an hour a day"; 2021 as short as possible; 2024 don't train to a clock.
  • Sources: (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01; The hypertrophy series： determining optimal training durations, 2020-06; Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01)

VOL-57 · Normal sessions run 60-90 minutes

  • Statement: About 60-90 min is a normal session and 90 min is "pushing it"; if you're done after 60 min of a planned 90, cut the day. Saying training past 1.5 h is pointless is a myth.
  • Numbers: A program that takes 2 h on paper takes ~30 min more in the gym; giant sets compress sessions to 60-70 min; novices: 3 x 1 h beats 2 x 2 h; ~80% of results come from the first 60-70% of a program (2022).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06; The hypertrophy series： modulating session timeframe to control volume/intensity, 2020-08; Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10; Better than 90% of bodybuilding routines： 4 HORSEMEN by Brian Alsruhe, 2021-10)

VOL-58 · His own session lengths

  • Statement: His own sessions went from multi-hour days toward fewer sets per session.
  • Numbers: 2020: 2-3 h, 6 days/wk (12-15 h/wk, 3 h arm days); 2023: ~2 h, 6 days (1.5-2 h excluding warm-up); 2024: commercial-gym days ≈ 24 sets in under 2 h.
  • Scope: Him (descriptive).
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — longer sessions in 2020, fewer sets by 2024.
  • Sources: (How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02; Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

Frequency as a variable

Frequency is how he fits volume in: the same weekly sets work better spread over several sessions.

FRQ-01 · Frequency is the pillar naturals ignore most

  • Statement: Frequency is one of the three pillars with volume and intensity and the most ignored, so for naturals it matters most; when sets happen comes before how many.
  • Numbers: Frequency rated S tier (2023).
  • Scope: Naturals; a coach who says "do 12 sets whenever" doesn't understand programming.
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： the inevitability of frequency control for optimal progr, 2021-01; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11)

FRQ-02 · Spread weekly sets over several sessions

  • Statement: The same weekly sets give better results spread out: lumping them forces lighter loads and adds cardio limits and junk, while spreading allows heavier loads, more tonnage and better recovery. Frequency exists to fit volume in.
  • Numbers: 3x3 sets beat 9 in one session; 5+5+5 beats 15 on Monday; 4 back sets 3x/wk beat 10 once; 12 back sets in one day after deadlifts is wasted; 15 sets in one day might need ~100 h of recovery.
  • Scope: All trainees beyond novice; front-loading early in the week is fine unless it turns into junk.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; Level up your back, 2022-02; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

FRQ-03 · Once a week is suboptimal unless you are coasting

  • Statement: Training a muscle once a week is always suboptimal for a natural unless you are deliberately coasting on it; it leaves the muscle idle most of the week and brings soreness and poor work capacity.
  • Numbers: Once-a-week all-out = 4 sessions a month, and a lifter training 4x/week beats you on tonnage.
  • Scope: Naturals. Exceptions he admits: a friend's legs growing on 1x/week (2023) and legs 1x/week while fixing an upper-body weakness (2024).
  • Confidence: high — ~11 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is every muscle you want to grow trained at least twice a week?
  • Sources: (The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11; The hypertrophy series： the inevitability of frequency control for optimal progr, 2021-01; Minimalist training bad, 2021-06; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-04 · Frequency is a recovery schedule

  • Statement: There is no universally optimal frequency, only one that matches the work done to its recovery time; retrain a muscle once it is ready, because leaving it dormant leads to stagnation.
  • Numbers: No hard 72 h rule; 24 or 48 h works if volume and intensity are managed.
  • Scope: All trainees; paper math fails because recovery fluctuates.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2021→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The Best/Worst of Reddit Fitness - The Ten Commandments of Lifting, 2021-10; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02; Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12)

FRQ-05 · Choose frequency first, then template and sets per day

  • Statement: Pick frequency first; templates mostly dictate frequency and grouping, and per-session numbers must scale to the number of days.
  • Numbers: A rep range that works on a 6-day PPL fails on a 3-day one.
  • Scope: Program design.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to program evolving rep ranges, 2020-07; PPL template review, 2020-08; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06)

FRQ-06 · Higher frequency, less per session

  • Statement: The more often you train a muscle, the less volume (and the shorter the session) each time; low frequency needs high volume and intensity per session.
  • Numbers: 48 h recovery pairs with 2-4 sets per muscle per session, 72 h with 4-8; 2-3 chest sets per session are plenty at 2-3x/week.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06)

FRQ-07 · Take only part of the recovery "pot" each session

  • Statement: Recovery is a fixed-size tub: fill it with quality tonnage as often as possible, taking only part of it per session; training once a week doesn't make the tub bigger.
  • Numbers: Take ~30-40% per session; if legs recover in 2 days, train them again after 2 days.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05; The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11; The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02; Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02)

FRQ-08 · Every pattern weekly, compounds 2-3x a week

  • Statement: Technique and strength depend on frequency: every movement pattern should return at least once a week, and compounds should be practised 2-3x a week. Once a lift is automatic, heavy-work frequency can drop.
  • Numbers: A lift done every 15-30 days is relearned each time; a pattern left for a month is "catastrophic".
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Body parts split： bro split vs Gentleman Split, 2020-09; Rotating lifts： What it should & shouldn't be, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： pairing neurological adaptation and muscle gains, 2021-02; Who can afford to only squat and deadlift once a week?, 2020-03)

FRQ-09 · Soreness means frequency is too low

  • Statement: Soreness signals too little frequency, not growth; with proper frequency it disappears.
  • Numbers: Still sore after 6 months on the same program = frequency too low; he hadn't been sore in 2 years while progressing (2021).
  • Scope: All trainees beyond the first months.
  • Confidence: high — ~4 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The issue with HIT (the intensity meme), 2020-11; Good leg day vs Bad leg day, 2021-09; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-10 · Never sacrifice intensity for frequency

  • Statement: Frequency should not cost per-set intensity; trading frequency for intensity is fine, and stronger lifters need longer recovery windows.
  • Numbers: 2021-22 examples: 3x/wk at 100% may do better as 5x at 85%; calves trained lightly 40 times a year beat 15 hard sessions; squatting 2x/wk for 5 years beats 5x/wk for 1 year.
  • Scope: All trainees; especially strong, advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: changed — 2021-22 frequency and consistency beat intensity bursts; 2023 stronger lifters need longer windows; 2024 "never sacrifice intensity for frequency", and training less often let him train harder with unchanged gains.
  • Sources: (ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you train like a Baki character? A Grappler Baki Training G, 2021-06; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; The Hardworking Lifter who BROKE the Natty Limit (Alex Leonidas), 2023-05; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-11 · Frequency has limits as a progression tool

  • Statement: Frequency is capped by the days in a week, so it can't drive progress through the intermediate and advanced stages; raising frequency on a stalled isolation keeps the muscle fatigued. Hitting a muscle more than 2-3x/week is earned.
  • Numbers: Only isolations are "spammable" at 2-4x/week; compounds near failure are not.
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced.
  • Confidence: low — 1 video, 2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12; Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12; Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12; Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12)

FRQ-12 · Small muscles more often, big muscles harder with more rest

  • Statement: Small muscles burn out fast in a session but recover fast, so train them more often with less per session; the opposite belief is "backwards".
  • Numbers: Every 2 days is a good default even for small muscles.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： big vs small muscle groups, 2020-07; Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; How to start training a neglected body part, 2020-10; 5 Reasons why Bro Splits are Garbage, 2021-02)

FRQ-13 · Frequency also exists inside the session

  • Statement: Intra-session frequency (how sets follow each other, rest and session length) matters too; alternating posterior-chain and quad work lets muscles recover between sets and allows more tonnage.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Session design.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： modulating session timeframe to control volume/intensity, 2020-08; Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08; Pull Push Legs 6 days Program Review, 2020-05)

Spacing between sessions for the same muscle

FRQ-14 · At least ~48 hours between hard sessions for a muscle

  • Statement: ~48 h is the default and minimum between hard sessions for the same muscle; don't hit a muscle hard two days in a row.
  • Numbers: 48 h ("a bare minimum", 2024); benching two days in a row is bad even with different variations.
  • Scope: All trainees; light hits are treated separately (FRQ-15).
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — he also calls two days in a row and 90/80/70% Mon-Wed valid (2020, 2022); likely hard vs light hits, not always stated.
  • Check: Are hard sessions for the same muscle at least 48 h apart?
  • Sources: (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12)

FRQ-15 · Light back-to-back hits are allowed

  • Statement: Full recovery matters for peak performance, not for hypertrophy, so lighter hits on consecutive days are fine.
  • Numbers: A light blood-flow movement 24 h after a heavy day (advanced); 90/80/70% Mon-Wed then rest until Saturday; a few pull-ups daily.
  • Scope: Mainly advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07; 5 Ways to shock the muscle (GONE WRONG), 2020-07; The hypertrophy series： muscular vs cardiovascular fatigue, 2020-04; Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02)

FRQ-16 · Match the recovery interval to the template

  • Statement: Each template implies a recovery interval for each muscle.
  • Numbers: 24 h = light daily full body; 48 h = upper/lower; 72 h = PPL; full body 3x/wk gives 48-72 h; arms 48-72 h, waiting longer gains nothing.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; Pull Push Legs 6 days Program Review, 2020-05; The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02; 5 Reasons why Bro Splits are Garbage, 2021-02)

FRQ-17 · Late view: longer gaps for strong lifters

  • Statement: By late 2024 he spaces sessions further apart.
  • Numbers: Upper days 72-90 h apart (2-3 days); legs 72-96 h.
  • Scope: Strong, advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~2 videos, 2024
  • Status: changed — earlier default was every ~48 h for upper and legs (FRQ-14, FRQ-19).
  • Sources: (So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-18 · The last hard session sets the next one

  • Statement: Check whether the muscle is back to baseline before retraining it; if a moderate session leaves days of unused rest, move the next one earlier, and if you can't match volume next time, you needed more rest.
  • Numbers: After a heavy Monday squat, do Wednesday's quad accessories without pushing them.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： strength baseline control for recovery & gains, 2020-05; How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12)

Frequency by muscle and lift

FRQ-19 · Legs about every 48 hours, later twice a week

  • Statement: Legs grow from volume spread out, not a weekly crushing day: a heavy knee flexion or hip hinge about every 2 days, with two leg days a week as the minimum beyond novices.
  • Numbers: ~3x/wk with 3-4 sets for quads or hamstrings per session (2024-05); 2x/wk with 72-96 h between sessions (2024-12), because 3x becomes unrecoverable at ~400s squat / ~500s RDL.
  • Scope: Naturals beyond novice; the lower back is usually what stops people training legs that often.
  • Confidence: high — ~20 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-2024-05 every 48 h / 3x a week; 2024-12 2x a week for strong advanced lifters.
  • Check: Are legs trained at least twice a week?
  • Sources: (How I utilize body part splits for maximum muscle hypertrophy (versus upper lowe, 2020-01; This is Peak Bulk (Hypertrophy Log #6), 2024-05; How the King of Zoomers Trains to Look like a Greek God (Alex Eubank Program Rev, 2022-12; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-20 · Upper body about three times a week

  • Statement: Upper-body muscles are numerous, less taxing and recover fast, so train them about every 2 days; chest does better 2-3x a week with fewer, more precise sets than on one chest day.
  • Numbers: Upper ~3x/wk; chest 2-3x/wk with 2-3 sets per session; 2024: forearms 3-4x, biceps and chest 2-3x weekly.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02; Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03; Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12)

FRQ-21 · Horizontal press at least twice, bench under three times

  • Statement: Bench once a week doesn't progress the bench, but raw bench 3+ times a week brings shoulder overuse; press horizontally at least twice and use push-ups, flies or close-grip for extra frequency.
  • Numbers: ≥2x/wk horizontal pressing; bench <3x/wk; 3x/wk as in novice programs is too much; at 5x/wk use shoulder-sparing variations.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1), 2020-10; Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08)

FRQ-22 · Vertical pressing about twice a week

  • Statement: Vertical pressing ~2x a week is needed for big shoulders; 3x OHP is overcorrection and once a week at 5x5 is too little. Do both a vertical and a horizontal press on each press day.
  • Numbers: 2x/wk; 2023: the vertical pattern 2-3x/wk, not the same lift.
  • Scope: Lifters wanting big shoulders.
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (3 days PPL program review, 2020-06; Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08; 4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11; We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05)

FRQ-23 · Squat twice a week long term

  • Statement: Once a week is not enough, 2x a week is the long-term sweet spot and 3x is hard to sustain; daily squatting works but builds strength more than size.
  • Numbers: 2x/wk; novices 1-2x; heavy squats 4x/wk was more than he could handle.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~9 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (6 days Body parts split program review, 2020-08; 7 days split program review (Rubgy focus), 2020-07; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03; Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03)

FRQ-24 · Deadlift rarely, the hinge pattern more often

  • Statement: The conventional deadlift needs the least frequency of the big lifts (low frequency, high intensity, moderate volume), while the hinge pattern can return every 2-3 days with variations.
  • Numbers: Deadlift every 7-10 days, 1x4-6 is excellent; 2024: max 1-2x/wk after 2+ years of pushing it. Hinge pattern every 2-3 days; he hinged heavy every 2 days (2022).
  • Scope: All trainees; he claims pulling heavy several times a week "just means you're still weak".
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — 2020 "only a few times a month" alongside heavy deadlifts 2x/week, and heavy hinging every 2 days in 2022; partly deadlift vs hinge variations.

FRQ-25 · Upper back: most frequency-tolerant, spread over days

  • Statement: The upper back tolerates training nearly every day with varied angles and intensities; train back at least 3x a week, add back movements to the split "as Lego blocks", and never put all back volume on one day.
  • Numbers: ≥3x/wk; per session ≤3 exercises / ~10 sets; e.g. 6 back exercises as 2/2/2 over Mon/Wed/Sat; ~6 sets per day instead of 30 once; no horizontal pull on consecutive days.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~16 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — 2022/2024 back can be trained every day if parts rotate; 2023 "never train back every day".
  • Check: Is back work spread over at least three days with no more than ~3 back exercises in any one session?
  • Sources: (My philosophy regarding upper back training (part. 1), 2020-02; Does Mr. Olympia know how to train BACK? (Analyzing Chris Bumstead's Workout w/ , 2022-10; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

FRQ-26 · Pull-ups can be done very often

  • Statement: Pull-ups are low-impact and the upper back recovers fast, so they can be done daily, even to failure; grease-the-groove works for them as an exception.
  • Numbers: His 2020 daily pull-ups: 100-120 reps on high days, 30-40 on low days; 40-60 weighted daily (2021). 2023: 1-2x/wk with grip rotation is enough to progress; 2024: calisthenics lifters ≥2x/wk.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-21 daily; 2023-24 1-2x a week is enough.
  • Sources: (Weak point Wednesday： Lats (how I will grow mine), 2020-02; How to do pull-ups to maximize muscle growth and minimize injury risks, 2021-09; We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

FRQ-27 · Bring in a neglected muscle by frequency first

  • Statement: For a neglected or small muscle, raise frequency (1x → 2x → 3x a week) before adding sets per session.
  • Numbers: Rear delts: 1x3 sets → 2x3 → 2x4 → 3x4 per week; early on 3 sets can leave them sore for 3 days.
  • Scope: Lagging or newly trained muscles.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to start training a neglected body part, 2020-10; Weak point Wednesday： Rear delts, 2020-07; Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; 3 steps to follow for Bigger Arms, 2021-02)

FRQ-28 · Arms: biceps on every upper day

  • Statement: Arm intensity is fixed at failure and per-session volume is limited, so arm growth comes from frequency; put biceps work on every upper day, and isolations need more frequency than the compounds they accompany.
  • Numbers: Advanced: biceps and triceps every 2 days or more, with only 6-15 weekly sets.
  • Scope: Mainly intermediate and advanced lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~5 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The hypertrophy series： big vs small muscle groups, 2020-07; Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01; Massive Arms Exercises： Build Boulder Biceps, 2022-08)

FRQ-29 · Bodyweight work often, spread through other days

  • Statement: Bodyweight and calisthenics movements, abs and nucleus-overload work are cheap to recover from, so do them often and spread them through other days instead of giving them a day of their own.
  • Numbers: Bodyweight movements 4-5x/wk; a dedicated ab day is a "monumental waste".
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current

Days per week

FRQ-30 · Four days a week is the sustainable sweet spot

  • Statement: 4 training days a week is his favourite and sustainable for life; 3 is fine, and intermediates need at least 3.
  • Numbers: 4 ideal (4-5 range, 2020); 3 or 6 days are "sub-extreme" (2021); 3 days "perfectly fine" (2024).
  • Scope: Most lifters.
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to program a Gentleman split, 2020-10; FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1), 2020-10; Fullbody template review, 2021-01; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

FRQ-31 · Advanced means more sessions

  • Statement: Advancing means more sessions per year, not just more sets.
  • Numbers: Intermediate 3 sessions/wk (12/month, 140-150/yr); advanced every other day (~4/wk, 15/month, ~180/yr), about 30 extra sessions a year.
  • Scope: Intermediate → advanced; a regular extra rest day puts you back on the intermediate program.
  • Confidence: medium — 1 video, 2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout), 2022-10; Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout), 2022-10)

FRQ-32 · Add days by spreading existing work

  • Statement: Start with 3-4 days and expand; add a day by spreading existing tonnage, not by piling on more, and never jump from 3 to 6 days at the same per-day volume.

  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2022

FRQ-33 · Long days → add a day; thin days → compress

  • Statement: If sessions run too long, add a day; if days are thin or redundant, compress them.
  • Numbers: Taking 10-15% from each of 3 overloaded days can create a 4th shorter day; 5 → 4 or 3 when compressing.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2021→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Fullbody template review, 2021-01; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10)

FRQ-34 · Who six days a week suits

  • Statement: Six days suits fast-recovering novices, advanced lifters who need frequency to accumulate volume, and rare volume responders with poor leverages.
  • Numbers: White-collar workers do well on 4-6 days; 6 days on top of MMA taxes recovery.
  • Scope: As stated.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to program a Gentleman split, 2020-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #5, 2021-01; Scheduling your training for White Collar workers, 2021-02; 6 days Upper Body dominant split review (MMA focus), 2020-06)

FRQ-35 · Busy lifters: two or three full-body days

  • Statement: Busy or sleep-deprived lifters don't need high frequency: 2-3 full-body days, or upper/lower twice with isolation in short gaps. A physique built on 5 days a week can be maintained on 2.
  • Numbers: 30 min = 4-5 hard sets; 2 h/week is already a lot; 10-15 min gaps for isolation; skip training on 16-hour shift days.
  • Scope: Busy, shift-working or sleep-deprived lifters.

FRQ-36 · Daily training is possible but not advised

  • Statement: Training every day works if volume and intensity are reduced and the split never builds enough fatigue to need a day off, but he doesn't advise it for others; for depressed lifters, daily training for structure can come before gains.

Split templates

FRQ-37 · The bro split is the worst template for naturals

  • Statement: One muscle per day once a week gives too little frequency and too much per-session volume, which fills sessions with junk; the fix is to hit each muscle twice a week.
  • Numbers: 2024 example: six back exercises for 25 sets, where 20% of the work gives ~95% of the gains.
  • Scope: Naturals. In his opinion enhanced lifters can recover from it, and would still grow more with more frequency.
  • Confidence: high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current

FRQ-38 · The gentleman split is his favourite

  • Statement: His preferred template is an upper/lower skeleton whose days are built around synergistic muscle groups and a main compound, with flexible boundaries.
  • Numbers: 4-5 days: 2 upper, 2 lower, optional arm day.
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced bodybuilders.
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: changed — terminology: in 2020 he praised a well-built "body-part split" as the best natural template; from 2021 that label means one-muscle-per-day splits and he condemns it, while the same idea lives on as the gentleman split.
  • Sources: (Body parts split： bro split vs Gentleman Split, 2020-09; How to program a Gentleman split, 2020-10; Analyzing the Rock's ＂Black Adam＂ training program, 2021-03; Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09)

FRQ-39 · Upper/lower is the most convenient skeleton

  • Statement: Upper/lower saves warm-up time, groups synergistic muscles and manages fatigue well, so it is the base for most templates; its weakness is poor upper-back frequency, and minimal upper/lower days waste it.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees; don't get stuck in a plain 2-upper/2-lower.

FRQ-40 · Run PPL as pull-push-legs

  • Statement: Never run push-pull-legs: pull day's hinges and rows fatigue the legs and lower back right before squats. Use pull-push-legs (or legs-push-pull) or put a rest day between pull and legs.
  • Numbers: Pull-push-legs-pull-push-legs keeps pull and leg days as far apart as possible (2023).
  • Scope: PPL users.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current

FRQ-41 · PPL is a good split

  • Statement: PPL is a very good split with an unwarranted bad reputation; run it about 6x a week (each muscle 2x) or 3x a week, and for 4-5 days just cut a day.
  • Numbers: PPL-rest-repeat allows more intensity than PPLPPL-rest.
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: medium — ~7 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020 standard PPL was lower-body biased and the worst order (push days should include pulling); 2023-24 a very good split in pull-push-legs order.
  • Sources: (Coolcicada 6 Days PPL Program review, 2020-05; The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11; The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

FRQ-42 · Full body works best three times a week

  • Statement: Full body is best at 3x a week with ~48 h between sessions; it is the hardest template to program because compounds get crammed and small muscles neglected, so skew it to priorities and rotate variations.
  • Numbers: Mon/Wed/Fri; 2x is fine for busy people but thin for intermediates; 4x is the upper limit; 6x unrecoverable except for novices; never back-to-back days.
  • Scope: Full-body users.
  • Confidence: medium — ~10 videos, 2020→2024

Sequencing days through the week

FRQ-57 · Separate heavy squats and heavy deadlifts

  • Statement: Never do heavy squats and heavy deadlifts on the same day or on consecutive days; if they share a day, make one heavy and the other a lighter variation in a higher rep range, squat first.
  • Numbers: E.g. squat + stiff-leg deadlift, or deadlift + pause squat; heavy hinge on the back day, heavy knee flexion on leg day (2021).
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~13 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are heavy squats and heavy deadlifts kept off the same day and off consecutive days?

FRQ-58 · One heavy lower pattern opens each lower day

  • Statement: Each lower day opens with one heavy knee flexion or hip hinge; the next heavy-ish movement is the other pattern, and which one leads alternates between days.

FRQ-59 · Alternate taxing and easy days

FRQ-60 · Heaviest lower day right before the rest day

  • Statement: Start the week with an upper day and put the heaviest lower or highest-tonnage day right before the rest day or weekend, so rest follows the sessions that drain the most.

Arm days

FRQ-66 · An arm day is the least taxing day

Session structure

FRQ-69 · Pyramid of priority within a session

  • Statement: Open with the most demanding, most important lift (heavy low-rep strength work while fresh), then lighter compounds, then isolation; if time runs short, cut from the bottom, never the top.

Rest between sets

Rest only as long as the next set needs; heavy strength work gets full rest as straight sets, and nearly everything else is supersetted.

RST-01 · Rest about 2-3 minutes, never more than 5

  • Statement: Rest as little as possible while staying performant; more than 5 min is overkill. He doesn't time rests and goes roughly by feel.
  • Numbers: 2020: 3-5 min strength, 1-2 min straight-set accessories, 3-4 min between heavy low-rep evolving sets; 2021: 2-3 min for strength, 1.5-3 up to 5; 2023: "2 or 3 is fine as long as you recover"; 2024: ~3 min by feel or a song.
  • Scope: All trainees; heavy Bulgarian split squats: he sits 3 min.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — mild drift from 3-5 min for strength sets (2020) to 2-3 min by feel (2021-24).
  • Check: Do straight sets get roughly 2-3 minutes of rest (not under ~90 s, not over ~5 min)?
  • Sources: (AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04; Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06; Hypertrophy Q&A #6, 2021-03; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11)

RST-02 · Rest so the muscle returns to baseline

  • Statement: The aim of rest is for the muscle to be back to baseline for the next set; too-short rests wreck performance and turn training into cardio.
  • Numbers: 20 s between curl sets gives a third of the reps; 15 s with a challenging weight isn't enough; 60-90 s improves conditioning but hurts performance; 100 reps is like 10x10 with no rest.
  • Scope: All trainees; rest-pause is the deliberate exception (INT-56).
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Transcendent training review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02; Hypertrophy Q&A #6, 2021-03; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; Another 𝐻𝒪𝑅𝑅𝐼𝐵𝐿𝐸 Bodybuilding Program (HYPERMASS by Noel, 2022-06)

RST-03 · Same-muscle exercises still need full rest

  • Statement: Between two exercises for the same muscle, rest 2-3 min; performance matters for biceps as much as for quads.
  • Numbers: 2-3 min.
  • Scope: All trainees; supersets of different muscles are fine.
  • Confidence: medium — 1 video, 2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02)

  • Statement: Low-rep sets run as straight sets with long rests; higher-rep sets can use rest-pause and shorter rests.

Supersets and giant sets

RST-06 · Don't superset the opening strength work

  • Statement: Heavy opening lifts (squat, deadlift, bench, hinges, heavy knee flexion, weighted chins) run as straight sets with full rest to keep focus and energy; at most pair them with small non-bracing work (neck, abs, curls, rear delts).
  • Numbers: 2024: bench and pull-ups standalone, the rest supersetted, ~1h10 session. Overhead press paired with a pull is an exception.

RST-07 · Never superset two movements for the same muscle

  • Statement: Pairing two lifts for the same muscle is pre-fatigue or a finisher, a different tool, and a last resort otherwise.
  • Numbers: No face pulls with reverse flies, dips with shoulder press, OHP with lateral raises, or two biceps movements back to back.

  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024

RST-08 · Leg exercises don't chain into each other

Rest and session time

RST-19 · Most gym time is rest; supersets reclaim it

  • Statement: If the same work fits in 1 h with supersets as in 2 h, the 2 h was lazy rest; know how long your program takes, because cramming 90 min into 60 raises intensity non-optimally.

4. Progression, fatigue & recovery

This chapter covers how a lift, a program and a lifter move forward over months and years (progression), how he manages the fatigue that training creates without deload weeks (fatigue, deloads, breaks), and what happens outside the gym (sleep and recovery). His stance: progressive overload is mandatory for naturals, best done through evolving rep ranges with small, steady, never-stopping progress and stable tonnage. He rejects scheduled deloads, blocks and peaking for bodybuilders and builds fatigue management into every week instead. Sleep and passive rest are the base of recovery; soreness and "feel" are poor guides.

Why progression matters

He treats rising tonnage as the target and getting stronger as the main way to raise it. Rep ranges and intensity windows themselves are in ch. 3.

PRG-01 · Progressive overload is non-negotiable

  • Statement: Without progressive overload there is no muscle gain; something has to go up for the muscles to go up, and a coach who never mentions it is a "hack".
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees, especially naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the program have a defined way for load, reps or sets to rise over time?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06; The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01)

Overload levers and their order

Load, reps, sets and frequency are all overload, but he insists the bar weight never leaves the mix.

PRG-11 · Overload has many modes

  • Statement: Overload can come from load, reps, sets, frequency, rest, technique/variation or range of motion; weight on the bar is just "the tip of the iceberg", and more sets and reps at the same weight are valid overload.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Should bodybuilders care about strength?, 2020-02; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08; Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09)

PRG-12 · Bar weight must stay in the mix

  • Statement: Weight on the bar is the simplest, most reliable and easiest lever to log and must stay in the mix, but load-only progression is "designed to fail" because the ability to add weight outpaces recovery (the "Milo paradox").
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All trainees past the novice stage.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-21: bar weight is the simplest and best method; 2022: weight is the "tip of the iceberg", most natural gains come from accumulated volume; 2024: his own bar-weight obsession caused progression anxiety, yet you must still get stronger.
  • Check: Does the program raise load as well as reps or sets, without relying on load alone?
  • Sources: (The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06; The hypertrophy series： controlling volume & intensity to promote progression, 2020-05; No one understands progressive overload, 2022-03; Escape Intermediate Hell (Path to Exceptional Physique), 2023-10)

  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023

  • Numbers: Superset isolation volume grows 2 → 3-4 sets, spreads to other days, only then add weight.

Evolving rep ranges (double progression)

His main tool: each lift gets a fixed range, reps climb week to week, and weight goes up when the first set reaches the ceiling. Ch. 3 (INT-46) covers why declining reps across sets matter for intensity.

PRG-20 · Evolving rep ranges are the core method

  • Statement: Give each lift a fixed rep range, start near the bottom, add reps weekly, add weight at the top and stay in the same range. He calls it the best way to progress.
  • Numbers: 6-10 example: 6,5 → … → 10,9,8 → jump; ~90-95% of his lifts (2020); "every one of his programs" (2024).
  • Scope: All lifts past the novice stage (see PRG-36 for novices).
  • Confidence: high — ~15 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does each lift have a rep range with a rule for when to add weight?
  • Sources: (Pull Push Legs 6 days Program Review, 2020-05; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06; We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

PRG-21 · Add weight when the first set hits the ceiling

  • Statement: Only the first (top) set needs to reach the top of the range, with the others close; waiting for every set to hit the top turns the range back into a static scheme.
  • Numbers: 6-10×4: 10-10-10-10 = should have jumped long ago, 10-9-8-7 = ready; 5-10: 8-7-7-5 → 9-8-7-6 → 10 → +5 lb.
  • Scope: All lifts on evolving ranges.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — Jan 2020: on 4×12, go up only if all four sets of 12 are comfortable; from Aug 2020: waiting for all sets makes ranges static; 2024: one set at the top is enough.
  • Check: Is weight added once the first set reaches the top of the range, not only when every set does?
  • Sources: (Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01; When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08; When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

PRG-22 · Readiness depends on the range

  • Statement: On a heavy low range less is needed to add weight; you needn't max every set.
  • Numbers: On 3-5, 5,4 is enough; on an 8-12 isolation, 11,10; 5-4 or 5-4-3 can be enough.
  • Scope: All lifts on evolving ranges.
  • Confidence: medium — 2 videos, 2021→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06)

  • Scope: All working sets.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08; Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09)

Range width

PRG-37 · Ranges that are too narrow fail

  • Statement: Narrow ranges leave no room for set evolution and drift toward sandbagged 5x5; keep at least 4 reps between floor and ceiling.
  • Numbers: Too narrow: 5-6, 6-8, 8-10 ×4 sets, 10-12 ×2-3 sets, 4×8-10 squat; good: 6-10, 8-12; 4-6 "a recipe for plateaus" (2025).
  • Scope: All lifts.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: changed — 2020 he often prescribed 4-6 (4×4-6 pull-ups/dips, 3×4-6 squat); 2023-25: ≥4 reps between floor and ceiling, 4-6 plateaus.

PRG-41 · Adjust the range to a plateau

  • Statement: When stalled in a range, adjust it to the exercise: widen if low reps stall, shrink if high reps stall; try widening first so tonnage climbs at the same weight.

  • Scope: Stalled lifts.

  • Status: current

PRG-42 · When testing a range, start wide

  • Statement: When beta-testing a new range, start wider and narrow it; shrinking is safer than expanding.
  • Numbers: Close-grip bench 6-12 → 6-10.
  • Scope: New lifts or programs.
