STR-48 · What carries over to the bench

  • Statement: Close-grip bench carries over and skull crushers barely do. Push-ups and ring push-ups don't build bench strength, but dips carry over a lot. A slingshot carries over little to raw benching, and using only a slingshot for 2 months could cost raw strength.
  • Numbers: he was advanced at push-ups yet benched ~145 lb the first time; a lifter hit a 4-plate bench after 6 weeks thanks to dip strength
  • Scope: bench accessories
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2024

STR-49 · Dips as the pressing strength lift

  • Statement: He believes not everyone can reach a 4-plate bench, but everyone can reach a 4-plate dip. Dips don't hurt him, so far heavier dips feel achievable.
  • Numbers: 4-plate dip for all; 5-7 plates feels achievable to him; "get to a 10-plate dip" before complaining about human limits
  • Scope: pressing strength, especially for those whose bench stalls or hurts
  • Confidence: medium — ~2 videos, 2024

STR-50 · What carries over to squat and deadlift

  • Statement: Front squats carry over to the back squat less than people think, and pause squats carry over more. Front squats barely help the conventional pull beyond upper-back rigidity. A stronger squat helps the deadlift only up to a point. The SSB box squat in deadlift stance may be the best conventional-deadlift accessory, and sumo carries to conventional better than the reverse.

Strength standards

He mostly dismisses strength standards, with a few minimum baselines he does endorse.

STR-57 · Strength standards are C-tier

  • Statement: He ignores strength standards unless you compete. They rest on unverified self-reports or powerlifter data and round plate numbers, and they ignore leverages, experience, the nervous system and timeline. They compare you to weak people and turn hypertrophy training into number-chasing. If you compete, use your sport's competition standards.

  • Scope: non-competing lifters; competitors use their sport's standards

STR-58 · Size-from-strength standards are illogical

Powerlifting, powerbuilding and strength sports

He sees powerlifting and bodybuilding as cousins that shouldn't be mixed, and he rejects powerbuilding.

STR-63 · Rejects powerbuilding

  • Statement: Heavy big-three work plus high-rep accessories usually delivers neither size nor strength. It trains one narrow kind of strength (1RMs on three lifts) that has to dominate and drains energy, and most powerbuilders never compete. The fix is to drop the 1RM training, and then you are just bodybuilding the silver/bronze-era way. He debated Dr. Milo Wolf on this.

Verifying lifts

STR-71 · Unverified lifts don't count

  • Statement: A lift with no video, witness or record doesn't count, and neither does one with bands, chains, boxes, cambered bars, above-parallel squats or unweighed plates. Weigh and load plates on camera, ideally at a sanctioned meet, and claim records only in competition.
  • Numbers: technical plates can fake ~100 lb; a deadlift-bar, deadlift-only event adds ~20-30 lb at 600
  • Scope: judging strength claims

8. Aesthetics & the gym look

This chapter covers what NH thinks a physique should look like and how to judge one: body fat, proportions, which muscles matter most to the eye, frame, measuring and the social side of looking muscular. His stance is that bodybuilding is an art of illusion aimed at beauty. Every muscle should be trained with aesthetic intent, imbalances should be deliberate, and a natural should carry a moderate body fat over a lot of muscle. He also holds that big limbs, a developed core, a thick neck and upper back count for more than stage leanness. How to train each muscle is in ch. 6; bulking and cutting are in ch. 11.

What bodybuilding is for

His starting point: looks are a legitimate goal, they come from function that you point toward appearance, and the goal is personal as long as it is chosen on purpose.

AES-01 · Bodybuilding is beauty through illusion, not mass

  • Statement: Bodybuilding pursues beauty through illusion, not a pile of mass or big measurements; flow, insertions and posing beat raw size.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters training for looks.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Natty or not (.com)： Jeff Nippard, 2020-05; Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11; Don't let this man ruin your physique, 2023-01; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12)

AES-02 · Train with aesthetic intent or get an accidental physique

  • Statement: Pure strength, big-three-only or compound-only training gives an "accidental" physique: big trunk and quads, small arms (spider, fridge, frog). A minimalist strength routine won't build an aesthetic body. His own 2020 big-three-only experiment confirmed it.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: Anyone whose goal is the look, not strength alone.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the program include work chosen for the look (isolation for arms, delts, traps and other visual muscles) rather than only the big compound lifts?
  • Sources: (＂The Big 3 is all you need to build a good physique＂, 2020-03; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; ᴅᴏᴏᴍᴇʀꜱ ᴡɪʟʟ ᴀʟᴡᴀʏꜱ ʜᴀᴠᴇ ꜱᴍᴀʟʟ ʙᴀ, 2022-12; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12)

Body fat and leanness

He wants lots of muscle at a moderate body fat. Fat, muscle size and fat pattern all change how lean someone looks.

AES-11 · Natural ideal is about 12-18% body fat

  • Statement: A natural should carry about 12-18% body fat with lots of muscle; stage condition is pointless for naturals. Old-school naturals and physique competitors 100 years ago were in this range and looked tremendous.
  • Numbers: 12-18% (old-school naturals); 10-16% (era competitors); abs look good at 10, 15 or 17%; 15% looks good; 6-8% "achievable but not reasonable"; 5% is masochism; 8% standards make men look like skeletons
  • Scope: Naturals training for looks, not stage competitors.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the target condition in the 12-18% range rather than stage leanness (5-8%)?
  • Sources: (Natty or not (.com)： Eric Bugenhagen, 2020-05; How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com), 2021-12; How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com), 2021-12; I WON! Japanese Boomers on 🅷🅰🆁🅰🅺🅸🆁🅸 Watch (Victory Q&A), 2022-09)

He frames ideals through Greek statues and the classical era, prefers a limb-heavy Herculean look for himself, and insists that neighbouring muscles grow together.

  • Statement: The Greek tradition has two branches: Apollonian (wide shoulders and lats, small waist, smaller legs, low fat) and Herculean/Farnese (thicker waist, big limbs, legs and core). He prefers the Herculean, ancient "bear mode"; the Farnese Hercules is closer to his ideal.

  • Scope: Goal-setting; he has written programs for both.
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2020→2022

He claims Blaha's "18 in" arms are really 14-15 in and that Blaha wears a belt shirtless to fake a V-taper (his unverified opinion).

9. Injuries

This chapter covers why lifters get hurt, how to read pain, how to treat tendinitis, how to program to avoid injury, and joint-by-joint rules for the back, knees, shoulders, elbows, wrists and other sites. His stance: injuries are almost never bad luck. They come from mismanaged load, fatigue, volume and repetition, so they are the lifter's responsibility. Tendinitis is treated by training around the pain, not by rest or drugs. For a natural, staying injury-free is the best way to keep growing.

Why injuries happen

He puts nearly every injury down to variables the lifter controls: load and fatigue, grinding reps, and repeating the same pattern.

INJ-01 · Injuries are preventable, not bad luck

  • Statement: Injuries come from variables you failed to control, so they are preventable; calling them bad luck is lazy and irresponsible.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters. Only things like being tackled mid-lift are truly out of your control; skipping a warm-up or slipping on ice still counts as yours.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07; Did I just snap my sh＊t up? (an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; 5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters, 2023-10)

INJ-02 · Volume/intensity mismanagement is the top cause

  • Statement: Ego, too much load and forcing the extra rep cause most injuries; together with poor positioning they account for the "vast majority". Perfect form cannot save poor volume/intensity management.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023

INJ-03 · Injury = load and fatigue exceeding tissue capacity

  • Statement: An injury is pressure exceeding what the tissue can handle, a failure to adapt to a cycle of stress. Risk depends on load and accumulated fatigue together.
  • Numbers: 50% of max is "baby weight"; 5 reps at 80% to failure every day raises risk daily as fatigue builds.
  • Scope: All lifters.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021

(an injury assessment guide & pain psychology discus, 2021-09; Injuries as a result of cyclical adaptation failure, 2020-07; No such thing as a dangerous lift (the good morning example), 2021-04)

INJ-04 · The "red zone" is where injuries happen

  • Statement: Acute injuries happen where the negative reverses into the positive; almost nobody gets hurt at lockout. Negative-first lifts (squat, bench) are the most dangerous at high intensity, and a controlled negative is injury prevention.
  • Numbers: "99%" of injuries in the red zone (2020); 95-98% (2021).
  • Scope: All lifts, especially heavy squat and bench.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current

INJ-05 · Grinding the last rep causes most injuries

  • Statement: Most gym injuries come in the last grindy reps of heavy sets. With no grinding, staying in the rep range and no last-rep chasing, risk is "almost zero". All his own past injuries came from grinding reps he wasn't capable of.
  • Numbers: Cutting 3-4 grinder squat reps gave him 3 years with no squat injury.
  • Scope: All lifters, heavy compound sets.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2022

Reading pain

He separates muscle pain from tendon/joint pain, separates "hurt" from "injured", and judges a lift by how it feels the next day.

INJ-23 · Never train through joint or tendon pain

  • Statement: Joint/tendon pain is a warning; pushing through turns minor issues into lifelong ones, and joint pain never goes away by itself. If a movement hurts, stop and re-check form; if form changes don't fix it, drop the lift, since there is "always a way around".
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters; applies to tendon/joint pain, not muscle soreness (INJ-24).
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: changed — 2020: absolute "never lift through pain; if it hurts, stop". 2021: graded pain scales where minor pain can be pushed aside (INJ-26). 2022-2025: tendon/joint pain is still a stop signal.
  • Check: Is any lift that causes joint or tendon pain modified or dropped rather than pushed through?
  • Sources: (How to work around pain, 2020-01; Any movement with a pain byproduct is a bad exercise (for you), 2020-02; 3 YEARS WITHOUT INJURIES： How I bulletproofed myself (and how you can do it too), 2022-06; 10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01)

INJ-24 · Muscle pain is fine, tendon/joint pain is an alarm

  • Statement: There are two kinds of pain: pump and muscle soreness (fine) versus tendon, ligament or joint pain (alarm). Tendons have more nerve endings because they repair poorly. Tension in the muscle is "more painful than dangerous"; pain at the tendon insertion is not.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters.

Tendinitis: diagnosis and treatment

Tendinitis is his most-discussed injury. His treatment is to keep training in a pain-free range, change angles, push blood to the tendon and build the surrounding muscle, with little rest and no painkillers.

INJ-32 · Tendinitis is a spectrum ending in rupture

  • Statement: Tendinitis is the most common lifting injury, ranging from occasional pain to deep all-day pain. Ruptures (biceps, patellar, hip labrum) usually follow months or years of ignored tendinitis.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters.
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Serious injuries don't just ＂happen＂, 2020-01; TENDINITIS, BEGONE! (Healing Tendinopathy / Tendon Pain Rehab for Lifters), 2021-11; TENDINITIS, BEGONE! (Healing Tendinopathy / Tendon Pain Rehab for Lifters), 2021-11; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08)

INJ-33 · Rest does not cure tendinitis

  • Statement: Rest only seems to cure tendinitis; it returns because the movement cause is unchanged. Immobility "fossilizes" the tendon and atrophies the muscle that shares its load. Take at most 1-2 days off when pain is bad, mainly to get over the emotional hump; longer builds a fear association.
  • Numbers: Max 1-2 days off; 3-4 weeks is far too long; 2 weeks off still re-flares.
  • Scope: Any tendinitis.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is tendinitis handled with at most 1-2 days off followed by modified training, rather than weeks of rest?

If you are on them anyway, avoid max singles and stay high-rep. He claims a powerlifter on painkillers squatted through months of hip pain until the labrum tore.

Programming for prevention

Most of his prevention is programming: rotating variations, keeping risky lifts at higher reps, ordering the session, balancing push and pull, and ramping in changes slowly.

INJ-46 · Rotate variations, grips and stances

  • Statement: Rotating variations, grips and stances prevents overuse and is how he gains year-round; small joint-angle changes shift strain while training the same muscle. On machines, rotate grips and machines too.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters, especially intermediate/advanced.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the program rotate variations, grips or stances rather than repeating one identical pattern for long?
  • Sources: (How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; The hypertrophy series： shocking the muscle synergistically & optimally, 2020-07; How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split, 2021-06; WEIGHTS vs MACHINES： Which one is better for muscle gains?, 2022-01)

INJ-47 · Risky lifts at higher reps

  • Statement: Put risky lifts in higher rep ranges so you can sense the bad rep coming. A 1RM concentrates risk into one all-or-nothing rep; an injury on rep 3 at 70% is milder, and a rounded 8RM deadlift is far less risky than at 1RM. 3RM and 10RM give the same hypertrophy, so pick the one you can progress safely.
  • Numbers: 10-15 reps instead of 3-5; burnouts with ~20RM weight, never an 8RM; lunges and good mornings never below 8; hypers ~15, never 3×3.
  • Scope: Injury-prone lifts; hypertrophy goal.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are injury-prone lifts (good mornings, lunges, pullovers, weighted dips/chins, etc.) kept at moderate-to-high reps rather than low-rep maxes?
  • Sources: (Why do injuries happen?, 2020-07; 3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11; 4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)

  • Scope: Small muscles, tendon-heavy lifts.
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020

INJ-72 · Most "back injuries" are SI, nerve or muscle

  • Statement: Discs are hard to destroy; most "back injuries" are SI-joint, nerve or muscle issues. The SI joint needs recovery, so don't hit it every session; only lower-day programming and recovery fix it, and a belt does nothing for it.

INJ-73 · After a back tweak, keep moving

  • Statement: After a low-back tweak, keep moving: unweighted good mornings/squats, then find a pain-free lower movement (leg press, hypers, DB RDLs), then return to squats and deadlifts light. Complete rest atrophies the protective muscles; rehab with hyperextensions rather than good mornings.

INJ-74 · A strong back and core protect

  • Statement: "A stronger muscle is a safer muscle": lower-back isolation is recommended, and deadlifting/squatting is the best prevention for back and knee injuries. Someone who deadlifts 400 lb won't hurt his back picking something up; people in their 30s with back pain mostly have weak backs/cores.

INJ-75 · Good mornings: high risk, high reward

  • Statement: Good mornings top his danger list, since failure pulls you into loaded lumbar flexion with no safe bail, but they remain high-risk/high-reward, not banned. Never do them with a fatigued lower back. Deadlift negatives are also risky because you lower while fatigued.

INJ-76 · Never AMRAP a deadlift

  • Statement: Pulls from the floor make ugly reps too easy to grind, so never AMRAP a deadlift.

  • Scope: Deadlifters.

INJ-77 · Daily posture carries into lifts

  • Statement: Sit tall, use a lumbar pillow, keep the head neutral and don't slouch; slouching carries into lifts and causes back, shoulder and disc problems. Decline starts at the head, then thoracic spine, shoulders, lower back, so fix it in that order. Don't hyperextend into a rigid spine; change positions often.
  • Numbers: Bad posture takes as many years to fix as it took to develop.
  • Scope: Everyone, especially desk workers.

INJ-78 · Scoliosis is no reason to stop lifting

  • Statement: Back and core muscles act as a brace, and he deadlifts heavy with scoliosis; posture can't fix bone. He believes his came from a one-shoulder backpack, and the asymmetry overloaded his lower shoulder, which was repeatedly injured on bench.

INJ-79 · Machines don't prevent back injuries

Knees and patellar tendinitis

INJ-80 · Patellar tendinitis: pattern, frequency, muscle

  • Statement: Patellar tendinitis is fixed in three parts: correct the movement pattern, manage frequency and tonnage, and build the muscles that unload the tendon. Never by rest. Even perfect form wears tendons if frequency is too high.

INJ-81 · Box-squat and widowmaker rehab

INJ-82 · Knee rehab habits and wraps

  • Statement: Morning knee extensions from small to full range, then knee bends; avoid impact sports, running on concrete and cat-style stretches that overextend the knee. Use short elastic wraps angled onto the tendon, not sleeves or hole-braces, and never too tight: X-shape for pain below the kneecap, around the kneecap for kneecap pain, wrapped inside → out. He still tapes his previously torn left knee when it flares.

INJ-83 · Signs of patellar tendinitis vs tear

  • Statement: Signs: pain at the knee break (not the rest of the rep), worse going up stairs, a warm/tender knee, sudden "giving way" when walking. Pain that fades once warm suggests tendinitis; pain that keeps rising suggests a tear.

INJ-84 · Squats aren't bad for knees

  • Statement: "Squats are bad for knees" is a boomer myth; deep squats are fine with controlled knee travel. Knee pain comes from bad form, too much frequency, fat and inactivity; the danger lies in knees shooting forward or caving out of the hole.

INJ-85 · Posterior chain protects the knee

  • Statement: Weak hamstrings and too-vertical, quad-only squatting prime knee injury; posterior chain work and hip hinges protect the knee.

INJ-86 · Knee-unfriendly options

  • Statement: Sissy squats, leg extensions (for some), pad-on-knee calf machines, Platz-style narrow toes-out squats and locking the knees every rep are knee-unfriendly. His own patellar injury came from jumping 225 → 275 in a narrower Platz-style stance after a break.

Shoulders

INJ-87 · Frequent heavy flat bench injures shoulders

  • Statement: Frequent heavy horizontal pressing is the main cause of shoulder injury regardless of form, unless you're an outlier. Injuries are almost always to the rotator cuff/AC joint, not the delts; he claims they are the #1 injury in retired powerlifters. The tell is an achy soreness between pec and shoulder the next day.
  • Numbers: Benching 3×/wk (or 10×10) smoked his shoulders; 3×/wk flat bench = shoulder pain for many intermediates.
  • Scope: Heavy pressers, intermediates and up.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is heavy flat bench kept infrequent (not 3×/wk) or rotated with other horizontal variations?
  • Sources: (Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02; Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; The Best Natural Lifter You've NEVER Heard Of (Hersovyac), 2023-04)

INJ-88 · Vertical pressing is shoulder-friendly

  • Statement: Vertical pressing done properly is easy on, even restorative for, the shoulder; end push days with it and press on top of you, not in front. Heavy OHP after bench made his shoulders "feel amazing".
  • Numbers: Replace one horizontal day with seated OHP 4×8-12 submax + face pulls; DB overhead press 3×6-10 for women.
  • Scope: Pressers with shoulder issues.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2022
  • Status: current

INJ-89 · Rotate horizontal presses, don't cut them

  • Statement: Don't cut horizontal volume for sore shoulders; rotate variations: push-ups, paused/Spoto/close-grip/slingshot/floor press, DB bench, rings, and alternate push-ups and dips.
  • Numbers: Very high-volume push-ups every 2 days are "amazing" for shoulders and pec tendons.
  • Scope: Pressers with sore shoulders.

INJ-90 · Touch-and-go bench wrecked his shoulder

  • Statement: Touch-and-go bench protracted his right shoulder until at 24 he could barely raise his arm; paused bench, Spoto press and the Slingshot let him bench pain-free again.
  • Numbers: Rehab to raw full-range bench in 4-5 months. Typical 2021 session: slingshot up to 315, then 205-235 paused/Spoto/close-grip. Touch-and-go plus scoliosis cost him ~3 weeks off repeatedly over two years.
  • Scope: His own history; benchers with shoulder pain.

INJ-91 · Fix bench mechanics for shoulder pain

  • Statement: For shoulder/AC pain fix the arch, slow negative, bar path and elbow tuck, keep both scapulae on the bench (narrow benches cause issues), and use a hand-off or lift-off rather than a traumatic solo unrack. He uses an in-between elbow angle, not a 90° flare; pain near the armpit means tuck the elbows.

  • Scope: Benchers.

INJ-92 · External rotation and upper back for pressers

  • Statement: External rotation, rear delt and upper-back work keep shoulders healthy, and heavy pressing needs it directly: an upper-back movement every push day. Keep rehab movements in even when pain is gone.
  • Numbers: Face pulls 15-20+ or AMRAP with a band (2020); 4×15-20 (2022); 20-25 between pressing sets (2023).
  • Scope: Heavy pressers.
  • Confidence: high — ~14 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — front delts: 2020 front-delt isolation fixed his shoulders and a strong front delt prevents injury (Response to Steve Shaw (Massive Iron) - Going to WAR Over FRONT DELT training, 2020-03); 2022 overdeveloped front delts versus weak rear/side delts invite injury, and shrinking them stopped his injuries (𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08). Both views value rear delts.
  • Check: Do push days include direct rear-delt/external-rotation/upper-back work (e.g. face pulls)?

INJ-93 · Train shoulder end ranges light

  • Statement: The shoulder is weak at its end ranges: train high-mobility ranges light, never heavy. Sloppy heavy or internally rotated raises cause impingement; upright rows aren't inherently dangerous, the danger is a big-mover mindset.

Elbows, biceps, triceps

INJ-101 · Never overextend the elbow under heavy curls

  • Statement: Never fully extend or overextend the elbow under heavy load in curls; stop the negative short and keep a slight bend. Bouncing off the tendon at full extension does nothing for growth and causes distal tears. If the shoulder moves with the arm, overextension is safe; with the shoulder frozen (preacher curls) it is not.
  • Numbers: ~45° short of extension on concentration-type curls.
  • Scope: Heavy curls.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04; Arm-wrestling style preacher curls tutorial, 2020-08; 𝙃𝙊𝙍𝙍𝙄𝙁𝙄𝘾 𝙡𝙞𝙛𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙞𝙣𝙟𝙪, 2022-08; Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02)

INJ-102 · No heavy supinated pulling, no mixed grip

  • Statement: No supinated/Yates rows, supinated shrugs, or mixed-grip deadlifts or rows: the biceps gives before the back. Bodybuilders should use double overhand, then straps; straps prevent tears and asymmetry. He claims he's never seen a tear with double overhand; mixed grip also causes bar rotation, uneven traps and lower-back torsion. Vertical supinated pulls are generally fine.
  • Numbers: If you insist on supinated rows: 4×10-12, not 3×6-8.
  • Scope: Bodybuilders; heavy pulls.
  • Confidence: high — ~16 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are heavy pulls done double overhand or with straps, never mixed grip or heavy supinated rows?

INJ-103 · Distal biceps tears are permanent

  • Statement: Biceps tears at the distal attachment need surgery, and the biceps never looks the same.

INJ-104 · Pull-ups are limited by tendons

  • Statement: Pull-ups are limited by the elbow, biceps tendon and shoulder, not the back. Rotate grips and implements, and don't drop into a disengaged dead hang and rebound. Weighted chin-ups are the riskiest pull-up (supinated overextension under load). Going unweighted for elbow pain is only temporary.

INJ-105 · Light band curls for biceps tendon health

  • Statement: Light, low-anchored band curls (as many reps as possible, noticeable but not hard) keep the biceps tendon and elbow healthy and keep the deep range. Use them as a finisher on arm days or after heavy push days; never cold or explosive.

10. Nutrition & supplements

This chapter covers what NH says about food, energy balance, protein and macros, meal timing, fasting, food quality, individual food choices, drinks, the psychology of eating, and supplements. His stance: for naturals, training drives growth and diet only fuels it, though diet is the top factor for long-term health. He eats mostly whole, home-cooked, carb-heavy food with modest protein, tailors it to his own body and ancestry, and treats supplements as "D tier", taking only creatine, MSM, bee pollen and a little whey. Bulking, cutting and cardio strategy are in ch. 11.

Where diet ranks

He ranks training above diet for building muscle, but diet above everything for health and longevity. Once a diet works, it should run on autopilot.

NUT-01 · Training matters more than diet for naturals

  • Statement: For a natural lifter, training drives muscle growth and diet only fuels it; the "diet is 70-80%" line is nonsense that comes from drug users. Nutrition only matters once training is on point.
  • Numbers: Training is "at least 50%" (2020), "80% or more" (2023)
  • Scope: Naturals, all levels; training's share grows as you advance
  • Confidence: high — ~15 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020: training is at least 50%; 2023: training is 80% or more
  • Check: Does the program treat training, not diet, as the main driver of muscle gain?
  • Sources: (Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02; Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06; Stop falling for these Ab Training Myths, 2023-03; Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03)

NUT-02 · Diet is the top factor for longevity

11. Bulking, cutting & cardio

This chapter covers how NH thinks a natural should manage bodyweight (bulking, cutting, recomposition, body-fat ranges) and how cardio fits into bodybuilding. His default is a very slow lean bulk on a small surplus, judged by gym progress, waist, mirror and calisthenics rather than the scale. He cuts only if you start fat or compete, and he calls dirty bulks, crash cuts and yo-yo cycles his own biggest mistake. On cardio he moved from "not necessary" (2020-21) to advocate (2023+): short hard sessions after lifting so that your lungs never end a set before your muscles do.

Who should bulk, cut or recomp

His starting question is where you are now: skinny, skinny-fat, lean but small, or fat. Over time he widened the group he tells to bulk.

BLK-01 · Default for naturals: small permanent surplus

  • Statement: Men who are not very over- or underweight should stay in a small surplus for their whole career ("perma-bulk"), unless they start out fat; overshooting body fat once ruins it.
  • Numbers: "permabulk from day one for 15 years"
  • Scope: Natural men not at a bodyweight extreme; fat starters cut first (BLK-04).
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024, still said in 2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the default plan a small, continuous surplus rather than repeated bulk/cut phases?
  • Sources: (What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02; Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02; Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?, 2020-08; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11)

BLK-02 · Who should bulk: from extremes only to most

  • Statement: In 2020 only extremes should bulk or cut (very skinny bulk, very fat cut, everyone else near maintenance). By 2024 lean, small and formerly chubby lifters must lean bulk, and maintaining or cutting is a mistake for them; moving past the lean "auto mode" physique requires an awkward bulking phase.
  • Numbers: example lean-but-small lifter: ~15% at 190 cm/81 kg (2024)
  • Scope: Naturals who are lean but not big, including escaped skinny-fat and formerly chubby lifters.
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020: only very skinny people should bulk; 2024: lean/small lifters must bulk.
  • Sources: (Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02; Greg Doucette's maingaining： gimmicky buzzword or perennial truth?, 2021-01; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12)

BLK-03 · Skinny naturals must gain weight, slowly

  • Statement: Skinny naturals should slow lean bulk on a small surplus, never dirty or aggressively (they just turn skinny-fat). You must gain weight to gain muscle; building muscle at maintenance at 130 lb is a meme. Skinny women need to gain too.
  • Numbers: a skinny novice transforms in 2-3 years
  • Scope: Skinny naturals, men and women.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: changed — 2022: "you do not need a caloric surplus" (he had gained at maintenance); 2022-2024: for skinny/lean lifters a surplus is required and "your best weapon".
  • Sources: (Ectomorphs can NEVER get buff, ripped & strong (Nattyornot.com), 2021-09; Greg Doucette's MainGaining is keeping you small?! (Analyzing Revival Fitness Ex, 2022-01; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11)

BLK-04 · Fat people: lift while you cut

  • Statement: If you start fat, cut while lifting: it keeps muscle, makes the cut easier and keeps skin firmer. A high-fat, low-muscle novice can still build muscle on a cut. Cut until skinny-fat or skinny, then build.

  • Scope: Overweight/obese lifters, especially novices.
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024

BLK-05 · Skinny-fat: recomp at maintenance, never cut

Surplus size

The body can only turn so much food into muscle; past a small surplus the rest is fat.

BLK-12 · Keep the surplus small

  • Statement: Bulk on a small surplus; a few hundred calories is enough and more is pointless for a natural past beginner.
  • Numbers: +200-400 kcal (2020); under 10%, "4% beats 40%" (2021); his own +300 (2022); ~500 kcal gets ~95-98% of possible gains (2022); 200 kcal "enough" (2024-09); 300 "plenty", 500 "pointless" (2024-12)
  • Scope: Naturals past the beginner stage; see BLK-15 for the hardgainer exception.
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024, still said in 2024
  • Status: changed — the advised surplus shrank: 10-15% ceiling (2020) and ~500 kcal near-optimal (2022) → 200-300 kcal, 500 "pointless" (2024).
  • Check: Is the bulking surplus around 200-300 kcal rather than 500+?
  • Sources: (Nutrition Q&A #1, 2020-11; Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)

BLK-13 · Big surplus = fat; big deficit = muscle loss

  • Statement: A big surplus doesn't build more natural muscle, only fat; a big deficit burns muscle as well as fat. Protein synthesis is limited, your capacity to get fat is not.
  • Numbers: no muscle benefit above ~10-15% surplus (2020); 1000-2000 kcal does not double muscle (2022)
  • Scope: Naturals.
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (STORY TIME： My entire diet history, 2020-10; What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02; My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time), 2023-09; Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11)

  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03)

Rate of gain

He measures a bulk by how slowly the scale moves, and the advised rate tightened over the years.

BLK-19 · Gain about 0.5-1.5 lb per month

  • Statement: Bulk slowly; past the beginner stage, more than a pound or so a month is mostly fat.
  • Numbers: under 4 lb/month (2020-08); 1-2 lb/month (2020-12); 0.5-1 lb/month or ~10 lb/year (2023-07); ~1 lb/month (2023-10); 1.5 lb/month "good" on a lean bulk (2024-11)
  • Scope: Intermediate and advanced naturals; true beginners can gain faster (BLK-21).
  • Confidence: high — ~6 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 1-2 lb/month (2020) tightened to 0.5-1 lb/month after his own too-fast 2023 bulk (20-30 lb in a year); 1.5 lb/month called good in 2024.
  • Check: Is the target gain about 0.5-1.5 lb per month (less if advanced)?
  • Sources: (Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?, 2020-08; BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12; Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07; Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11)

Training drives the bulk

Calories only fuel what the training creates.

Bulk checks: muscle or fat?

Rising scale and bar weight do not prove muscle; he uses calisthenics, waist, mirror and the ratio of strength to bodyweight.

BLK-32 · The calisthenics check

  • Statement: If bench rises while push-ups regress, or rows rise while pull-ups drop, you're gaining fat: slow down or stop the bulk. Keep calisthenics in while bulking.

Recomposition

A recomp trades fat for muscle at a fixed bodyweight. He ran one for three years and then concluded a slow bulk grows you faster.

BLK-54 · Recomp is real but slower than a bulk

  • Statement: A recomp is its own thing, not a bulk/cut hybrid: heavy training at maintenance makes the body draw on fat stores, like sculpting a statue. It is slow but real; for growth, a slow bulk beats it.

  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2024

Cardio: purpose

For a bodybuilder, cardio exists so your heart and lungs never cut a set short.

  • Statement: Never end a squat or deadlift set out of breath with reps left in the muscles. Getting winded after one rep, on curls or after a bench set means poor conditioning; fix it with conditioning work or a slower tempo.
  • Numbers: he squats 8 reps to failure and deadlifts 5 heavy without breathing hard

12. Beginners, training levels & equipment

This chapter covers how he defines novice, intermediate and advanced lifters, what he wants a novice to do, and his views on gear, straps and building or choosing a gym. On beginners, his stance is that "anything works", so a novice should play the long game: a minimal, written full-body program with isolation from day one, free weights and calisthenics, few hard sets, and adherence above all. On equipment, he says straps are a must whenever grip limits a pulling set and most other gear is optional. His gym advice moved from home-gym evangelism (2020-2021) to a hybrid home/commercial view (2023-2025).

Why the novice phase matters

He treats the novice phase as a foundation for a long career rather than a race, and novice results as proof of nothing.

BEG-01 · Anything works, so choose for the long term

  • Statement: Almost any program works for novices. That should free them to pick what sets up the rest of their career, not justify random programs, and novice results prove nothing about a program, coach or channel.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: novices; it becomes "a game of inches" only later
  • Confidence: high — ~18 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the novice phase judged by skill, habits and base built rather than by how fast the numbers rise?
  • Sources: (How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03; Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08; RIP Natural Hypertrophy; Welcome School of Strategy!, 2025-01)

BEG-02 · Build a base and habits, not performance

  • Statement: Novice status is short but you are an intermediate or advanced lifter for life, so use the novice period to build a base, prevent injuries and form habits rather than to chase numbers.
  • Numbers: noob gains may be only 3-4% of your lifting time
  • Scope: novices
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (The training principles series： noob gains, 2020-02; AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03; How often should you change programs?, 2020-08; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03)

BEG-03 · Don't rush out of the novice phase

  • Statement: Treat the novice phase like childhood and prolong it. The noob-gain "poison" and the "noob" stigma make people rush.
  • Numbers: 1-2 years as a novice "doesn't matter" over a 20-year career; 6-12 months costs nothing; strength novice status can last up to 2 years
  • Scope: novices
  • Confidence: high — ~8 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — see BEG-10 (2020-04 "no more than 4-6 months" → 2020-11/2021 prolong to 1-2 years → 2024 done within a year for many)
  • Sources: (How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11; Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03; Strength standards are useless, 2022-04)

Reps, loading and progression

Novices start light, build skill before load, and learn overload methods beyond adding weight.

BEG-40 · Start light and accumulate quality reps

  • Statement: Start light, even with the empty bar, and accumulate quality reps without struggling or compromising the next session. Repeat a hard weight before adding more; no PR is worth an injury.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: novices
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: current

BEG-41 · Fixed schemes first, evolving ranges on accessories

  • Statement: Fixed schemes (5x5, 3x5) are fine at first; use evolving ranges on accessories, then spread them. If every lift uses evolving ranges, tonnage collapses when all hit their low point at once.
  • Numbers: evolving ranges 6-10, 8-12; turning a 3x3 into a 3x3-5 takes ~2 weeks to learn
  • Scope: novices
  • Confidence: medium — ~6 videos, 2020→2021
  • Status: contradicted — "evolving ranges are not suitable for beginners" vs "teach them early so they become second nature"
  • Sources: (How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09; How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09; The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08)

BEG-42 · Use rep ranges where form stays clean

  • Statement: Novices should use higher reps in a range where form stays clean; back work that loads the lower back and hamstrings needs at least 6-10 reps.
  • Numbers: ≥6-10 reps; 3x6 rows get butchered; 4x8 squats are risky because of grinding and ugly reps
  • Scope: novices
  • Confidence: medium — ~3 videos, 2020
  • Status: current
  • Sources: (Ivysaur Novice program review, 2020-08; Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05)

Exercise selection for novices

Novice-specific choices; general exercise selection is in ch. 5 and body-part detail in ch. 6.

BEG-47 · Free weights and bodyweight before machines

  • Statement: Novices should learn on free weights and bodyweight; machines, cables and the Smith are for advanced lifters. Novices on machines "stay small for years", and a machine-and-cable novice program is a bad sign.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: novices; exception from 2024: the Smith vertical press, which handles stabilisation
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020-2023: the Smith is useless or harmful for beginners (never learn squat or bench on it); 2024: novices should lean on the Smith vertical press

ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09)

  • Statement: Calisthenics is an ideal entry and perhaps the best base for bodybuilding: learn to move your body through space without needing a gym, rep ranges or plate math.

BEG-49 · Pull-ups over pulldowns; vertical over horizontal

BEG-50 · Pull-up progression for novices

  • Statement: Use negatives if you can't do a pull-up, then many low-rep sets or AMRAP sets, and stay at bodyweight until a clean 15. No weighted chins for novices.

BEG-51 · No barbell or Pendlay rows for novices

BEG-52 · A full-ROM floor pull, at low volume

  • Statement: A full-ROM pull from the floor is mandatory for novices, but deadlift volume stays low. Any full hip hinge counts (conventional, sumo, trap bar, Atlas stones).

BEG-53 · Deadlift entry points and grip

  • Statement: Ways in: trap bar (high → low handles → conventional), rack pulls to learn the hinge, deficits to teach leg drive, dumbbell deadlifts. No Jefferson or snatch-grip deadlifts for novices; grip double overhand with straps (see EQP-07).

Learning to program

He sees learning to write your own program as the real exit from the novice phase, and optimisation as a novice trap.

BEG-63 · Learn by modifying the program you run

  • Statement: Learn to program by modifying the novice program you run, then use it as a skeleton: copy its rep ranges, match its tonnage, stay minimalist. The first draft will look terrible; if the base program is very bad, start from scratch.
  • Numbers: run it 3-6 months with fixes; drafting your own while on it may take a year
  • Scope: late novices
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: changed — 2020: novices shouldn't write programs (theirs are almost always bad); 2021: draft your own while running the novice program; 2024: start on an established program, then write your own and have a coach review it (a refinement, not a flip)
  • Sources: (How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11; How often should you change programs?, 2020-08; How to program your training yourself, 2021-02; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11)

Straps, grip and hand care

Straps are his strongest equipment position: grip should never be what ends a back set.

EQP-01 · Strap up when grip limits a pulling set

  • Statement: Use straps as soon as grip limits a back or pulling set, and spend the saved grip on direct forearm work. "Letting grip limit the back is criminal"; straps let you isolate the back better and don't hurt forearm growth.
  • Numbers: forearm isolation costs only 10-15 min/week
  • Scope: non-powerlifters with a hypertrophy goal, once grip limits (not novices at first, see EQP-04)
  • Confidence: high — ~10 videos, 2020→2025
  • Status: current
  • Check: Are straps used on back and pull sets where grip would otherwise end the set, with forearms trained directly?

Minimal-equipment training

You can grow with little equipment, but calisthenics alone makes legs and big size hard.

EQP-27 · Core minimal kit: pull-up bar, rings, bands

  • Statement: A pull-up bar, wooden gymnastic rings and bands are enough for excellent gains; rings are invaluable without a gym. Add a dip station.

EQP-53 · How to build the platform

  • Statement: Plan on paper and do a mock assembly; buy plywood in person (online stock is warped). Use mid-quality wood for the base and the best wood for the top; glue the base layers but screw the mats and top wood so damaged pieces can be swapped. Shim sloped garage floors, add a vapour barrier in arctic climates, and use wood screws if bolting a rack.
  • Numbers: plan 1-2 months ahead; top wood ~3x the price; glue dries ~40 min; swapping a damaged piece ~$30
  • Scope: platform builders

13. The fitness industry & reading science

This chapter covers how NH sees the fitness business (programs, coaching, supplements, influencers, YouTube itself), how to judge whom to trust, and how he weighs scientific evidence against lived experience. His stance: the industry exists to sell, hard work can't be sold, and lifting knowledge should be free, so learn to program for yourself and question anyone who profits from you. On science he calls himself experience-based rather than "science-based": he is against scientism and the "science-based" brand, not against the scientific method. Everything said here about named people and brands is his unverified opinion. PEDs and natural limits as such are in ch. 2, training variables in ch. 3-4, supplements in ch. 10.

Selling knowledge: programs and coaching

He holds that knowledge you got for free should stay free, that a lifter who can program needs no one, and that most paid programs and coaching exploit beginners. His own paid tier from late 2024 is the main exception (see IND-21).

IND-01 · Lifting knowledge should be free

  • Statement: Charging for knowledge you got for free is unjust; all his own programs are free, and he likens paid plans to selling festival water when free water is hidden nearby.
  • Numbers: ~30 free programs by 2023; a $50-100 non-personalised program or ebook is "ridiculous"; $1000 for plans is overpriced
  • Scope: Non-personalised programs, ebooks and plans
  • Confidence: high — ~12 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: changed — he stayed opposed to selling generic programs, but from Dec 2024 runs a paid personalised tier (see IND-21)
  • Sources: (RANT： You don't need a coach, 2020-02; Vertical diet review, 2020-06; Censorship on Youtube： How Greg Doucette betrayed the entire Fitness community b, 2021-05; HUGE ANNOUNCEMENT 🎁 (You're gonna love this), 2023-12)

IND-02 · Learn to program for yourself

  • Statement: A program you build and beta-test yourself is "ten times better" than a bought one, and knowing how to program protects you from exploitation; gurus who discourage self-programming keep you dependent so they can sell.
  • Numbers: His planned $40 program (BBBS) would have been "garbage" marketed, so stop buying programs
  • Scope: All lifters, novices encouraged to explore programming early
  • Confidence: high — ~9 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: current
  • Check: Does the lifter understand and control his own program rather than depend on a seller for it?

How he weighs evidence

He ranks your own tested experience above studies, pooled experience above single papers, and treats science as a bonus that is useful only if it improves training.

SCI-01 · Your own body is the best evidence

  • Statement: Your own body's data is the most valid evidence; studies are group generalisations that are worthless until tested on yourself, and your experience matters more than his or all the science. "Optimal" is whatever you've proven works on your body.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: All lifters
  • Confidence: high — ~7 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: current
  • Check: Is the method judged by how the lifter actually responded to it, not only by what studies say?
  • Sources: (You don't need science to see results, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： using mind muscle connection for tonnage quality control, 2020-06; The impact of exogenous estrogen on the male body (from a broscientist perspecti, 2020-03; 5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters, 2023-10)

SCI-02 · He doesn't cite studies

  • Statement: He never cites or links studies or uses them as arguments of authority; his channel shares experience, and a natural with a good physique is "a mine of knowledge" as valuable as peer review.
  • Numbers: —
  • Scope: His channel
  • Confidence: high — ~5 videos, 2020→2024
  • Status: contradicted — he invokes specific studies when they support him (tempo, ROM, boxers, 500 mg testosterone, lengthened vs 90°), close to the cherry-picking he criticises (SCI-12)
  • Sources: (The impact of exogenous estrogen on the male body (from a broscientist perspecti, 2020-03; The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01; The ULTIMATE Triceps Exercises Tier-List (Mythical-tier to Toothpick-tier), 2022-10; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01)

SCI-03 · You can grow without science

14. Life philosophy, culture & manga

This chapter covers what NH teaches beyond training: how to live, what to value, how to handle relationships, and the anime, manga, books and physical-culture history that shaped him. His core position is that lifting is one half of a complete life: body and mind must be built together, struggle beats comfort, you own your life completely, and strength only counts once it serves others. His philosophy moved from Stoicism (2020) through Nietzsche (2022-23) to Jung (2024), and much of this chapter is opinion, not training method. Claims about real people are his unverified opinions.

Body and mind: the complete man

The base of his worldview is that the body is not secondary. Training is a spiritual practice, but it does not fix your life by itself.

PHI-01 · Build body and mind together

  • Statement: Body and spirit must be developed together; the ideal is the "complete man" or "educated barbarian". Training without reading and thinking is as unbalanced as theory without a body.
  • Numbers: Training 10 h/day without reading "won't even produce proper gains".
  • Scope: Everyone, especially men; applies to lifters and to intellectuals alike.
  • Confidence: high — ~20 videos, 2020→2023
  • Status: changed — 2020: the body is "the lesser part", an envelope ("you are not your body"); 2021-23: body and soul are one coin and the body belongs at the centre of life (see PHI-03).
  • Check: Does the program or advice treat training as part of a whole life that also includes reading, thinking and other people?
  • Sources: (The Educated Barbarian： Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 4), 2020-05; The Educated Barbarian： Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 6), 2020-06; The Educated Barbarian： Hagakure analysis (part. 5), 2020-08; The Problematic Masculinity of 300, 2023-01)

  • Numbers: ~95% mind / 5% body today vs ~50/50 in antiquity; 2 h of school PE a week is not enough.
  • Scope: Society, schools, children.
  • Confidence: medium — ~4 videos, 2022→2023

  • Sources: (Indian Lifting Wisdom, 2022-07; Medieval Lifting Wisdom, 2022-04; Are you too smart to lift?, 2023-01; Are you too smart to lift?, 2023-01)

Appendix A. Contradictions & how his views changed

Collected by script from the topic syntheses: where NH changed his mind over time, and where he said conflicting things without a clear evolution. The principles in the chapters carry the same information in their Status field; this appendix shows it all in one place.

Aesthetics

Changed over time

  • Shoulders: 2020-2022 kept delts deliberately small, cut shoulder tonnage, wanted arms bigger than delts (Road to bigger shoulders update, 2021-05; Hypertrophy Q&A #8, 2021-09; My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE), 2022-06) → 2023 shoulders are his weak point and must catch up with his huge upper back; 2024 priorities: rounder shoulders via vertical presses and isolation (Wild Man Training (Hypertrophy Log #0), 2023-06; Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09); 2024 tier list puts shoulders top tier, though he still likes them small next to the arm (The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). Later view: grow them, keep arms dominant.
  • Neck size: 2020 neck should be wider than the jaw and ≈ arm size (18 in for 19 in arms) (Road to a bigger neck： 18 inches or bust!, 2020-01; How to body measurements & discussing my weak points, 2020-02) → 2022-2024 in line with the jaw is enough, more looks like a ball (Most UNDERRATED Muscle for Aesthetics (TAKE THE NECK PILL), 2022-11; The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03). Later view: jaw-line standard.
  • Chest in his ideal: 2020-2022 trunk/chest comparatively small (Berserker, Buddha physique) (Going Berserker mode (Berserk physique introduction), 2020-03; Why you NEED a goal body, 2021-09; My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE), 2022-06) → 2023 Berserker includes a big chest (Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09).
  • Abs' importance: 2020-2023 core is key and ties the physique together (My philosophy regarding abs training, 2020-03; Come with me if you want ABS! (6 PACK MASSterplan), 2023-05) → 2024 tier list: abs bottom tier for everyday clothed looks (The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03), while he still says never skip core (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09). A refinement by context (clothed vs shirtless).
  • Glutes: 2022 silver era didn't chase glutes, posterior chain optional (Silver Era Aesthetics Program (Steve Reeves Physique Workout), 2022-10) → 2024 glutes top tier (The Most Important Muscles to Look JACKED (Aesthetics Tier-List), 2024-03) (he already said in 2021 they can't hurt a male physique (Level up your legs, 2021-06)).
  • His own body fat/weight: 210 lb at 17-18% (2020) and 16-17% (2021-22) → 220 lb, 17-18% (2024) (What everyone gets WRONG about bodyfat %, 2020-05; How Big Can You Get Naturally? (Nattyornot.com), 2021-12; This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06; 10 Signs you might be a Blackpilled Natty, 2024-04).

Contradictions

  • Leanness as a goal: 2020 "as big as his body allows at the lowest bodyfat possible" (Seven Deadly Fitness Sins： Lust, 2020-05) vs 2024 "never cared about being lean and still does not" (Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11).
  • Do heavy squats and hinges thicken the waist? 2022: they develop the waist, don't overdo them (Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05) vs 2022: that idea is "mostly nonsense" (Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03).
  • Tight waist: 2020 he doesn't care about a tiny waist (Going Berserker mode (Berserk physique introduction), 2020-03) vs 2020 keeps the waist as tight as possible (Natural Hypertrophy： What I picture as my ideal physique, 2020-01). Probably both mean "can't be tiny, keep it tight".
  • Upper back and other limbs as priorities for others: 2020 "never too much upper back" (Road to a Bigger Back update, 2020-11) vs 2022 classical statues/Apollonian lack a wide lat flare and have smaller arms and legs (Farnese Hercules Bodybuilding Program (Ancient Greek Herculean Physique Workout), 2022-03; Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05). These are goal-dependent, not a real conflict.

Beginners

Changed over time

  • Small muscle groups: "later" → "from day one". 2020: calves are unimportant for novices, and neck, traps and calves can wait until you have a solid physique (Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02; Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02). 2023: forearm isolation is optional (Come with me if you want big forearms (7 Steps MASSterplan), 2023-02). 2024 (later view): isolate forearms from day one and catch dormant weak points early (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12).
  • What "base" means. 2020: novices should build a wide base covering all movement patterns, and in one video should focus only on bench, squat and deadlift before hypertrophy work (Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07; Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01). 2023 (later view): a real base is push-up and pull-up proficiency, and his programs skew toward bodybuilding because there is "no reason to waste years building a 'base'" (These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List), 2023-02; Powerbuilding Drama： The Final Answer, 2023-11).
  • Length of the novice phase. 2020-04: novices shouldn't stay novices more than 4-6 months (Programming for high change personality types, 2020-04). 2020-11 → 2021: prolong it to 1-2 years (How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11; Surviving Novice Syndrome (a beginner's guide to lifting), 2021-08). 2024: done within a year for many (So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11).
  • Smith machine. 2020-2023: useless or harmful for beginners (Is the smith machine completely useless?, 2020-02; The ULTIMATE Quads/Legs Exercises Tier-List (Platz-tier to Chicken-tier), 2023-07). 2024 (later view, vertical press only): novices should lean heavily on the Smith vertical press because it handles stabilisation (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09).
  • Lateral raises. 2020: beginners don't need side raises (Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02). 2022: they are in his novice shoulder example (Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10).
  • Writing your own program. 2020: novices should not write programs because theirs are almost always bad (How to never have to buy a training program again in your life, 2020-11). 2021: draft your own while running the novice program (How to program your training yourself, 2021-02). 2024: start on an established program, then write your own and have a coach review it (So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11). This is a refinement, not a flip.

Contradictions

  • Daily vs 3x/week full body. He prefers "full body every day" with one heavy compound per day, and novices can recover from daily calisthenics (Fullbody template review, 2021-01; Don't turn your back on calisthenics, 2021-06). Elsewhere: 3x/week is the default and full body needs programming knowledge novices lack (Fullbody template review, 2021-01; The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09).
  • Squat/deadlift frequency. Novices should squat and deadlift several times a week (using deloads) (Who can afford to only squat and deadlift once a week?, 2020-03). His own routine deliberately lowers squat and deadlift frequency, and deadlifts once a week (ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10; The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03).
  • Intensity. Lower intensity and volume at first, never struggling (Your Fitness New Year's Resolution will fail. Here's why：, 2022-01; Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02). But the top beginner mistake is training too easy, and novices should go to failure (Can you look like Kratos from God of War in real life? (RAGNAROK WORKOUT), 2022-11; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11).
  • Variations. "No variations for novices", with the paused squat as the exception (How to use pause reps for SIZE, 2021-05; ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06). Yet he likes novices doing variations (Programming for people with limited mobility, 2020-11; How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split, 2021-06).
  • Evolving rep ranges. Not suitable for beginners (The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05). Teach them early (The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08; Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02).
  • Explore vs repeat. Beginners should be "tossed into the sea" and explore (How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02). A good novice program embraces monotony (Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02; ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10).
  • Isolation dose. "Would never prescribe that much isolation to a novice" (Jeff Nippard's Push Pull Legs program review, 2021-01). Isolation in every program from the start (Isolation movements benefits： attacking muscles more precisely, 2020-03).

Bulk cut

Changed over time

  • Recomp evangelist → slow bulker. 2020-2021: recomping is "the future", better than bulk/cut, and "recomp beats bulking for me". He planned to recomp 4-5 more years (2021-05, 2022-03) (Recomp guide (part. 2)： Who can do it & diet manipulation, 2020-05; Natural Q&A #2, 2020-09; Natural Q&A #7, 2021-05; Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03). August 2022: ended the 3-year 210 lb maintenance and said his recomp growth was "minimal compared" to a bulk. He switched to a 2-3 year slow lean bulk to 215-220 lb (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08; Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08; 3 YEAR RECOMP TRANSFORMATION (From Husky to Jacked) - 50K SPECIAL, 2022-08). 2024: "perma-bulker is the way to go unless you start out fat" (So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11). Later view: slow bulking.
  • Surplus necessity. 2022: "you do not need a caloric surplus", having gained at maintenance (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08). 2022-2024: for skinny/lean lifters, a surplus is required ("you must gain weight to gain muscle"), and "a caloric surplus is your best weapon" (Greg Doucette's MainGaining is keeping you small?! (Analyzing Revival Fitness Ex, 2022-01; How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01; So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11). Later view: a surplus is the main tool except for people with fat to trade.
  • Who should bulk. 2020: only very skinny people should bulk (Should natural lifters bulk / cut?, 2020-02). 2024: lean/small and formerly chubby lifters must bulk, and maintaining is a mistake (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12). Later view: broader bulking.
  • Rate tightened. 1-2 lb/month (2020-12) (BLOATMAXX： the Kyriakos Grizzly example, mogging general & potential downsides, 2020-12) → 0.5-1 lb/month after his own too-fast 2023 bulk (20-30 lb in a year) (Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07; My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time), 2023-09). In 2024 1.5 lb/month was "good" (Therapy is CANCELLED (Jung ｜ Modern Man in Search of a Soul), 2024-11).
  • Surplus size shrank. 10-15% ceiling (2020) (What you should NOT be doing during a bulk, 2020-02) → 200-300 kcal, 500 "pointless" (2024) (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). Note: in 2022 he called ~500 kcal near-optimal (Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11).
  • Recomp floor. 2020: recomp down to ~12-13% (Recomp guide (part.1)： What it is & isn't, 2020-05). 2022: don't recomp below ~14-15% (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08). Later view: 14-15%.
  • Maintenance as a summer tool. Since 2024 he cycles winter bulk / summer maintenance-recomp (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09; BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09). That replaces both his 2020 "no cycles" stance and his 2023 continuous-bulk plan (Wild Man Training (Hypertrophy Log #0), 2023-06).

Contradictions

  • Dirty vs slow bulk muscle gain. He claims dirty bulking builds less muscle because junk lacks protein (The dangers of dirty bulking (and why I don't recommend it), 2020-03) (2020). He also claims the muscle difference is "negligibly small, if it exists" (Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11) (2021).
  • Target bodyweight. Never set a goal bodyweight (Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11; My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time), 2023-09). But he praised Hamza's 180 lb target as "good nuanced advice" (How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can’t Gain Muscle), 2023-01) (2023-01).
  • Tall lifters. Slow patient bulking (2023-12) (Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12) vs aggressive bulking justified (2024-12) (So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12).
  • Years spent bulking. "Bulked 14 of his 15 years" (Story Time (Top 10 NH stories), 2024-12) vs a 3-year maintenance at 210 lb (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08).
  • Recomp vs bulk+cut efficiency. Similar or slightly less long-term (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08) vs losing dirty-bulk fat by recomp ~15x slower than a slow bulk (Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11).
  • His ideal body fat. 10-12% advised for an "otter mode" look (2023-03) (Is THIS the most attractive body type? (Ottermode Physique), 2023-03) vs 15-16% best for himself in the same video (Is THIS the most attractive body type? (Ottermode Physique), 2023-03). Likely physique-specific, not a real conflict.

Cardio

Changed over time

  • No cardio → cardio advocate. 2020-2021: he "does not do cardio in the conventional way", hadn't done cardio in 3 years, did all cardio with weights and never used ellipticals or steppers. Cardio was "not necessary", and 30 min lifting beats 30 min cardio (The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health, 2020-10; The hypertrophy series： surpassing cardiovascular limitations, 2020-05; Building work capacity with cardio specificity, 2021-02; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07). From 2023-11: cardio is "S tier", 5-15 min after every session, and it "makes you a better bodybuilder". He now does the stair machine, treadmill miles and carries (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12). Later view: do cardio.
  • Calories framing. 2020: cardio kills gains indirectly through calories, and skinny lifters should avoid it (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; ANIME WORKOUTS - Would Jack Hanma's Transformation in Grappler Baki be possible , 2020-12). 2024: good cardio boosts gains (The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02).
  • Leg-day cardio. 2022: avoid intense leg cardio on leg days (Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01). 2024-12: hard cardio on top of leg training boosts recovery and conditioning (How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12). Later view: it's fine.
  • Stepper/jump rope. 2020: prefer stepper or jump rope over treadmill (The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health, 2020-10). 2021: never steppers (Building work capacity with cardio specificity, 2021-02). 2024: StairMaster is S tier and jump rope is poor for bodybuilders (The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02; The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02).
  • Running. 2020: uphill running "unmatched" for cardio (4 days Upper Lower program review, 2020-06). 2024: running C tier, long distance D (The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02; The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02). Sprints and fartlek stay highly rated.

Contradictions

  • Running surface vs running. He says best cardio is outdoors on soft ground (2020) (The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health, 2020-10), yet he runs on a self-powered treadmill and ranks the treadmill D tier (2024) (So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12; The ULTIMATE Cardio/Calves Exercises Tier-List, 2024-02). The manual treadmill is his exception (This is what the Perfect Physique looks like (Physical 100 Season 2), 2024-04).
  • Weights-only cardio. "He does not recommend that people do cardio only through weight training" (The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health, 2020-10) vs, in the same era, he does all his cardio with weights and says high-rep work and giant sets "already provide enough" conditioning (Building work capacity with cardio specificity, 2021-02; Doggcrapp Training review, 2021-01).

Culture manga

Changed over time

  • Goal physique: adult Gon in 2020 (Natural Hypertrophy： What I picture as my ideal physique, 2020-01). A Zodd/Guts/Uvogin/Toguro mix in 2022, with Guts "too much shoulder" (My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE), 2022-06). In 2023 he describes an explicitly unreachable anime body as the point of striving (Build your Dream Physique with Image Training ｜ The Power of Placebo & Visualiza, 2023-02). This is a refinement, not a reversal.
  • Guts as a model: in 2021 Golden Age Guts was a physique target (Can you look like Guts from Berserk in real life?, 2021-12). In 2023 he warns against emulating Guts's psychological traits (the physique is still fine; a Guts program is offered in 2024) (You are not Guts (The Berserk Trauma), 2023-10; Swinging a sword WON'T make you jacked, 2024-02).

Contradictions

  • Favourite film: Star Wars Episode III "of all time" (2021) (Natural Q&A #8, 2021-10) vs Watchmen (2022) (I WON! Japanese Boomers on 🅷🅰🆁🅰🅺🅸🆁🅸 Watch (Victory Q&A), 2022-09).
  • Favourite fiction: a French YA fantasy series ranked with Lord of the Rings (2022) (I WON! Japanese Boomers on 🅷🅰🆁🅰🅺🅸🆁🅸 Watch (Victory Q&A), 2022-09) vs Dune as favourite book of all time (2024) (The Philosophy of Dune, 2024-03).
  • Physique role models: he "never looked up to any physique" and was his own standard (2020) (Why your Genetics don't matter, 2020-12) vs adult Gon as his goal physique the same year (Natural Hypertrophy： What I picture as my ideal physique, 2020-01).
  • Baki's height: given as 5'2" (A Shonen rewriting of David and Goliath： Baki vs Hanayama in Grappler Baki, 2020-12) vs 5'6" (MUSCLE MANGA - Ohma ＂The Ashura＂ Tokita's Physique in Kengan Ashura (part. 1), 2021-05) (fictional stats; minor).

Equipment home gym

Changed over time

  • Home vs commercial gym: in 2020-2021 he said owning your gym unlocks progress, commercial gyms are dying, and an elite physique eventually needs a personal gym (Benefits of having a home gym： King in your own castle, 2020-03; Swole shaming is real, BIGot, 2021-03; Buy a home gym, escape the Gestapo, 2021-01). From 2023 to 2025 he calls commercial gyms optimal for building muscle, trains about 50/50, joined a gym for delts and triceps, and recommends cheap uncrowded gyms (Mountain Training Arc (100K SPECIAL), 2023-08; Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01). The later view is the hybrid one.
  • Machines: he was a "barbell purist" in 2020 who didn't need guided machines (Should home gym owners invest in machines?, 2020-02). In 2022-2024 he rates good machines, Smith machines and cables highly (converging presses may beat the bench) (The ULTIMATE Chest Exercises Tier-List (Gorilla-tier to A cup-tier), 2022-12; Hypertrophy training is CANCELLED, 2024-06; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Shoes: in 2020 he wore heeled lifting shoes for all squats (What shoes should you wear for lifting? ( Flat sole vs high heel), 2020-01). In 2024 he squats flat with no difference and keeps lifting shoes only for high-bar (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Sleeves/wraps: in 2020 they added poundage for almost anyone (The utility of lifting gear, 2020-08). In 2021 they were mostly placebo, 10-20 lb (The form p＊lice is under arrest, 2021-07; Injury Q&A #4, 2021-06).
  • Slingshot: he reviewed it positively in 2020-2021 (Should you buy this instead of a slingshot? (Bench daddy review), 2020-01; Hypertrophy benefits of the Slingshot, 2021-01). In 2025 he no longer uses it and is selling it (You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01).
  • Adjustable dumbbells: in 2020 they made sense vs fixed sets (Rogue DB-10 DB-15 loadable dumbbells review - Best on the market?, 2020-07). In 2024 they're a "trap" unless used ≥3x/week (TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09).
  • Neck harness: in 2022 plates and bands were enough for an aesthetic neck (Most UNDERRATED Muscle for Aesthetics (TAKE THE NECK PILL), 2022-11). In 2023 a harness is far better and he regrets not buying one sooner (HELP! I'm getting too BIG (Hypertrophy Log #5), 2023-11).
  • Fat grips: in 2020 he wasn't using them ("beta take") (Fat grips training for forearm hypertrophy, 2020-03). In 2023 they're A tier (The ULTIMATE Forearm Exercises Tier-List (Popeye-tier to Skeletor-tier), 2023-03).
  • Kettlebells: in 2022 any resistance was valid (Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01). In 2024 they're inferior for hypertrophy (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12).
  • Timing to build: in 2020 he said don't build during the COVID crisis (Benefits of having a home gym： King in your own castle, 2020-03). In 2021 it was a good time because prices had fallen (Buy a home gym, escape the Gestapo, 2021-01) (context change, not a reversal).

Contradictions

  • Used gear value: buying a home gym is like owning a house because you can resell, and even overpriced gear saves money long term (Save your money, buy a home gym, 2021-07; Save your money, buy a home gym, 2021-07). Elsewhere, used gear loses value and isn't an investment like stocks (Fake Merc Character Study (part. 9)： Grifter by day, Porker by night, 2021-02). In the same video he also calls the membership-savings argument weak (Save your money, buy a home gym, 2021-07).
  • Cheap used dumbbells: in 2022 cheap second-hand DBs feel terrible and can cause tendonitis (💸 Revolutionary Money-Saving Hack (MUST-HAVE for ALL Lifters!), 2022-09). In 2024 he says buy used dumbbells from closing gyms or private sellers (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09) (probably junk vs gym-grade, but not stated).
  • Sneakers: in 2020 he says avoid sneakers/Jordans for lifting (What shoes should you wear for lifting? ( Flat sole vs high heel), 2020-01). Also in 2020 he calls LeBron lifestyle sneakers his favorite lifting shoes (10 000$ Home Gym Tour - 10k subs special, 2020-12).
  • His platform cost: ~$500 for 16x8 ft (Feb 2020) (Equipment you can afford to go cheap on for your home gym, 2020-02) vs $800-900 for 16x9 ft (Dec 2020) (10 000$ Home Gym Tour - 10k subs special, 2020-12).
  • Months of cold: 8 months at ~20 °F (Everything wrong with Online Masculinity and Modern Bodybuilding all in one meat, 2022-02) vs ~6 months at 20-30 °F (Natural Q&A #9, 2022-01), both 2022.

Exercise selection

Changed over time

  • Deadlift → RDL. 2020-21: deadlifts are mandatory, ~85% of his back thickness, the best whole-body builder, floor pulls never optional (FREE 4/5 days Gentleman split (part. 1), 2020-10; Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12; Coolcicada 6 Days PPL Program review, 2020-05). 2022: the deadlift is an accessory to the RDL (Top 8 WORST Lifts for Hypertrophy (and why you should still do them), 2022-09). 2023-24: RDL is king, the deadlift is B/C tier, an "energy vampire" done ~once a month, and bodybuilders don't need it (Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04). Later view: RDL first.
  • Bench → dips/ring push-ups. 2020: bench is the best horizontal press by risk/reward; he wouldn't recommend dips over bench (Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03; Response to Husaka - CHEST - Bench vs Ring Push Ups, 2020-03). 2023-24: weighted dips are S tier, "squat of the upper body", and he dropped bench after shoulder injuries (I was WRONG about these lifts, 2023-12; So you think you look good? (Physique Critique Chad Edition), 2024-12; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Lat pulldowns. 2020-21: replace them with pull-ups; he used no pulldowns (5 days Upper Lower program review (part. 2), 2020-10; Weak point Wednesday： Lats (how I will grow mine), 2020-02). 2022-24: close-grip neutral and iliac pulldowns are top tier, and the pulldown is the best pull-up substitute, worth rotating in anyway (The ULTIMATE Back/Lats Exercises Tier-List (Yujiro-tier to Peewee-tier), 2022-11; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09).
  • Incline curls. 2020-22: poor, mediocre, C tier (Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06; The ULTIMATE Biceps Exercises Tier-List (Arnold-tier to Noodle-tier), 2022-10). 2023-24: A/S tier, and he admits he was "just bad at it" (I was WRONG about these lifts, 2023-12; Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11).
  • Squat style. 2020: deep (back) squats are the best leg builder; never Smith squat (The dangers of dirty bulking (and why I don't recommend it), 2020-03; AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04). 2023-24: 80% of his squat volume is heel-elevated, he back squats ~once a month, all squats heel-elevated, and Smith feet-forward squats and Smith split squats are top tier (I was WRONG about these lifts, 2023-12; The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12; The ULTIMATE Quads/Legs Exercises Tier-List (Platz-tier to Chicken-tier), 2023-07).
  • Unilateral/split squats/lunges. 2020: bias against unilateral work; never lunges (knees) (Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05; Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 1)： Causes & symptoms, 2020-05). 2023-24: unilateral A tier, split squats his favourite leg lift, reverse lunges S tier (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; The ULTIMATE Legs/Hamstrings Exercises Tier-List (Horse-tier to Polio-tier), 2023-04).
