  • Cheat curls: 2020, they are what grew his biceps, done weekly for 7-10 years (Cheat curls： EZ bar vs Dumbbells, 2020-07; How to avoid bicep tears, 2020-03). 2022, quit after reaching 100 lb, and says they are "not a good exercise" (13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS： Was it worth it?, 2022-05; The ULTIMATE Biceps Exercises Tier-List (Arnold-tier to Noodle-tier), 2022-10). Later view: the 2022 one.
  • Training volume/frequency: 2020-2022, 6-7 days/week, 2-3 h, volume is king (Fullbody template review, 2021-01; Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02). 2024, less volume, less frequency, more intensity, 5 days/week; his first-year programs were too high in volume and frequency (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Final program: 2021, "final program" to run indefinitely (How to program your training yourself, 2021-02; Alpha/Beta testing your program, 2021-05). 2022, there is no final program because the body evolves forever (𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐈𝐬 𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐖𝐞 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭, 2022-10). In 2023 he no longer liked much of his original novice program (ULTIMATE HYPERTROPHY PROGRAMS (Novice to Advanced), 2023-06).
  • Rigidity and rest: 2021, antsy after a few rest days, cannot go 2 days without lifting (The Educated Barbarian： Meditations analysis (part. 9), 2021-02; Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07). 2024, balanced, can take a week off or move sessions for family (I was a Gymcel (and it made me miserable), 2024-01). He still needs daily activity (carries on rest days) (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12).
  • Crash-cut interpretation: 2020, he lost mostly water and muscle (Recomp guide (part.1)： What it is & isn't, 2020-05; What NOT to do during a cut, 2020-02). 2021-2022, the 30 lb lost was almost all fat (Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11; Don't fall for the bulking meme, 2022-11). The later view is the 2021-22 one.
  • Monetization: 2020-2021, he would never make money from the channel (Natural Q&A #3, 2020-10; The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01). 2023+, funded by Ko-fi pledges as a second job; still no ads or sponsors (The Natty FREAK with Superhero Aesthetics (Bald Omni-Man), 2023-06; How to get buff GF (Dating & Relationships Q&A), 2024-11).
  • Coaching: 2020/2024, refuses to coach (The Educated Barbarian： Hagakure analysis (part. 3), 2020-07; You weren't chosen by God. Now what?, 2024-06). 2025, coaches ~30+ people in the School of Strategy (3 hours of Story Time, 2025-02).
  • Bench/pressing: 2020, loves bench and built his chest with it (Road to a bigger chest, 2020-01). 2023, quit benching for dips and push-ups and calls dropping push-ups for bench a mistake (HELP! I'm getting too BIG (Hypertrophy Log #5), 2023-11; These Lifts BUILT My Physique (Top 10 Hypertrophy List), 2023-02).
  • Bodyweight goal: 2020-2022, maintain ~210 and recomp (Greg Doucette's MainGaining is keeping you small?! (Analyzing Revival Fitness Ex, 2022-01). 2022-2024, slow bulk to 220 and maintain; in 2024 he wants to be "too big for doors" (Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12).

Contradictions

  • Own program vs others' plans: 2020, he "has never followed someone else's program" (Free novice program for hypertrophy, 2020-02; Why I talk about programming and what you can get from it, 2020-03). 2022, after finding YouTube Fitness "he followed others' plans", growth stopped, and he ran a YouTube-style machine/20-rep program for months (5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09; The Great MOGGING of Bodybuilding： How Strength Came to DOMINATE Fitness, 2022-02).
  • Never >1 week off since 14 vs a lost year: 2024, he has never gone more than a week without training since 14 (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). 2023, after university rejections he played LoL 10 h/day and stopped training for a year (Mountain Training Arc (100K SPECIAL), 2023-08). 2020 adds breaks and skipped periods (No one trains for 10 years, 2020-03).
  • Start age/weight: 14 at 100 lb (STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08; My philosophy regarding abs training, 2020-03); 15 at 110 lb (10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04); 15 at 120 lb (Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01).
  • Teen height: 110 lb at 6 ft (Generation Aesthetics： Zyzz, the Godfather of Terrible Role Models, 2021-12) and 140 lb at 6 ft at 18 (10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04); but under 5 ft at 14 (STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08), 5'5" at 14 (You weren't chosen by God. Now what?, 2024-06), ~5'2" until 15 (Stop Manlet Hate (A Message to Short Men), 2023-03).
  • Bodyweight at 22: 200-205 lb (10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs), 2020-04) vs 220 lb (180→220 from 20-22) (Natural Hypertrophy： my lifting history, 2020-01).
  • Timing of the 240-lb peak: ~4 years before 2021, i.e. 2017 (Crazy bulks： secret for INSANE gains?, 2021-11); 2018-2019 (Recomp guide (part.1)： What it is & isn't, 2020-05; The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04). In 2020 he said he had been recomping ~1.5 years at ~215 (What NOT to do during a cut, 2020-02), yet in 2025 recalled 110 kg in Dec 2019 (3 hours of Story Time, 2025-02).
  • Crash-cut duration: ~1 month (Recomp guide (part.1)： What it is & isn't, 2020-05) vs ~5 months (What NOT to do during a cut, 2020-02).
  • Competing (2024): he won't compete because he won't lose weight (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12), yet will "someday" cut to 180-190 lb to compete (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Bench in 2022: "benching 255 lb" (The Great MOGGING of Bodybuilding： How Strength Came to DOMINATE Fitness, 2022-02) vs bench best 325 lb two months later (Strength standards are useless, 2022-04). Possibly current working weight vs all-time best.
  • Recomp start BF: 17-18% (Nutrition Q&A #2, 2021-04) vs 18-19% (Building Muscles AND Losing Fat WITHOUT Gaining Weight? (My Best Recomp Lessons), 2022-08).
  • Video-game quit age: ~21 (Natural Q&A #6, 2021-03); 18-19 (Why you should stop playing videogames, 2022-04); ~11 years before 2024, i.e. ~18 (TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09).

Progression

Changed over time

  • When to add weight: Jan 2020: on 4×12, go up only if all four sets of 12 are comfortable (Free 3 times a week full body hypertrophy program, 2020-01). From Aug 2020 on: waiting for every set to hit the top turns ERRs static (When to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-08), and by 2024 only one set must reach the top (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). Later view: first set at the ceiling.
  • Narrow low ranges: 2020 he prescribed 4-6 often (4×4-6 pull-ups/dips, 3×4-6 squat) (2 days Upper (Torso/Arm dominant) split program review, 2020-04; Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05). 2023-25: keep ≥4 reps between floor and ceiling, and 4-6 is "a recipe for plateaus" (How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03). Later view: wider ranges.
  • Very low reps: 2020 elevator schemes of 2-5 reps on deadlift and OHP (How to progress forward with evolving rep ranges, 2020-09). 2022: compounds never below 4 (Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10); 2023: sub-5 sets ~5% of volume (Giants DO Exist (Tom Haviland), 2023-12).
  • Isolation ranges: 2020: 3×6-10 "great" for isolation (AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03). 2024: 6-10 too low, use 8-12/10-15 (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10). Exceptions remain for hard curls (6-12, 6-10 in 2023-25) (The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03).
  • Evolving sets: 2020 he hadn't introduced evolving set ranges because removing both limits removes structure (Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07), and 2021 he called them advanced tools that destabilize programs (How to use Evolving Rep Ranges for Hypertrophy, 2021-10). 2022-24: they are standard in his programs (add a set, then weight, drop a set) (Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Final program: 2021: his "final program" no longer changes (STORY TIME： My entire training history, 2021-08; How to program your training yourself, 2021-02). 2022: no final program exists because the body keeps evolving, and he admits he pushed the idea earlier (🌌5 BIG BRAIN TRAINING TIPS TO 🆄🅽🅵🆄🅲🅺 YOUR PROGRAM🧠, 2022-05; 5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting, 2022-09).
  • Rest-pause: 2021: an afterthought that complicates rep/set manipulation (The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03; The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03). 2024-25: a recommended plateau-buster for isolation (Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04; 10 years of lifting for this (Hypertrophy Log #10), 2025-01).
  • Microloading: 2020: avoid microplates unless really advanced (Weight progression on evolving rep ranges, 2020-07). 2021-22: use ~2 lb jumps for arms; microloading is good for presses (Good arm day Vs Bad arm day, 2021-01; Hypertrophy Q&A #10, 2022-06).
  • Tempo: 2020: slower tempo listed as an overload method (Should bodybuilders care about strength?, 2020-02). 2021-24: tempo is hard to track and should be standardised, not progressed (The hypertrophy series： the most reliable way to progressively overload, 2021-03; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12).
  • Rep goals vs RIR: 2020: the rep-goal system is excellent (Rep Goal System (by Steve Shaw of Massive Iron) review, 2020-07). 2021: he prefers RIR for clearer brackets (Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03). 2023: autoregulation with RIR chosen on the day is "S tier" (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11).
  • Can plateaus be avoided: 2021: "fully avoidable" with smart programming (The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07). 2023: plateaus can't be avoided, so aim for fewer and later ones (How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07).
  • Weight on the bar emphasis: 2020-21: the simplest, most reliable and best method (The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06; The hypertrophy series： the perfect progression scheme for muscle growth, 2021-08). 2022: weight is the "tip of the iceberg", and most natural gains come from accumulated volume via set multiplication and frequency (The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08; The Ten 𝐋𝐀𝐖𝐒 of HYPERTROPHY (that you MUST break to grow), 2022-08). 2024: his own obsession with bar weight created progression anxiety (The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04), yet you must eventually get stronger (Swinging a sword WON'T make you jacked, 2024-02). Later view: load is one lever among several, but it can't be dropped.
  • Adding a variation on a stall: 2020: never let a stall trigger rotation (Rotating lifts： What it should & shouldn't be, 2020-05). 2024: if a lift doesn't progress, move to another variation of the pattern, or add a variation when it stalls (Exercise Tier Lists are STUPID, 2024-11; Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04). The 2023 middle ground: only add a variation if you truly can't break the plateau (The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11).

Contradictions

  • Evolving ranges for novices: He says novices should not use them because they're hard to track and need beta-testing (Hypertrophy Q&A #4, 2020-12; The Best Science-Based Full Body Workout for Size and Strength by Jeremy Ethier , 2021-03), and that they are dangerous for lazy novices (The benefits of evolving rep ranges, 2020-05). He also says a program's 3-5×4-6 evolving scheme is "very intelligent" for novices (AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 1： training), 2020-03), novices can handle leeway (Candito Upper Lower Hypertrophy Program review, 2020-05), and ERRs for novices are good (The Best Science-Based Full Body Workout for Size and Strength by Jeremy Ethier , 2021-03). All of this is 2020-21 with no clear direction.
  • Order of overload levers (both Dec 2022): "weight, then reps, then sets, then frequency" (How the King of Zoomers Trains to Look like a Greek God (Alex Eubank Program Rev, 2022-12) vs "reps, then sets, then weight" (How to Get Bigger by Doing Less (The 85% Rule), 2022-12; ☣️ Biohacking Muscle Growth with Nucleus Overload 💪, 2022-03). The first probably ranks importance and the second gives the order of steps, but he states both as the way to progress.
  • 8-15 range: too wide, since if you can get 15 you'll get 12-13 (2020) (4 days Body parts split program review, 2020-10). Later he says hitting 15 lets you add ~10 lb and still get 8 (2023) (How to Keep Growing FOREVER (Unlimited Hypertrophy Method), 2023-07).
  • Body measurements: the worst way to judge progress (The hypertrophy series： the optimal measure of progression for muscle growth, 2020-10) and too slow to guide programming (The hypertrophy series： the optimal measure of progression for muscle growth, 2020-10) vs "the only reliable way to know if a muscle grew" (Why you will NEVER have freaky, thick forearms if your wrists are small (Natty o, 2021-02).
  • Stall tolerance: no lift should stagnate more than ~1 month (The hypertrophy series： promoting progression in your training, 2020-06) vs 4-5 months on a compound before the program is wrong (How to set up evolving rep ranges (theoretical aspects), 2020-06). Both are from June 2020.
  • Pull-up threshold for adding weight: 10 clean pull-ups (FREE 4 days Upper Lower sheiko inspired Bodybuilding Program, 2020-09; Everything I do to get HUGE (Split, Reps, Lifts), 2023-09) vs 15-20 pull-ups / 30 dips (Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09) vs 25 dips (So you think you look good? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-11) vs 30 pull-ups (3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11). The thresholds vary, but every version says to add load.

Rest periods

Changed over time

  • Rest length drifts shorter and looser. 2020: 3-5 min for strength sets (Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06). 2021-2024: 2-3 min, by feel, "rest times don't matter" as long as you recover (Doggcrapp Training review, 2021-01; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). This is a mild refinement; 3-4 min after giant-set rounds persists through 2024 (So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11).

Contradictions

  • Supersetting strength work. "Don't superset strength work such as main bench or weighted chins" (4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review, 2020-11; 5 days Upper Lower program review (Week 1), 2020-07), repeated in 2025 (low reps as straight sets with long rests) (New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03), vs "even strength work can be supersetted, e.g. bench with rows; resting 5 min after bench is wasted" (Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05).
  • Leg pairings. Pair leg press with leg curl and leg extension with calf raises (The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06), or lunges with skull crushers (Jeff Nippard & Minimalism： Working Hard or Hardly Working?, 2022-10), vs moving straight from one leg exercise to another being "a cardinal sin" (Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01). Probably same-region circuits vs paired isolation, but he doesn't make that distinction.
  • Does supersetting hurt performance? It is "not detrimental" and "costs nothing" (Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01; The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06) vs the loss growing in a long full-body day (Fullbody template review, 2021-01) and leg circuits destroying performance (Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01).

Science evidence

Changed over time

  • Stretch/eccentric versus concentric. 2020-2021: muscle is gained mostly via weighted stretch, the negative is the key, and weighted stretching is "now backed by studies" (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07; Natty or not (.com)： Alpha Destiny (part. 2), 2020-07). 2023-2024: he cites a ~100-man study where ~90° training outgrew lengthened-only. He calls the stretch-focused trend contrarian and believes the concentric builds more than the eccentric, proposing a partner-removes-the-negative experiment. He notes Milo Wolf says lengthened partials help only a little (Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01). The later view is current.
  • Rep range and load. 2020: some studies favour heavy weights, and heavy loads are needed for damage (The hypertrophy series： the issue of volume without intensity, 2020-05; The hypertrophy series： why using metabolic stress for muscle growth fails, 2021-02). 2025: rep range is "mostly dead" as long as you're close to failure (New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03). This is a refinement.

Contradictions

  • Physique as evidence. "Being bigger is not an argument" (The Brainlets of YT Fitness don't understand Science, 2021-02) versus judging knowledge by ability to replicate it and science people being small (Science-Based Fitness needs a reality check., 2023-07; The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01). Partly reconciled by his natural-only qualifier (Jeff Nippard is WRONG about Natty or Nots., 2023-08).
  • Uses studies while dismissing them. He never cites studies (The Galaxy Brains of YT Fitness have ruined science, 2021-01), yet he invokes specific studies when they support him (tempo, ROM, boxers, 500 mg testosterone, lengthened versus 90°) (New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01; Why you should STOP doing incline curls, 2023-02). This is close to the cherry-picking he criticises.

Sleep recovery

Changed over time

  • Active vs passive recovery. In 2020-2021, light blood-flow work, calisthenics and a busy rest day ("not a couch day") aided recovery ( (The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; Push Pull Legs Upper Lower 5 days split Program review, 2020-05; 3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11)). In 2024: "you do not need active recovery", constant active recovery keeps you fatigued, and couch rest matters ( (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05; Time to become indestructible (Self-Improvement Q&A), 2024-10)). Later view: passive rest, with light activity allowed.
  • His sleep target rose. He said 7 h in 2021 ( (Natural Q&A #7, 2021-05)) and 7-8 h in 2022 ( (🕑 OPTIMIZE YOUR LIFE 📈： Time Management, Productivity Hacks & Energy Budge, 2022-07)), then tried for 8-9 h in 2024 ( (Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12)). In 2025 he said hypertrophy training raises sleep need ( (You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01)).
  • Screens. In 2020 blue light didn't bother him and only susceptible people needed to avoid it ( (5 tips to sleep quick & deep, 2020-08)). In 2024 he said to ban screens ≥1.5 h before bed ( (How to get buff GF (Dating & Relationships Q&A), 2024-11)).
  • Forearm frequency. In 2020 a grip drill was every 4-6 days, never daily ( (How to do Coan grip, 2020-01)). In 2024 forearms recover fast enough for consecutive days with different curls ( (So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11)). Later view: more frequent.
  • Lower-body recovery lengthened. In 2022 he trained legs every 2 days without soreness ( (Level up your back, 2022-02)). In 2024 he needed 72 h+ and said lower body 3×/week is too much ( (Bodybuilding is killing me (Hypertrophy Log #8), 2024-09)).
  • Cold exposure de-emphasized. In 2020 he discussed it at length as useful for sleep and circulation ( (Cold showers benefits, 2020-06)). In 2024 he said it won't revolutionise recovery, and recovery is eating, sleeping and napping ( (You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05; You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05)).

Contradictions

  • Full recovery needed? In 2020: "training again before full recovery steals gains" ( (The hypertrophy series： modifying sessions frequency to control volume/intensity, 2020-09)). In 2021-2022: you can train at 20% or 90-95% recovery and still grow ( (The Recovery Pot Explained (a complete guide to muscle recuperation), 2021-02; Why I never deload (and why you shouldn't either), 2022-02)). The two can be reconciled only as "not constantly".
  • Triceps recovery speed. In 2020 his triceps recovered very fast ( (Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05)). In 2023 triceps take long to recover, especially if untrained ( (We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!, 2023-05)). The first is personal and the second general, so this is possibly not a real conflict.

Strength

Changed over time

  • Deadlift practice: 2020-21 he pushed the deadlift hardest with 2RMs and saw the most progress there (495x2 PR) (Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11; ⚠️ Don't make this mistake ⚠️, 2021-09). 2024: frequent max testing had stalled him at 465-485 for a year, so he now deadlifts every ~40 days with RDLs, good mornings and hypers doing the work (The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04; The WORST Bodybuilding Program Ever Created (my bad), 2024-04). Later view = low-frequency deadlifts, no max testing.
  • Strength blocks and powerbuilding: 2020 says most bodybuilding "is really powerbuilding", and 1-2 mesocycles of a powerlifting program to raise strength is "a good use" (Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06; The Bridge (by Austin Baraki & Jordan Feigenbaum ft Alan Thrall) Program review, 2020-07). 2022-24 rejects powerbuilding and strength blocks, and calls "build a strength base first" a lie (Tips to Avoid a Mediocre Physique, 2022-11; Powerbuilding Drama： The Final Answer, 2023-11; Powerbuilding is an Abomination., 2023-10). Later view = no strength phases for bodybuilders.
  • Size and strength moving apart: 2020 rejects that strength can rise while muscles shrink, saying size can't rise while strength stays flat (＂What is the point of lifting natty past 30 if test levels crash?＂, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： developing the values of size and strength, 2020-10). 2022 cites Candito losing size while his total rose and says you can trade one for the other (Strength standards are useless, 2022-04; Strength standards are useless, 2022-04). Later view = correlated within a person but tradeable.
  • Role of big-lift strength work: 2020-21 "a day with zero strength work is bad", strength work is the backbone, never cut (Kizen Strength & Aesthetics Powerbuilding program review, 2020-09; The hypertrophy series： utilizing tonnage for muscle growth, 2021-01). 2024-25: high-bar squat and bench only 3-5x/year, he "doesn't care about strength", and his heavy work moved to dips and weighted pull-ups (You know what time it is... STORY TIME, 2025-01; 3 hours of Story Time, 2025-02; Do you look better than Silver Era lifters? (Physique Review LIVE), 2024-12). Later view = strength via less risky movements, still trending up.
  • Neural window (refinement): "~6 months of weekly practice" (2020) (Strength training is for SUCKERS (Natty or not.com), 2020-07) → "a month to a year" (2021) (The hypertrophy series： pairing neurological adaptation and muscle gains, 2021-02).

Contradictions

  • OHP suitability: "a safe lift, you can even do 1-2 rep maxes" (Upper Lower Light/Heavy 4 days split with mirror Week program review (part. 1), 2020-12) vs "progresses too slowly and strains some lower backs" for daily maxing (Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02) (both 2020; different contexts, so a mild conflict).
  • 2RMs vs no maxing: he recommends never maxing and calls 1RMs a waste (5 reasons to only lift heavy weight DEBUNKED, 2021-01), while personally doing deadlift 2RMs and calling them hypertrophy training (The issue with Novice Programs, 2021-03). It is consistent only if 2RM ≠ 1RM.
  • Bench strictness: "Bench is the one lift you can get away with not treating as strict strength work" (5 days Upper Lower program review (part. 1), 2020-10) vs bench never below 4 reps, needing full focus and never supersetting (Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle), 2020-01) — yet he also allows bench and row supersets (3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part., 2020-11).

Supplements

Changed over time

  • Protein powder use: 2020 he used whey or pea for convenience (Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06). In 2021 he cut from 3x/day to ~2 scoops/week (TURKESTERONE / ECDYSTERONE MARKETING SCHEMES： How Supplements Companies TRICK yo, 2021-12). In 2023-24 he takes 1 scoop/day or 3-4x/week (Full Day of Eating (Lean Bulk), 2023-10; Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03), and in 2024 he says powder is "not worth the money" (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09).
  • Bee pollen: six months a year (2022) (Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03) → every day (2024) (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09).
  • Garlic dose: 3-6 cloves/day (2020, nutrition file) (Raw garlic for insane pumps & a stronger immune system, 2020-03) → 1-2 cloves every other day, starting at ½ clove (2023) (My Favorite ＂Anabolic Herbs＂ for Bodybuilding, 2023-05). The later view is the lower dose.
  • MSM: 1-2x/week (2020) (Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06) → daily and nonstop (2024) (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09; Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03).
  • Coffee: 2020-21 he called it an addiction and a sleep-wrecker (5 tips to sleep quick & deep, 2020-08; Nutrition Q&A #2, 2021-04). By 2024 he says to drink coffee instead of a pre-workout, and that one morning cup is a ritual, not an addiction (Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01; TIME TO GROW BOYS (Live Q&A / Self-Improvement), 2024-09). He still personally abstains.
  • His stack: creatine/MSM/bee pollen (2022) (Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03) → creatine/MSM/protein (2024) (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10). Garlic and ginger became his preferred "tonic herbs" from 2022-23 (Nutrition Q&A #3, 2022-03).

Contradictions

  • Vitamins. 2022: vitamin supplements are crutches a balanced diet removes, and vitamin D replaces sun (🥐 My New Diet for Natural Hypertrophy 🍖 (Vegan? Meat only?), 2022-07; SIGMA： Critiquing More Plates More Dates’ Testosterone Booster (feat Gorilla M, 2022-04). 2024: multivitamins and vitamin D are among the only four worth taking (Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01).
  • Dose. He says to take half the label dose of any supplement (Nutrition Q&A #1, 2020-11; TURKESTERONE / ECDYSTERONE MARKETING SCHEMES： How Supplements Companies TRICK yo, 2021-12), yet takes creatine above the label dose (Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03).
  • MSM frequency, same month (2020-06). About a teaspoon a day (Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 3)： Recovery hacks & supplements, 2020-06) vs once or twice a week (Supplements are (mostly) useless, 2020-06).
  • Whey. In 2024 it is one of the few worthwhile supplements (Judging and Grading every Fitness Channel (Sam Sulek, Max Euceda, Lex Little), 2024-01) and he still uses it (Everything I eat to get HUGE (Full Bulking Plan), 2024-03), but powder is also "not worth the money" (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09).

Technique

Changed over time

  • Cheating: 2020-2022 cheat reps are a legitimate tool; he did almost only cheat curls for ~10 years and biceps became his best part (Cheat curls tutorial (theoretical aspects), 2020-08; 13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS： Was it worth it?, 2022-05) → 2022 in hindsight strict curls would likely have given the same (13 YEARS OF CHEAT CURLS： Was it worth it?, 2022-05) → 2023 cheat reps C tier, "mostly wasteful" (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11) → 2024 cheat reps/body English = ego lifting (New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01). Later view: strict.
  • Scapula on back work: 2020-2021 retract the scapula, novices fail by not retracting on rows (Fierce 5 novice program review (from an hypertrophy standpoint), 2020-02; Jeff Nippard's Push Pull Legs program review, 2021-01) → 2024 protraction to stretch the back matters more; "shoulders back" is the wrong cue (Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04; Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04). (Pull-ups keep scapular engagement.) Later view: protract on rows.
  • Rounded back on rows/hinges: 2020 rounding as the weight descends on rows is bad form (Tips to combat lower back pain #1, 2020-02); he "never rounds his back" (Lower back rounding： The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, 2020-09) → 2024 rounded-back T-bar rows and deep rounded rack hinges at slow tempo are OK, earned exotic form (Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04; This is Peak Bulk (Hypertrophy Log #6), 2024-05; Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01). Lumbar rule for squat/deadlift unchanged.
  • Squat stance: 2020 slightly wider stance with knees out spares the knee (Curing patellar tendinitis (part. 2)： Rehab & precautions, 2020-05) → 2021-2024 narrow/medium stance, toes forward, knees forward; wide toes-out stance injured him (How to do squats for SIZE, 2022-09; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12).
  • Top squeeze: 2020 squeeze at the top (curls slow positive for the squeeze; Piana calf raises: squeeze matters more than stretch) (The training principles series： slow negatives, 2020-02; How to do Piana & Toshiki raises, 2020-01) → 2021-2024 top squeeze gives no tension, C/D tier; bottom of calf raise is where growth is (The form p＊lice is under arrest, 2021-07; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11).
  • Tempo emphasis: 2020 "slow negative, fast positive"; 2021 don't slow negatives on purpose, TUT overrated (The hypertrophy series： eccentric vs concentric movements, 2020-09; The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07) → 2023-2024 tempo S tier, slow down near the stretch, ≥1 s eccentric, negative "where most hypertrophy occurs" (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11; Training for Aesthetics： You're doing it WRONG., 2023-05; I am officially obese (Hypertrophy Log #7), 2024-08). Later view: more weight on controlled/slow negatives, still no counting.
  • Partials / lengthened partials: 2020 full ROM best, novices never partial (The training principles series： full range of motion, 2020-04; How to program for novices (with an hypertrophy bias), 2020-02) → 2021 full ROM all the time is a mistake (The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07) → 2023 partials A tier (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11) → 2024 lengthened partials may beat full ROM (New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01). Later view: full ROM default, lengthened-range emphasis.
  • Mind-muscle connection: 2020 central (prioritising muscles in compounds) (The training principle series： mind muscle connection, 2020-02) → 2021-2023 only useful for lagging muscles, B tier, can be an excuse for baby weights (5 lifting conspiracy theories, 2021-04; The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11).
  • Lat pulldown: 2020 V-bar to the stomach, lean back (Push/Pull Pull/Legs Legs/Push 3 days program review, 2020-05) → 2023-2024 don't lean way back, pull in line with the cable; leaning back is valid but he prefers vertical (This is why you don't have a Demon Back (Advanced Tips), 2023-11; Arnold trained like an idiot?, 2024-04).
  • Wall curls: 2021-2022 wall curls don't stop cheating (How to do curls (strict barbell curls tutorial), 2021-02; The ULTIMATE Biceps Exercises Tier-List (Arnold-tier to Noodle-tier), 2022-10) → 2024 wall curls reduce cheating and allow slower negatives (I am officially obese (Hypertrophy Log #7), 2024-08).
  • OHP minimum reps: 2020 ≥5 reps (Tips to combat shoulder pain, 2020-02) → 2022 never below 6, lower reps degraded his form (Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10).

Contradictions

  • Pristine form vs heavier sloppy reps: 2023 slight ego lifting with more weight and a better stretch "can be better" (I'm BACK! (Hypertrophy Log #4), 2023-08) vs 2023-2024 cutting ROM to lift more and body English are ego lifting (What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03; New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01).
  • Elbow flare on bench: 2020 flaring is objectively bad 100% of the time (The training principles series： good form, 2020-02; How to do high frequency/volume bench press without shoulder pain, 2020-02) vs 2022 flaring is how you recruit more chest (The ULTIMATE Chest Exercises Tier-List (Gorilla-tier to A cup-tier), 2022-12).
  • Lengthened partials: 2023 C tier, used only for calves (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11) vs 2024 may beat full ROM (New hypertrophy study just dropped (And Basically You're F＊cking Stupid), 2024-01) (possibly an update from new data, but only 3 months apart).
  • OHP range: prefers full ROM down to the collarbone (AlphaDestiny Novice Program review (part. 2： FAQ), 2020-04) vs "he doesn't use full ROM on overhead press either" (Response to Steve Shaw (Massive Iron) - Going to WAR Over FRONT DELT training, 2020-03) (both 2020).
  • Bench negative: slow negatives as philosophy (The hypertrophy series： eccentric vs concentric movements, 2020-09) vs on bench he lowers "fairly fast but controlled" since slow never helps his positive (The training principles series： slow negatives, 2020-02); cheat curls not deliberately slowed (Cheat curls： EZ bar vs Dumbbells, 2020-07).
  • Partials' purpose: high reps, not heavy weight (Synchronizing evolving rep range with movement patterns, variations & rotations , 2020-11) vs a good partial lets more reps with more weight (What everyone gets WRONG about Range of Motion, 2023-03).
  • Technique value: S tier (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11) vs "technique is the enemy of the bodybuilder" (The Streetlifting MUTANT w/ Steel Cable Tendons (Artem Shirokov), 2023-12) (reconcilable: master enough, no more).
  • Bodybuilder vs powerlifter form: "only form" exists (No such thing as a dangerous lift (the good morning example), 2021-04) vs optimal strength and bodybuilding form sit at opposite ends (You're not hardcore, you're just an idiot., 2024-05).

Volume

Changed over time

  • Overall volume, from maximalist to minimal-effective. 2020: more work always gives better results, sit at the brink of overtraining, and naturals can't build a big body in an hour a day (The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?, 2020-10). From 2021: do as little as possible for as much as possible (The hypertrophy series： the optimal number of sets for muscle growth, 2021-02; Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03). 2024: low on the volume spectrum, "closer to HIT than to 18-20 sets", and his earliest programs had far too many sets (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; 1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09). 2025: volume serves progression only (New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03). The later view is the minimal-effective one.
  • Sets per exercise. 2020: accessories almost always 4 sets, 2 not enough (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01). 2023: rule of three (2-4) (The Monster Natty that trains EVERY DAY (Geoffrey Verity Schofield), 2023-04). 2024-2025: 3 for novice/intermediate, 2 for advanced, 2 per taxing lift (So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11; New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡, 2025-03). Later = fewer.
  • His own training. 2020: 2-3 h sessions, 6 days/wk, responds to high volume (How I split up my week for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; Recomp guide (part. 3)： performance & body fat loss/distribution, 2020-06). 2023: prefers fewer quality sets made possible by high frequency (Leg Day + Bulk Update (Hypertrophy Log #2), 2023-07). 2024: chest 6/wk, arms 9 each, shoulders 9-12, legs 6+6 (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11). In 2020 he attributed his legs to hundreds of thousands of pounds of volume squats (Wisconsin method aka Bulgarian light review (from a muscular hypertrophy standpo, 2020-02).
  • Nucleus overload. 2020-2022: an advocated accessory method for nearly every body part he wanted to grow (Nucleus overload guide (part. 3)： my experience & sports applications, 2020-06; Greek Aesthetics Bodybuilding Program (Apollonian Physique Workout), 2022-05). 2023: D tier, 1-2% of results (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11).
  • Back-off/backup sets. 2020: "a must for hypertrophy… free tonnage" (The hypertrophy series： utilizing back-off sets to accumulate quality tonnage, 2020-10). 2023: B tier, better as a variation (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11). 2024: he skips them on dips and on non-priority squats (Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • Finishers. 2021: fine, they build work capacity (The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07). 2023: D tier, junk volume or active recovery at best (The Most IMPORTANT Methods for Muscle Growth (Hypertrophy Tier-List), 2023-11).
  • Leg volume. 2020: at least 11-12 heavy squats per squat day, plus giant-set finishers (My sets/frequency for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-01; How I program my Squat days for Natural Hypertrophy, 2020-02). 2022-2024: legs respond to minimalism; 3 sets each of a quad and a hinge movement; 6+6 weekly sets (Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01; Hypertrophy Q&A #9, 2022-01; How I Built Monster Legs, 2024-12).
  • High reps. 2020: high ranges fine for isolation, pump work up to 50, face pulls 15-20 "never enough" (Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06; Upper Body dominant 4 Days split review, 2020-06; Upper Body focused 5 days PPL + sprints program review, 2020-09). 2021-2023: stay at 2-12 with few sets near 15, above 15 risks junk, never below 6 on accessories (The hypertrophy series： bypassing muscular endurance thresholds, 2021-01; Come with me if you want big shoulders (JOIN THE CHALLENGE!), 2022-10; Come with me if you want massive arms (Step by Step MASSterplan), 2023-01).
  • Junk-volume framing. 2021: the concept is "overblown" and junk is only bad if it replaces hard sets (The Hypertrophy Iceberg Explained (a complete guide to muscle growth), 2021-07). 2022-2024: he applies the label widely and calls for the "bare effective minimum" (Good chest day vs Bad chest day, 2022-05; This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD), 2024-06).
  • Session-length philosophy. 2020: advanced lifters must lengthen sessions (Hypertrophy Q&A #3, 2020-11). 2021: as short as possible, 1h15 target (The hypertrophy series： determining the optimal workout length, 2021-01; Viking's the Bare Bones Series Program review, 2021-03). 2024: don't train to a clock, 45-60 min of hard sets exhausts most (Don't be THAT GUY in 2024, 2024-01).

Contradictions

  • Maximalist vs near-HIT, both in 2024. He calls maximalist whole-body isolation the best, with the last 20% mattering for advanced lifters (1st Natural Hypertrophy stream! ASK YOUR QUESTIONS AND I SHALL ANSWER, 2024-09), yet also places himself closer to HIT and says most could cut 20-30% (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review), 2024-10).
  • 20 weekly sets. 2022: almost no one needs 16-20 and 20/wk is impractical (How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07; How often should you train for 𝐁𝐎𝐃𝐘𝐁𝐔𝐈𝐋𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 , 2022-07). 2023: back caps reach 20-28 and he runs 20 back and 18 shoulder sets (Come with me if you want a BIG BACK (4 steps MASSterplan), 2023-09; The ULTIMATE PPL Program (Doom Slayer Physique), 2023-11). Partly explained by the back's tolerance.
  • Isolation vs compound share. 2023: about 2:1 isolation:compound per muscle (Why spamming lateral raises won't work, 2023-12). 2024: compounds should be the bulk of a program (Why you shouldn't listen to Genetic Freaks (The Joel Williams Example), 2024-02).
  • Deadlift sets (2020-2022). 1x5 is "good for strength not hypertrophy, prefer 3x3" (4 days Upper Lower split Program review, 2020-04), vs 1x5 is "great" and enough (Icecream Fitness Program review, 2020-06; Icecream Fitness FAQ review, 2020-06). 2021: 3x5 is too much (The Smartest Push Pull Legs Routine by Jeff Nippard review, 2021-06), vs 2022: deadlifts only need 3x5 (Can you look like Zodd from Berserk in real life? (ANIME WORKOUTS), 2022-10).
  • Supersetting squats/deadlifts (2020). He will never superset them (5 days Upper Lower (2 Uppers 2 Lowers + 1 Arm day) program review, 2020-10), yet he giant-sets even lower-body lifts (FREE 4 days Body Parts split for Intermediates, 2020-06). 2022 refines this: pair squats only with unrelated small muscles (Going to WAR over Giant Sets (Response to Bald Omni Man), 2022-09).
  • Calves/abs. "You can never train abs or calves too much" (BLOW UP your ARMS with these 3 GIANT sets (Biceps/Triceps/Forearms), 2022-09), vs 6 sit-up sets is too much and two ab isolations are redundant (BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions), 2024-09; So you think you can lift? (Program Review LIVE), 2024-11).
  • Can extra sets hurt? 2020/2022: one or two extra sets won't stop progress (The hypertrophy series： maximum recoverable volume, 2020-04; Mike Mentzer： Mustachioed fraud or Bodybuilding genius? (🆃🅷🅴 🅷🅸, 2022-08), vs 2021: too much volume can stop a muscle growing (glued-chair analogy) (Hypertrophy Q&A #7, 2021-05).

Appendix B. Glossary

NH's own vocabulary and the training jargon used in this book, defined as he uses it, with pointers to the principles where each term does its work.

  • 1/2/3/4-plate standard — The idea that a trained man should bench 1 plate, squat 2 and so on; NH says it roughly fits novices because the loads are low, but leverages make fixed numbers meaningless after that. See STR-59, STR-57.
  • 85% rule — His step-loading rule: build reps and sets at a weight until it feels like about 70% effort, then add weight to get back to about 85%, trim sets or reps, and rebuild. It deliberately does not maximise strength, so volume can accumulate. See PRG-48, STR-29.
  • 543 (elevator) scheme — A ladder for heavy deadlifts and overhead press: keep the weight, climb sets and reps up the ladder, then add weight and restart at the bottom. See PRG-43.
  • Ab anxiety — Clinging to a skinny six-pack and refusing to gain weight; a form of "small guy syndrome" that keeps lifters small. See BLK-87.
  • Absolute intensity — What you can move fresh and warmed up. Contrast relative intensity, which climbs through each set and session as fatigue builds. See INT-09, INT-10, VOL-04.
  • Accidental physique — The look you get from strength-only or compound-only training without aesthetic intent: big trunk and quads, small arms. See AES-02, AES-30.
  • Adherence — Sticking with a program. He puts it at the top of the muscle-building pyramid: a lift or program you enjoy beats a "better" one you skip. See MND-14, BEG-73, PRG-117.
  • AMRAP — "As many reps as possible." He keeps it for finishers and unweighted calisthenics, never for loaded top sets or deadlifts. See INT-59, INJ-76.
  • Anabolic bank — His image for how naturals grow: long, stable exposure to their own hormones over years, as opposed to the flat, permanently high levels of an injector. See NAT-17, GEN-57.
  • Anabolic window — The supposed post-workout deadline for protein; he calls it a protein-powder marketing tactic. See NUT-36, IND-11.
  • Apollonian vs Herculean — Two branches of the Greek ideal: Apollonian is wide shoulders and lats, small waist, smaller legs, low fat; Herculean (Farnese) is thicker waist, big limbs, legs and core. He prefers the Herculean. See AES-20.
  • Arm day — A low-CNS day of a few upper compounds then arm isolation; earned once legs are trained twice a week, optional, and able to double as active recovery. See FRQ-66, FRQ-67, ARM-37.
  • Artificial failure — A set ended by cardio, burn, pump, occlusion or a structural breakdown rather than by the target muscle; it feels hard but builds little. See INT-25, TEC-16.
  • Autoregulation — Adjusting the day's work to how you are recovering. It needs rotation options built into the program and regulation skill first, so it suits advanced lifters. See FAT-16, PRG-116.
  • Back-off sets — Sets after the opening strength work, tied to its weight and still pushed near failure; usually 2-3 of the same pattern with a modest drop. See INT-50, VOL-51, PRG-84.
  • Bear mode — His term for the thick, Herculean look: big limbs, waist, legs, upper back and traps. See AES-20, AES-39.
  • Berserker physique — His personal ideal: massive arms, forearms and legs slightly out of proportion with the trunk, a strong core, developed upper back and smaller shoulders. See AES-21.
  • Big ten — The bare-minimum list of lifts that together cover every body part and the six size patterns. See EXS-09.
  • Bigorexia — Muscle dysmorphia, the "I am too small" feeling; he says every lifter meets it, himself included. See MND-87, MND-88, JRN-72.
  • Blackpill — Demoralised fatalism about genetics or natural potential; he calls it an excuse for passivity and a self-fulfilling prophecy. See MND-76, NAT-73, PHI-113.
  • Body English — Using torso movement to finish a rep. Acceptable in small doses on heavy back rows, not on isolation work. See TEC-67, TEC-64.
  • Bracing — A normal nose breath and tightening the abs as if about to be punched, holding the spine position through the rep; it matters mainly on heavy squats and deadlifts. See TEC-30.
  • Bridge program — A transition program between low-volume novice training and high-volume intermediate training, because "an advanced program must be earned". See VOL-39, BEG-64.
  • Bro split — One muscle per day, once a week. He calls it the worst template for naturals: too little frequency, too much per-session volume. See FRQ-37, NAT-28.
  • Bulk-cut purgatory — Yo-yoing the same 10-20 lb up and down forever with no real progress. See BLK-78, BLK-79.
  • Bulking hypnosis — "Size goggles" that hide fat gain on a bulk; the cut-side version is "lean goggles". Checking the mirror as often as the scale counters it. See BLK-35.
  • Cheerleader effect — One outstanding muscle makes the weaker ones around it look better. See AES-27.
  • CNS fatigue — Nervous-system fatigue; he says most people can't reach real CNS burnout, and strength loss blamed on it is usually diet, sleep or stress. See FAT-27, FAT-28, FAT-29.
  • Compounds and isolation ("shotgun and sniper") — Compounds supply most of the tonnage, isolation covers what they miss; neither works alone. See EXS-01, EXS-02, EXS-08.
  • Crabs in the bucket — People who ridicule and pull you down because your progress removes their excuses. See MND-77, PHI-50.
  • Danger rep — The last grinding rep on a heavy squat, deadlift or variation, which he leaves in the tank. See INT-33, INT-28.
  • Deload — A planned week of reduced training. For bodybuilders he calls scheduled deloads unnecessary, an emergency response to a programming mistake. See FAT-01, FAT-03, FAT-04.
  • Dirty bulk — Gaining with junk food and a big surplus; he says it adds mostly fat and leverage, and his own was "wasted years". See BLK-41, JRN-14.
  • Educated barbarian — His ideal of the lifter who develops body and mind together and arrives at the gym knowing exactly what to do. See MND-18, PHI-01.
  • Ego lifting — Using more weight than the exercise can turn into a justified stimulus, including cutting range to lift more; he notes the label is often thrown as an insult. See TEC-19, MND-68.
  • Evolving rep ranges — His core progression method: a fixed rep range per lift, start near the bottom, add reps, add weight when the first set hits the ceiling, stay in the range. See PRG-20, PRG-21, INT-46.
  • Evolving sets — Progressing the number of sets inside a narrow span (usually 2-4): add a set when the top set tops the range, then add weight and drop a set. See PRG-26, VOL-52.
  • Fake natty — Someone who uses PEDs while claiming to be natural; he says their real crime is killing trust that naturals can grow. See NAT-74, IND-38.
  • Failure — The point where no further clean rep is possible; the set ends as soon as body English is needed. Only failure where the target muscle is the limit counts. See INT-26, INT-25, INT-27.
  • FFMI — Fat-free mass index; he calls it worthless for judging natural status. See NAT-58.
  • Fishing-rod deadlift — Knees locking early with a rounded back, so the back finishes the lift and the lifter struggles past the knees. See TEC-99, JRN-60.
  • Frame — Clavicle width, waist, hips and joint size; it sets potential width and how muscle looks, and can't be trained. See AES-62, GEN-36, GEN-37.
  • Frequency — How often a muscle or pattern is trained; the pillar of the trinity he says naturals ignore most. See FRQ-01, FRQ-04, NAT-29.
  • Fridge physique — A thick trunk and back with no width or V-taper, typically from deadlift-only back training. See BAK-04, AES-02.
  • Frog physique — Big legs on a small upper body, from PR-driven, squat-heavy or powerlifting training. See AES-55, STR-64.
  • Gentleman split — His favourite template: an upper/lower skeleton whose days are built around synergistic muscle groups and a main compound, with flexible boundaries. See FRQ-38, FRQ-43.
  • Giant set — Four or more exercises back to back; 4-5 is the sweet spot, ordered from most to least intense, and they double as a bodybuilder's conditioning. See RST-14, RST-15, CAR-21.
  • GOMAD — "A gallon of milk a day"; he calls it idiotic, an uncontrolled surplus of milk fat and protein. See NUT-87, BLK-43.
  • Good-morning squat — The cardinal squat fault: hips rise first, the squat turns into a good morning and the lower back takes the load instead of the quads. See TEC-109, TEC-33.
  • GPP — General physical preparedness. For a bodybuilder, mostly supersets and giant sets of non-interfering moves plus carries and similar low-cost work. See CAR-21, CAR-27.
  • Grease the groove — Very frequent submaximal practice of one movement; he allows it for pull-ups as an exception but blames highly repetitive Big-3 versions for novice injuries. See FRQ-26, INJ-53.
  • Gym look — Looking like you lift in everyday clothes, relaxed. He says a relatively lean 200 lb already reads as trained, and it takes years before people notice. See AES-60, AES-66, AES-79.
  • Gymcel — Someone who isolates in the gym believing a better body fixes everything; NH describes a "gymcel phase" of his own. See MND-96, JRN-70.
  • Hard set — A set with a challenging load that ends at muscular failure and is repeatable within 2-3 days; he wants as much tonnage as possible to come from hard sets. See INT-40, INT-41, INT-32.
  • Hard vs soft variation — A soft variation keeps the pattern and changes implement, grip, pause or range (near-full carryover); a hard variation is a different pattern and a new skill, so cap it. See EXS-15, EXS-17.
  • Hardgainer — The supposed person who can't gain; he says there are no true hardgainers, only people who don't eat or train enough. See GEN-03, NUT-85, BLK-52.
  • HIT — High-intensity training, one set to failure with long gaps (Mentzer); he says it is right about intensity but far too little volume for naturals. See INT-62, VOL-12.
  • Holy trinity of fake-natty nonsense — His name for three ideas he says come from enhanced lifters: volume without an intensity window, avoiding compounds, and not understanding frequency. See NAT-25.
  • Intermediate hell — The stage after novice gains where precise programming is needed and many lifters stall for years; "intermediate syndrome" is crashing by jumping straight to high volume. See JRN-26, VOL-39, MND-73.
  • Junk volume — Work outside a relevant intensity window: unchallenging loads, pump chasing and sets ended by cardio rather than the muscle. It hurts most when it replaces hard sets. See VOL-07, VOL-08, VOL-09.
  • Lengthened partials — Partial reps in the stretched part of the range. He says they may work and in 2024 likely beat full range, but finds them hard to standardise and prefers rest-pause. See INT-58, TEC-52.
  • Liquid tonnage — His term for PEDs: each injection works like weeks of training. See NAT-16.
  • Maingaining — He calls it a rebranded lean bulk and prefers "lean bulk" or "recomp". See BLK-88.
  • Mechanical failure — The set ends because your structure (thoracic extension, setup, technique) gives out before the muscle, so tonnage stops reaching the target. See TEC-15, TEC-16, INJ-07.
  • Microloading — Adding very small increments (microplates) to extend linear progression, especially on small muscles and presses; it also stalls eventually. See PRG-58, PRG-59.
  • Milo paradox — Load-only progression is "designed to fail" because the ability to add weight outpaces recovery. See PRG-12.
  • Mind-muscle connection — Prioritising the target muscle within a lift so stronger muscles don't take the work; useful for muscles that won't grow, no excuse for baby weights. See TEC-68, TEC-69, TEC-70.
  • Mirror days — A/B days with the same emphasis but different lifts, rep ranges or order, to reduce boredom and overuse. See FRQ-75, FRQ-56.
  • MRV (maximum recoverable volume) — The most work you can recover and grow from; individual, found by experiment and rising with training age. He aims between medium volume and MRV. See VOL-16, SLP-30.
  • Muscle memory — Lost muscle comes back faster than it was first built; real, but not magic. See SCI-48, NAT-02.
  • Natty-or-not — Content judging whether people are natural; he says it mostly hurts viewers by lowering standards and pushing beginners toward PEDs. See NAT-60, IND-48.
  • Natural ("natty") — Never having taken PEDs, including TRT; take them once and you can never be natural again. See NAT-51, NAT-46.
  • Natural limit — The claimed point where a natural stops growing. He calls it "a cultural limit, not a biological one": progress slows but continues if weight, volume and intensity keep rising. See GEN-11, GEN-12, GEN-13.
  • Noble natty — A natural who takes pride in building a big, strong body naturally, not merely in being natural. See NAT-71.
  • Noob gains — Fast early gains; he treats them as a quantity of development (about half your potential), not a time window that closes. See BEG-04, GEN-17, GEN-60.
  • Novice — A lifter still on session-to-session linear progression; the stage ends when that stops, or when you want to and can write your own program, not at a strength standard. See PRG-93, BEG-06, BEG-07.
  • Novice syndrome — Overdoing it as a beginner, the main reason novices crash; burnout is over-stimulation, not lack of potential. See BEG-71, BEG-16.
  • Nucleus overload (NO) — Frequent, high-volume, very light work kept easy enough to repeat, complementing strength work for a muscle; the one exception to intensity windows. Later rated minor. See VOL-55, FAT-52, SCI-35.
  • Otter mode — The lean, athletic, not-too-big look (Fight Club Brad Pitt) most women pick; staying there means never getting really strong or fully big. See AES-73, STR-17, GEN-37.
  • Overtraining — Real but relative to the program; he says it is mostly coming back under-rested, and most "overtrained" lifters answered regression with more volume. See FAT-58, FAT-59, FAT-60.
  • Pain valley — The window between inactive moderate pain and acute pain where he trains an irritated area to widen the pain-free range. See INJ-35.
  • Power coper / strength coper — A lifter who hides poor muscle gains behind strength numbers or claims "the best way to get big is to get strong". See MND-64, STR-66.
  • Powerbuilding — Heavy big-three work plus lazy isolation; he calls it a marketing term that delivers neither size nor strength. See STR-63, IND-58.
  • Progressive overload — Something must go up for the muscles to go up: load, reps, sets, frequency, rest, variation or range. Non-negotiable. See PRG-01, PRG-11.
  • Pull-push-legs — His order for a PPL split, so pull day's hinges and rows don't fatigue the legs right before squats. See FRQ-40, FRQ-41.
  • Pump — The swollen feeling from fast, light reps; a by-product, not a growth signal. See INT-54, SCI-28.
  • Recomp — Training hard at roughly maintenance so the body trades fat for muscle; slow but real, needs fat to trade, and needs at least a year. See BLK-54, BLK-55, BLK-57.
  • Recovery pot — His model of recovery as a tub whose size is your MRV: take only part of it each session, keep it relatively full, never empty. See SLP-30, FRQ-07, SLP-31.
  • Red zone — The disadvantaged part of a rep, usually where the negative turns into the positive; it stimulates most and is where injuries happen. Enter it with care, don't avoid it. See TEC-22, INJ-04.
  • Relevant intensity window — The load range where volume actually counts (roughly 60-95% of 1RM); tonnage outside it is junk. See VOL-02, INT-15.
  • Rest-pause — His preferred intensity technique: at failure, rest briefly, then add reps that must be the hardest of the set. See INT-56, INT-55.
  • RIR (reps in reserve) — Reps left in the tank at the end of a set. He uses it on heavy, risky, low-rep work and says you must learn real failure first. See INT-34, INT-35, INT-36.
  • Rotation — Alternating close variations in one slot (week A / week B) to fight overuse and accommodation; never because a lift stalled. See EXS-17, EXS-21, FRQ-76.
  • RPE — Rating of perceived exertion; with percentages and RIR, an "A-tier" tool he doesn't use himself. See INT-37, INT-36.
  • Sandbagging — Giving less than full effort without a reason. Chosen sandbagging (warm-ups, planned RIR) is fine; sandbagging forced by a fixed scheme wastes quality tonnage. See INT-44, INT-45, INT-38.
  • Schrödinger's genetics — Before working you can't know your potential; those who stick with it get called gifted, those who quit get called low-T. See GEN-06, NAT-61.
  • Selective failure — Taking isolation, presses, rows and other low-risk lifts to failure, while keeping 1-2 reps in reserve on squats, deadlifts and good mornings. See INT-28, INT-39.
  • SFR (stimulus-to-fatigue ratio) — How much growth stimulus a lift gives for the fatigue it costs. He calls it overrated as an excuse to avoid compounds, but relevant where fatigue lands on tendons and stabilisers. See FAT-22, FAT-24.
  • Shelf muscles — Delts, traps and upper chest, the muscles that give the "bodybuilder look". See AES-37.
  • Skinny-fat — Low muscle with some fat; he calls it metabolic distress, not a body type, and says to recomp at maintenance rather than cut. See BLK-05.
  • Skinny pack — Abs that only show because the person is skinny, as opposed to trained abs that stay visible at higher body fat. See ABS-02.
  • Specificity tree — His early way of organising lifts: movement-pattern branches topped by a king lift fed by lower lifts. Later rated C tier for bodybuilding. See EXS-39.
  • Spider physique — A big torso on spaghetti arms, from programs that neglect arm isolation. See AES-30, ARM-39.
  • Static (fixed) schemes — Fixed sets and reps such as 5x5 or 4x10; they force sandbagging and can only progress by adding weight. Fine for novices and as deliberate tools. See PRG-51, PRG-52, PRG-53.
  • Step loading — Adding stimulus as reps first, then sets, then frequency, then weight, always in small steps. See PRG-14, PRG-48.
  • Strength restoration — Tiny band or light exercises for problem tendons, supersetted between sets of main lifts at almost no recovery cost. See INJ-63.
  • Strength work — The 1-3 heavy opening sets of a session: the "lighthouse" that drives progression while being a minority of the tonnage. Never supersetted. See PRG-83, STR-21, VOL-41.
  • Superset — Exercises back to back with no planned rest, then rest after the round. He supersets accessory and isolation work for different or antagonist muscles. See RST-13, RST-09, RST-10.
  • Technical rating — How much practice a lift takes to master and keep; high-rated lifts are "jealous" and decay without constant practice. See TEC-74, TEC-75.
  • Tonnage — Reps x weight accumulated over time; "tonnage is king" as long as it sits in a relevant intensity window. See VOL-02, PRG-02, VOL-06.
  • Tonnage sacrifice — Deliberately holding strength work steady while pushing volume or a secondary lift; not a plateau. See PRG-80.
  • Top set — The first and heaviest working set of a lift; only it needs to reach the top of the range before you add weight. See PRG-21, PRG-47.
  • Trinity (volume, intensity, frequency) — The three variables he treats as one system and the main drivers of hypertrophy; push one while ignoring the others and the system breaks. See VOL-01, SCI-25, FAT-15.
  • TRT — Testosterone replacement therapy. He says any exogenous hormone revokes natural status, real TRT is rare, and clinics use it as a gateway. See NAT-46, NAT-47, NAT-48.
  • V-taper — Width from shoulders, lats and serratus over a small waist; without lats you get a T-taper. See AES-36, BAK-21.
  • Weighted stretch — Loading a muscle in its lengthened position; he calls it underused, and the way traps and forearms grow from heavy holds. See TEC-89, BAK-35, FOR-04.
  • Widowmaker — A high-effort squat set he treats, like burnouts, as an occasional tool rather than regular programming; also the last phase of his knee rehab ladder. See INT-60, INJ-81.
  • Work capacity — The ability to do and recover from the volume that drives growth; built and lost gradually. Novices lack it more than they lack recovery. See VOL-38, BEG-15, CAR-02.

Appendix D. FAQ

The questions viewers asked most often in NH's Q&As, merged and answered from the principles in this book.

Volume and intensity

How many sets per muscle per week should I do?

A weekly set count means little on its own, and ±1-2 sets don't matter. If you need a number, 8-14 hard sets per muscle per week; at three sessions a week and high intensity, 9-15 is enough to keep growing. Almost no one needs 16-20. → VOL-19, VOL-20, VOL-22

How do I know if my volume is too high or too low?

Lingering soreness or failing to repeat last session's performance means too much; if you are doing high weekly sets with slow strength gains, try less volume and more intensity. No progress means either too little stimulus or too much. When unsure, err slightly high but add conservatively. → VOL-17, FAT-61, VOL-14

Is one set to failure (HIT) enough?

No. Mentzer was right to focus on intensity but went too far: one set every 6-8 days is too little for a natural. Both extremes fail; naturals grow in the middle, with several hard sets. → INT-62, VOL-12

Should I train to failure?

Take isolation, upper-body presses, rows and other low-risk lifts to failure; keep 1-2 reps in reserve on squats, deadlifts and good mornings. Failure is a calibration tool, not the goal, and you should never actually miss a rep. → INT-28, INT-30, INT-27

When should I use reps in reserve?

On low-rep work and heavy, risky compounds, where the last grinding reps aren't worth the risk; 0-1 RIR on 10-20-rep sets is pointless. RIR only means something once you have trained to failure many times, so learn failure first. → INT-34, INT-35, INT-36

What rep range builds muscle?

Intensity isn't tied to a rep range. Bodybuilding work sits mostly at 6-12 within an overall 3-15; choose 6-10, 8-12 or 10-15 by preference and by what lets you progress. Low reps build size too. → INT-12, INT-17, INT-22

Are sets of 20+ reps worth doing?

Rarely. Above about 15-20 reps each extra rep adds little intensity, and cardio, burn or technique stop you before the muscle does. → INT-18, INT-17

How long should I rest between sets?

About 2-3 minutes, never more than 5: as little as possible while the muscle returns to baseline. Two exercises for the same muscle still need full rest between them. → RST-01, RST-02, RST-03

Do supersets hurt performance?

Pairing unrelated or antagonist muscles costs little or no performance, only some cardio capacity, so superset all accessory and isolation work. Don't superset the opening strength work or two lifts for the same muscle. → RST-09, RST-10, RST-06

Are drop sets and rest-pause useful?

Rest-pause is his preferred technique: at failure, rest briefly and add reps that are the hardest of the set. Drop sets on every set are pump-chasing junk; use them only to reach target reps once rest-pause fails. Both go on top of a quality set, never in place of it. → INT-56, INT-57, INT-55

How long should a session be?

About 60-90 minutes is normal and 90 is pushing it. There is no fixed cap: train until the day's stimulus is done, then leave. → VOL-57, VOL-56

Progression and plateaus

How do evolving rep ranges work?

Give each lift a fixed rep range, start near the bottom and add reps each week. When the first set reaches the top of the range, add weight and stay in the same range. If the first set misses after a jump, return to the previous weight. → PRG-20, PRG-21, PRG-25

How can I progress besides adding weight?

Reps, sets, frequency, rest, variation and range of motion are all overload. But reps-only or sets-only progression stalls too, so bar weight must stay in the mix. → PRG-11, PRG-13, PRG-12

What should I do when a lift stalls?

First change rep ranges, widen the range, add some volume or frequency, not the exercise. Don't deload and re-run the same progression. If truly stuck, add a same-pattern variation as back-offs or on another day. → PRG-73, PRG-74, PRG-76

Should I swap a lift when it plateaus?

No. Swapping a stalled lift dodges the plateau, the "progress" on the new lift is neural relearning, and stalling is exactly when the body must build muscle. → PRG-75, EXS-20

Do I need to log every set?

Yes: weights and reps for every set of every exercise, curls included. Not counting reps is the easiest way to make no progress. → PRG-109

Do bodybuilders need periodization, mesocycles or training blocks?

No. The whole year is a hypertrophy block; variation lives inside the program through rotations and evolving ranges. Muscle never needs resensitising, and a good program runs indefinitely. → PRG-88, FAT-10, FRQ-78

Recovery, deloads and sleep

Do I need deloads?

Not scheduled ones. Needing a deload means you have been doing too much; trim the program yourself instead, which loses less tonnage. If deloads genuinely help you, he says keep them. → FAT-01, FAT-03, FAT-11

Do I need rest days for my CNS?

Most people can't reach real CNS burnout. Strength loss blamed on the CNS is usually a calorie deficit, poor sleep, stress or a bad day. → FAT-27, FAT-28

Is soreness a sign of growth?

No. Strength and tonnage over time are the signal. Soreness should fade with training age and frequency; constant soreness means poor adaptation or too little frequency. → SLP-42, SLP-43, FRQ-09

How much sleep do I need?

Most adults need 7-8 hours, and hypertrophy training raises the need. Cutting an hour to be productive backfires; between sleep and entertainment, always sleep. → SLP-02, SLP-03, SLP-04

Should I train when sick or short on sleep?

Slightly unwell or underslept: still train, but avoid heavy work. If kept up very late, sleep instead of training. → SLP-21, SLP-20

How do I come back after a long break?

Restart at about a third of your usual tonnage with short, low-volume sessions of favourite exercises, and ramp up stepwise; muscle returns fast, but jumping straight to old loads causes injuries. → FAT-57, BEG-89, INJ-60

Frequency and splits

Is training a muscle once a week enough?

For a natural it is always suboptimal unless you are deliberately coasting on that muscle. The fix for a bro split is to hit each muscle about twice a week. → FRQ-03, FRQ-37

Can I run push-pull-legs on 4-5 days?

PPL is a good split: run it about 6 times a week or 3 times a week, and for 4-5 days just cut a day. Order it pull-push-legs so pull day's hinges don't tire your legs before squats. → FRQ-41, FRQ-40

I'm very busy. What's the minimum?

Two or three full-body days, or upper/lower twice with isolation in short gaps. A physique built on 5 days a week can be maintained on 2. → FRQ-35

Do I need an arm day?

Only if big arms are a goal, and only once legs are trained at least twice a week with plenty of upper-back work. It adds to arm work on other days and should be low-stress. → FRQ-67, ARM-37, FRQ-66

Exercises and body parts

Do I need direct ab work?

Yes. Compounds and bracing don't build a six-pack; ab isolation is "non-negotiable". Diet only reveals abs. → ABS-01, ABS-02

Will oblique training make my waist wider?

No. Waist width is hip bone structure and love handles are fat; bigger obliques tighten the side and make love handles look smaller. → ABS-13, AES-44

Is the bench press necessary? Are dips better?

The bench is not mandatory: dips, push-ups and ring push-ups can replace it. Weighted dips are top tier for chest, triceps and shoulders, with slightly higher shoulder risk. → CHE-03, CHE-04

Overhead press or lateral raises for shoulders?

Both, with pressing first: vertical pressing is the bread and butter of delt size, and raises support it rather than replace it. → SHO-01, SHO-02

Do I need forearm isolation?

Yes. Heavy pulling doesn't build big forearms, and going strapless won't either; direct isolation does. → FOR-01, FOR-02

Should I use straps?

Yes, whenever grip limits a back or pulling set; letting grip limit the back is "criminal", and straps don't hurt forearm growth. Skip them on warm-ups and where grip isn't the limit. → EQP-01, EQP-02, EQP-04

What's the best pull-up substitute?

The lat pulldown, especially close-grip neutral, wide supinated or the diagonal pulldown taken heavy for 8-10 to failure. → BAK-14

Are machines and the Smith machine okay?

Yes, for stable, hard, joint-friendly sets and extra volume. But free weights should stay most of a natural's training. → EXS-51, EXS-50, EQP-61

How often should I train my neck?

One or two sessions a week, ideally supersetted with the first lower-body lift, already gives great results; more than 3-4 is pointless. He calls the sleep-apnea worry a myth. → NCK-05, NCK-06, NCK-01

Are small calves just genetics?

No. Calves stay small because they aren't trained, or are trained inconsistently with poor exercise choices. Insertions limit absolute size, not looking beefy. → CLF-01, GEN-50

Should I stretch?

Not statically before lifting. Lifting through full range builds mobility. The one stretch he kept is a hip-flexor stretch after leg days. → INJ-59, TEC-87, INJ-66

Injuries

How do I train around tendinitis?

Never push through joint or tendon pain. Find which movements load the painful tendon and switch to variations that work the muscle without pain. Rest doesn't cure it, because the cause is unchanged. → INJ-23, INJ-36, INJ-33

Are deadlifts dangerous for the back?

Done properly the deadlift is one of the safest lifts; deadlifting with bad form is the problem. Next-day low-back pain means a style you aren't built for or improper pulling. → INJ-68, INJ-69

Nutrition and bulking

How much protein do I need?

Far less than commonly sold. About 0.8 g/lb is near optimal but more than he needs; 2 g/kg, 2 g/lb or 200 g a day is wasted. → NUT-16, NUT-17, NUT-18

Should I bulk, cut or maintain?

Most men who aren't very over- or underweight should stay in a small permanent surplus. Fat lifters cut while lifting; skinny-fat lifters recomp at maintenance. → BLK-01, BLK-04, BLK-05

How fast should I gain weight?

Slowly: about 0.5-1.5 lb a month, and slower the more advanced you are. Past the beginner stage, more than about a pound a month is mostly fat. → BLK-19, BLK-20

How big should my surplus be?

Small. A few hundred calories is enough; a big surplus only builds fat. → BLK-12, BLK-13

Is weight loss just calories in, calories out?

Energy balance governs weight change, but food choice decides what kind of weight you gain or lose, and the source of calories matters. → NUT-08, NUT-09

Can I train fasted or eat one meal a day?

He never trains fasted; eat a carb-rich meal 2-3 hours before. Meal timing is "D tier" and OMAD isn't inherently bad for hypertrophy. → NUT-37, NUT-35

How long should a recomp last? Can I recomp forever?

Commit at least a year. When it stalls, don't cut deeper: run a very slow bulk, then recomp again. A recomp that only holds mass is wasted time. → BLK-57, BLK-63, BLK-64

I can't gain weight. What do I do?

"Can't gain" means not eating enough. Use scheduled meals, more of them, and drink calories through homemade shakes. → BLK-52, NUT-85, NUT-86

Which supplements are worth it?

Almost none matter for muscle. In 2024 he named whey, creatine, multivitamins and vitamin D as the only ones worth anything. Take creatine daily without loading or cycling. → SUP-01, SUP-09, SUP-12

Natural lifting

Doesn't testosterone crash after 30?

No. Natural men peak in their 30s-40s, and most muscle is built between your 20s and 50s. You lose muscle by stopping training and diet, not by turning 40. → NAT-34, SLP-49

Should I plan on TRT when I'm older?

He says no: men in their 50s-60s do fine without it, and any exogenous hormone ends natural status. → NAT-50, NAT-46

Can a natural reach 20 or 21-inch arms?

19-20-inch cold arms are possible naturally; 21 inches is doubtful. → NAT-39

Is there a natural limit?

Not a locatable one. Progress slows but continues as long as weight, volume and intensity keep rising; most people who claim a limit stopped finding the work worth it. → GEN-11, GEN-12

How long until I stop looking like I don't lift?

With average genetics it took him about 6 years to look trained and 10+ to look jacked; changes show in months and people notice in years. → JRN-06, AES-79, GEN-20

Beginners

How often should a novice train?

Three full-body days a week, about 48 hours apart. → BEG-11, FRQ-80

Is StrongLifts 5x5 a good beginner program?

It works only because anything works for novices. It is a powerlifting program that lacks isolation and pushes beginners into weights they shouldn't handle. → BEG-33, PRG-51

When should I write my own program?

You stop being a novice when you want to, and can, write your own. Start by modifying the novice program you run: copy its rep ranges and tonnage and stay minimalist. → BEG-07, BEG-63, MND-45

Can kids and teens lift?

Children can start conservatively around 10 (goblet squats, pull-ups, push-ups), heavy squats and deadlifts at 15-16. Teens should prioritise form, work capacity and enjoyment, with no ego lifting. → BEG-83, BEG-84

Does cardio kill gains?

No. Done right it helps through more volume and faster recovery; its real cost is calories. Never do it before lifting. → CAR-09, CAR-10, CAR-15
